facts.pair.description: Joins two short independent facts on one line of a change's page or in a tooltip, for example "Fix the header · by @maya · 3h ago". {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next fact. Only the separator between them is translated.

appBlocked.title.description: Title of the dialog shown when a person tries to open an app they blocked earlier. "Blocked" describes the app: this person chose not to see it.

appBlocked.message.text: You blocked this app. Unblock it in Settings → Blocked apps to open it again.
appBlocked.message.description: Body of the dialog shown when a person tries to open an app they blocked. "Settings → Blocked apps" is the path to a section of Settings; keep the arrow.

appBlocked.openSettings.description: Confirm button of the blocked-app dialog: goes to the Blocked apps section of Settings. "Open" is a verb.

preview.loader.rebuildingTitle.description: Heading on the loading screen of a change's preview (a running test copy of the app) when the preview had been paused and is being started again.

preview.loader.rebuildingSub.text: The preview was paused after a while of inactivity. Rebuilding it from the session’s latest changes. This usually takes 20–60 seconds.
preview.loader.rebuildingSub.description: Explanation under the heading on the loading screen of a change's preview while a paused preview is rebuilt. "Session" is the agent session in which the change is being built.

preview.loader.loadingTitle.description: Heading on the loading screen of a change's preview (a running test copy of the app) while it opens.

preview.loader.loadingSub.text: Automated checks are running against this preview, so the first load may be a little slower.
preview.loader.loadingSub.description: Explanation under the heading on the loading screen of a change's preview when the platform's automated checks are using the same preview.

launch.cover.opening.description: Small note under an app's icon and name on the cover shown while the app is being opened.

launch.cover.slow.text: This is taking longer than expected…
launch.cover.slow.description: Note that replaces "Opening…" on the cover shown while an app opens, once it has taken unusually long.

appStatus.sample.text: Preview sample app. You can try its discussion, favorites, reporting and blocking. No live app is deployed here.
appStatus.sample.description: Message shown in place of an app on a test build of Homeroom, for a made-up sample app that has no running version.

appStatus.spinningUp.description: Message shown in place of an app while its first deployment is still starting.

appStatus.awaitingSecrets.text: Awaiting required secrets. Deploy is blocked.
appStatus.awaitingSecrets.description: Message shown in place of an app that cannot be deployed until its required secrets (private configuration values such as API keys) are entered. The names of the missing secrets are listed under it.

appStatus.configureSecrets.description: Button under the message that an app is waiting for its secrets: opens the dialog where the secrets (private configuration values such as API keys) are entered.

appStatus.failed.description: Message shown in place of an app whose deployment failed. The reason, when known, is shown under it.

appStatus.viewBuildLog.description: Button under the message that an app failed to start: opens the log of the failed build. "Build" is a noun here.

appStatus.notAvailable.description: Message shown in place of an app that is not running and has no more specific state to report.

appStatus.checking.description: The only line shown in place of an app while Homeroom asks the server whether the project's first version is live yet.

appStatus.needsConnection.text: This app needs a connection. Reconnect to open it.
appStatus.needsConnection.description: Message shown in place of an app when the device is offline and the app has not been saved for offline use.

appStatus.unsafe.description: Message shown in place of an app whose address would not keep it separated from Homeroom, so Homeroom refuses to open it.

appStatus.unsafeDetail.text: Its address is not isolated from Homeroom.
appStatus.unsafeDetail.description: Smaller line under "This app cannot open safely." giving the reason. "Homeroom" is the product's name.

firstVersion.reviewPlan.description: Button on a new project's App tab while Homeroom bot waits for its maker to agree to the plan for the first version: opens the chat with Homeroom bot where the plan is.

firstVersion.openBot.description: Quiet link on a new project's App tab while its first version is being built: opens this person's chat with Homeroom bot. "Open" is a verb; "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant.

firstVersion.opensWhenReady.text: It opens here when it’s ready.
firstVersion.opensWhenReady.description: Line under a new project's card on its App tab while the first version is being built, for everyone but the person who started the project. "It" is the app.

firstVersion.notifyWhenLive.text: We’ll notify you when it’s live
firstVersion.notifyWhenLive.description: Line beside a small check under a new project's card on its App tab while its first version is being made, for the person who started the project and for its other members: a promise that Homeroom will send them a notification once the app is live. "It" is the app; "live" means published and running for everyone.

firstVersion.tryAgain.description: Button under a new project's card on its App tab, for the person who started the project, when Homeroom bot's build of its first version stopped before the app went live: opens the build's conversation in their chat with Homeroom bot, where they can start it again.

firstVersion.tryFromChat.description: Line on a new project's App tab, for its maker, when the first version is built and can be tried from their chat with Homeroom bot. "It" is the first version of the app.

firstVersion.waitingForApproval.description: Line on a new project's App tab, for someone who is not its maker, when the first version is built and has not been approved yet.

firstVersion.openMyBotChat.text: Open my chat with Homeroom bot
firstVersion.openMyBotChat.description: Button on a new project's App tab, for its maker, when the first version is ready to try: opens their own chat with Homeroom bot. "Open" is a verb; "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant.

firstVersion.tryIt.description: Button on a new project's App tab when its first version is waiting for approval: opens a preview of that version so the person can use it.

firstVersion.seeChange.description: Button on a new project's App tab when its first version is waiting for approval: opens the page of the change that holds the first version, where people vote. "Change" is a noun.

firstVersion.waitingForYourApproval.description: Line on a new project's App tab when the first version cannot go live until the person reading approves it.

firstVersion.noVote.soon.text: No vote needed. It goes live in a minute or two.
firstVersion.noVote.soon.description: Line on a new project's App tab when its first version is ready: a project's first version goes live without a vote once it passes its checks, and it has, so it is about to be released. "It" is the first version of the app.

firstVersion.noVote.onceTested.text: No vote needed. It goes live once it passes its checks.
firstVersion.noVote.onceTested.description: Line on a new project's App tab when its first version is ready to try: a project's first version goes live without a vote, and it is released as soon as its automated checks pass. "It" is the first version of the app.

firstVersion.wait.soon.text: It goes live in a minute or two.
firstVersion.wait.soon.description: Line on a new project's App tab when its first version has been approved and is about to be released. "It" is the first version of the app.

firstVersion.wait.liveToday.text: It goes live later today if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.liveToday.description: Line on a new project's App tab when nothing more is needed for its first version except time: it is released automatically unless somebody votes against it. "It" is the first version of the app. Used when the release is later the same day.

firstVersion.wait.liveTomorrow.text: It goes live tomorrow if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.liveTomorrow.description: Line on a new project's App tab when nothing more is needed for its first version except time: it is released automatically unless somebody votes against it. "It" is the first version of the app. Used when the release is the next day.

firstVersion.wait.liveWeekday.text: It goes live on {{weekday}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.liveWeekday.description: Line on a new project's App tab when nothing more is needed for its first version except time: it is released automatically unless somebody votes against it. "It" is the first version of the app. {{weekday}} is the name of a day within the coming week, already in the reader's language, for example Wednesday.

firstVersion.wait.liveDate.text: It goes live on {{date}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.liveDate.description: Line on a new project's App tab when nothing more is needed for its first version except time: it is released automatically unless somebody votes against it. "It" is the first version of the app. {{date}} is a month and day already in the reader's language, for example October 12.

firstVersion.wait.forApproval.description: Line on a new project's App tab, for someone whose own approval is not asked for, while the first version still needs other people's approval.

firstVersion.wait.people.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", naming the people whose approval the first version still needs. {{people}} is a list of @usernames already joined, for example "@sam and @ada" or "@sam, @ada and 2 more".

firstVersion.wait.peopleOrToday.text: Waiting for {{people}}, or it goes live later today if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.peopleOrToday.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", naming the people whose approval the first version still needs. {{people}} is a list of @usernames already joined, for example "@sam and @ada" or "@sam, @ada and 2 more". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it.

firstVersion.wait.peopleOrTomorrow.text: Waiting for {{people}}, or it goes live tomorrow if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.peopleOrTomorrow.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", naming the people whose approval the first version still needs. {{people}} is a list of @usernames already joined, for example "@sam and @ada" or "@sam, @ada and 2 more". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it.

firstVersion.wait.peopleOrWeekday.text: Waiting for {{people}}, or it goes live on {{weekday}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.peopleOrWeekday.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", naming the people whose approval the first version still needs. {{people}} is a list of @usernames already joined, for example "@sam and @ada" or "@sam, @ada and 2 more". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{weekday}} is the name of a day within the coming week, for example Wednesday.

firstVersion.wait.peopleOrDate.text: Waiting for {{people}}, or it goes live on {{date}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.peopleOrDate.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", naming the people whose approval the first version still needs. {{people}} is a list of @usernames already joined, for example "@sam and @ada" or "@sam, @ada and 2 more". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{date}} is a month and day, for example October 12.

firstVersion.wait.more_one.text: Waiting for one more person to approve.
firstVersion.wait.more_one.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

firstVersion.wait.more_other.text: Waiting for {{count}} more people to approve.
firstVersion.wait.more_other.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one".

firstVersion.wait.moreOrToday_one.text: Waiting for one more person to approve, or it goes live later today if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrToday_one.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrToday_other.text: Waiting for {{count}} more people to approve, or it goes live later today if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrToday_other.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrTomorrow_one.text: Waiting for one more person to approve, or it goes live tomorrow if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrTomorrow_one.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrTomorrow_other.text: Waiting for {{count}} more people to approve, or it goes live tomorrow if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrTomorrow_other.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrWeekday_one.text: Waiting for one more person to approve, or it goes live on {{weekday}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrWeekday_one.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{weekday}} is the name of a day within the coming week, for example Wednesday. {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrWeekday_other.text: Waiting for {{count}} more people to approve, or it goes live on {{weekday}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrWeekday_other.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{weekday}} is the name of a day within the coming week, for example Wednesday.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrDate_one.text: Waiting for one more person to approve, or it goes live on {{date}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrDate_one.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{date}} is a month and day, for example October 12. {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrDate_other.text: Waiting for {{count}} more people to approve, or it goes live on {{date}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrDate_other.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{date}} is a month and day, for example October 12.

firstVersion.wait.approved.description: Line on a new project's App tab for someone who has approved the first version, when there is nothing else to say. "It" is the first version of the app.

firstVersion.wait.approvedThen.description: Line on a new project's App tab for someone who has approved the first version. {{next}} is one more complete sentence saying what it still waits for, for example "It goes live tomorrow if nobody objects."; keep it after the first sentence.

firstVersion.people.lastTwo.description: Ends a list of @usernames whose approval a first version is waiting for, as in "@sam, @ada and @kim". {{first}} is the name or comma-joined names before the last one, and {{last}} the last name. The result is placed in "Waiting for …".

firstVersion.people.andMore_one.description: A list of @usernames whose approval a first version is waiting for, followed by how many further people are not named, as in "@sam, @ada and 2 more". {{people}} is the comma-joined names and {{count}} the number of unnamed people. The result is placed in "Waiting for …".

firstVersion.people.andMore_other.description: A list of @usernames whose approval a first version is waiting for, followed by how many further people are not named, as in "@sam, @ada and 2 more". {{people}} is the comma-joined names and {{count}} the number of unnamed people. The result is placed in "Waiting for …".

versionPill.redeploying.description: Tooltip on the small version pill of an app while a new version is being deployed. Nothing more is known.

versionPill.redeployingFrom.description: Tooltip on the small version pill of an app while a new version is being deployed. {{sha}} is the short code of the version being replaced, for example 3f9a2c1.

versionPill.redeployingElapsed_one.description: Tooltip on the small version pill of an app while a new version is being deployed. {{count}} is how many seconds it has taken so far; "s" abbreviates seconds.

versionPill.redeployingElapsed_other.description: Tooltip on the small version pill of an app while a new version is being deployed. {{count}} is how many seconds it has taken so far; "s" abbreviates seconds.

versionPill.redeployingFromElapsed_one.description: Tooltip on the small version pill of an app while a new version is being deployed. {{sha}} is the short code of the version being replaced, for example 3f9a2c1, and {{count}} how many seconds it has taken so far; "s" abbreviates seconds.

versionPill.redeployingFromElapsed_other.description: Tooltip on the small version pill of an app while a new version is being deployed. {{sha}} is the short code of the version being replaced, for example 3f9a2c1, and {{count}} how many seconds it has taken so far; "s" abbreviates seconds.

versionPill.deploying.description: Lower-case label inside the small version pill of an app, beside a spinner, while a new version is being deployed. It stands where the version code normally is.

versionPill.dev.description: Lower-case label inside the small version pill of an app that has no deployed version on record. Short for "development"; it stands where the version code normally is.

versionPill.noVersion.description: Tooltip on the version pill of an app that has no deployed version on record.

versionPill.mergedBy.description: One whole fact in the tooltip of an app's version pill: who merged the change that produced this version. The tooltip lists independent facts separated by middle dots (the change's title, this, how long ago), so it is not part of a sentence and starts in lower case. {{username}} is that person's username; keep the @ before it.

versionPill.commit.description: Tooltip on an app's version pill when nothing is known about the version except its commit. "Commit" is a noun, the saved revision of the code; {{sha}} is its short code, for example 3f9a2c1.

header.appFallback.description: Title in the header bar over a project's old discussion channel when the project's name is not known. A noun.

header.channel.description: Subtitle in the header bar, under the project's name, when its old discussion channel is open. A noun: a chat room.

header.communities.description: Title in the header bar while a project's page is open: the name of the Communities section of Homeroom, which the page belongs to.

discussion.openFailed.description: Brief notice shown when the link to the discussion of a proposal (here a proposed change to a project's settings or rules) could not be followed; the person is taken to the project's board instead.

discussion.readOnlyNotice.text: You're viewing this app's dev space read-only. Only collaborators can post.
discussion.readOnlyNotice.description: Notice in place of the message box of a project's discussion, and of the replies on a change's page, for a person who may read and may not write. "Dev space" is the project's build area; "post" is a verb, to send a message.

discussion.archivedNotice.text: This was Homeroom’s project discussion. It is read-only now: Homeroom’s channel is #general.
discussion.archivedNotice.description: Notice above the old discussion channel of the Homeroom project itself, which can still be read and no longer written in. "Homeroom" is the product's name and "#general" the name of a channel; keep both.

discussion.door.empty.text: Talk with everyone building this app
discussion.door.empty.description: Line under the door to a project's discussion on its page, shown when there is no latest message to preview.

discussion.door.said.description: Preview of the latest message under the door to a project's discussion. {{author}} is the username of the person who wrote it, or the word for the system, and {{message}} the start of what they wrote.

discussion.door.system.description: Stands in for the author's name in the preview of a project's latest discussion message when the message was written by the platform and not by a person. A noun.

discussion.card.empty.text: Talk with everyone building this app
discussion.card.empty.description: Line on the General discussion card at the top of a project's board, shown when there is no latest message to preview.

discussion.card.said.description: Preview of the latest message on the General discussion card of a project's board. {{author}} is the username of the person who wrote it and {{message}} the start of what they wrote.

discussion.card.tooltip.description: Tooltip on the General discussion card of a project's board. "Open" is a verb.

discussion.card.titleFor.description: Title of the card at the top of a project's board that leads to its discussion. {{app}} is the project's name.

discussion.card.title.description: Title of the card at the top of a project's board that leads to its discussion, when the project's name is not known.

card.meta.visibleToGroup.description: Status at the end of the small line on the card of a change that is still being built, when its owner has shared it with the project's members.

card.meta.notShared.description: Status at the end of the small line on the card of a change that is still being built, when only its owner can see it.

card.actions.continueBuilding.description: Button on the card of a person's own proposal: opens the agent session where the change is built so they can keep working on it. "Building" is a verb.

card.actions.continueBuildingTitle.text: Open the agent session behind this change
card.actions.continueBuildingTitle.description: Tooltip on the Continue building button of a proposal's card. "Open" is a verb; "change" is a noun.

card.actions.explore.description: Button on a proposal's card: starts a chat with an AI coding agent, with a message about this proposal already written, so the person can ask what it does.

card.actions.exploreButton.description: Label, after a sparkle icon, of the button on a proposal in the vote list: starts a chat with an AI coding agent, with a message about this proposal already written.

card.actions.moveBack.description: Button on the card of a person's own proposal that is up for a vote: takes it out of the vote so they can keep working. "Underway" is the name of the board's column for work in progress.

card.actions.moveBackTitle.text: Take this proposal out of review to keep working on it (clears its votes, keeps the PR open)
card.actions.moveBackTitle.description: Tooltip on the Move back to Underway button. A proposal is a change put up for a vote; "PR" is the pull request on GitHub.

card.actions.withdraw.description: Button on the card of a person's own proposal that is up for a vote: takes the proposal back for good. A verb.

card.actions.withdrawTitle.text: Withdraw this proposal (closes the PR, removes it from the vote panel)
card.actions.withdrawTitle.description: Tooltip on the Withdraw button of a proposal's card. "PR" is the pull request on GitHub.

card.actions.askForApproval.description: Button on the card of a change imported from GitHub that its owner has not put up for a vote yet: puts it up for the group's vote.

card.actions.askForApprovalTitle.text: Ask the group to approve this imported change
card.actions.askForApprovalTitle.description: Tooltip on the Ask for approval button of an imported change. "The group" is the project's members; "change" is a noun.

card.reasons.attention.description: Heading over the list of problems on the card of an imported change that is not up for a vote yet.

card.reasons.cantMerge.description: Heading over the list of problems on a proposal's card when at least one of them stops the change from being merged into the project.

card.reasons.worthKnowing.description: Heading over the list of notes on a proposal's card when none of them stops the change from being merged.

card.menu.retractKudos.description: Row in a card's ⋯ menu: takes back the kudos (a thank-you point) this person gave for the change. "Retract" is a verb.

card.menu.giveKudos.description: Row in a card's ⋯ menu: gives kudos (a thank-you point) to the author of the change.

card.menu.openCard.description: First row in a card's ⋯ menu on the board: opens the card on a page of its own. "Open" is a verb.

card.menu.openCardTitle.text: The card on its own page
card.menu.openCardTitle.description: Tooltip on the Open card row of a card's ⋯ menu.

card.proposal.fallbackTitle.description: Title shown on a proposal's card when the change has no title of its own. {{username}} is the account name of the person who made the change. "Change" is a noun here: a set of edits to the project.

card.proposal.revertLead.description: Coloured label at the start of the title of a proposal that undoes an earlier change. The title of the change being undone follows it in its own element. Keep the arrow.

card.proposal.revertedPr.description: Stands in for the title of the change being undone, after "↩ Revert of" on a proposal's card, when that change has no title. {{number}} is its pull request number. "PR" abbreviates pull request.

card.proposal.openTitle.description: Tooltip of a proposal's card on the Workshop board: pressing the card opens the proposal's page with its discussion. "Open" is a verb.

card.proposal.mineIconTitle.text: This is your PR. Its session is under ⋯.
card.proposal.mineIconTitle.description: Tooltip of the icon on a proposal's card that the viewer made. "PR" abbreviates pull request; "session" is the agent session that built it; ⋯ is the card's menu button and stays as it is.

card.provenance.importedBy.description: Fact on a proposal card's line of details, saying the change came from a GitHub pull request. {{author}} is the GitHub name of its author. Lower case: it sits among other facts separated by dots.

card.provenance.imported.description: Fact on a proposal card's line of details, saying the change came from a GitHub pull request whose author is not known. Lower case: it sits among other facts separated by dots.

card.provenance.builtWith.description: Fact on a proposal card's line of details. {{agent}} is the name of the coding agent that made the change, for example Claude Code. Lower case: it sits among other facts separated by dots.

card.provenance.maintenance.description: Fact on a proposal card's line of details, marking a change Homeroom itself opened to keep the project up to date. Lower case: it sits among other facts separated by dots.

card.provenance.autoTitle.description: Fact on a proposal card's line of details: the title shown is a placeholder and an automatically written one is on its way. Lower case: it sits among other facts separated by dots.

card.waiting.yourApproval.description: Status of a proposal on a project that is just the viewer, where their own Yes is the only approval needed.

card.waiting.approval.description: Status of a proposal that has been put up for the group's vote and is not approved yet.

card.waiting.noVote.description: Status of a proposal that is a project's first version: it is not put to a vote, and goes live once its automated checks pass.

board.plusMenu.settingsTitle.description: Title of the sheet, on a phone, listing a project's settings and rules, opened from the board's + menu.

board.filterChip.search.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that the cards are filtered by a search. {{query}} is what the person typed. Pressing the chip removes the filter.

board.filterChip.stageOpen.description: Chip above All items showing that only the work still open (requests, work underway and changes up for a vote) is shown, set by tapping the open items figure on the Workshop. Pressing the chip removes the filter.

board.filterChip.stageUnclaimed.description: Chip above All items showing that only the open requests nobody has picked up yet are shown, set by tapping that figure on the Workshop. Pressing the chip removes the filter.

board.filterChip.stageShipped.description: Chip above All items showing that only the changes that went live this week are shown, set by tapping that figure on the Workshop. Pressing the chip removes the filter.

board.filterChip.priorityLow.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only cards the group marked as low priority are shown. Pressing it removes the filter.

board.filterChip.priorityMedium.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only cards the group marked as medium priority are shown. Pressing it removes the filter.

board.filterChip.priorityHigh.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only cards the group marked as high priority are shown. Pressing it removes the filter.

board.filterChip.nobodyYet.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only cards with no person assigned to them are shown. It answers "who is on this?".

board.filterChip.needsVote.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only the proposals the viewer has not voted on yet are shown.

board.filterChip.assignedToYou.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only the cards assigned to the viewer are shown.

board.filterChip.yours.description: Chip above the Workshop board (All items) showing that only the person's own work as the Homeroom bot tab reads it: everything they filed, built, claimed, voted on, wrote in or chose Notify me on. It is dismissable.

board.filterChip.category.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only the cards in one category are shown. {{category}} is that category's name.

board.column.emptyFiltered.description: Shown inside a column of the Workshop board when filters or a search are on and no card in that column matches.

board.column.empty.description: Shown inside a column of the Workshop board that has no cards at all.

board.column.requests.description: Title of the first column of the Workshop board: requests people have filed that nobody has started on. A plural noun.

board.column.underway.description: Title of the second column of the Workshop board: requests and changes somebody is working on now.

board.column.underwayHint.text: A person or an agent is on each of these. The chip on each card says how.
board.column.underwayHint.description: Explanation shown with the "Underway" column of the Workshop board: each card there is being handled by a person or an AI agent. The "chip" is the small status label on each card (worked on, auto-solving, paused, waiting on an answer, claimed). Keep it short.

board.column.review.description: Title of the third column of the Workshop board: changes that have been put up for a vote and are not approved yet.

board.column.done.description: Title of the last column of the Workshop board: changes that were merged and requests that were closed.

board.deploy.childFailed.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when putting the newest merged change into production failed.

board.deploy.childFailedTitle.text: The latest merged change has not been confirmed in production.
board.deploy.childFailedTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Latest merged change · deploy failed" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column. "Production" is the live, running project.

board.deploy.childPending.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when the newest merged change is not running in production yet.

board.deploy.childPendingTitle.text: Production is still serving an earlier revision.
board.deploy.childPendingTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Latest merged change · awaiting deployment" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column. A "revision" is one version of the project's code.

board.deploy.childLive.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when the newest merged change is running and no pull request number is known for it. {{sha}} is the short code that identifies the running version, for example 3fa9c21.

board.deploy.childLiveTitle.text: The latest merged change is included in the observed production revision.
board.deploy.childLiveTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Live in production …" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column when the newest merged change is running.

board.deploy.stalled_one.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when merged changes are not live and the release has stopped making progress. {{count}} is how many merged changes are waiting.

board.deploy.stalled_other.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when merged changes are not live and the release has stopped making progress. {{count}} is how many merged changes are waiting.

board.deploy.stalledTitle.text: Production is still running an earlier revision. The release watcher has detected a stalled deployment.
board.deploy.stalledTitle.description: Tooltip of the "deployment stalled" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column. The "release watcher" is the automatic process that monitors releases.

board.deploy.waiting_one.text: {{count}} merged change waiting to go live
board.deploy.waiting_one.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when merged changes are not running in production yet. {{count}} is how many.

board.deploy.waiting_other.text: {{count}} merged changes waiting to go live
board.deploy.waiting_other.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when merged changes are not running in production yet. {{count}} is how many.

board.deploy.waitingTitle.text: Production is still running an earlier revision.
board.deploy.waitingTitle.description: Tooltip of the "merged changes waiting to go live" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column.

board.deploy.liveThroughPrSha.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column: every merged change up to and including this pull request is running. {{number}} is the pull request's number and {{sha}} the short code of the running version.

board.deploy.liveThroughPr.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column: every merged change up to and including this pull request is running. {{number}} is the pull request's number.

board.deploy.liveThroughSha.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column: every merged change up to this version is running. {{sha}} is the short code of the running version.

board.deploy.liveThroughLatest.text: Live in production through the latest merged change
board.deploy.liveThroughLatest.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when every merged change is running and no version code is known.

board.deploy.liveThroughTitle.text: Every merged change through this point is live in production.
board.deploy.liveThroughTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Live in production through …" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column.

board.deploy.unmatched.text: Production deployment could not be matched to completed history
board.deploy.unmatched.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when the running version does not correspond to any merged change on record.

board.deploy.unmatchedTitle.text: Production is running {{sha}}, but no completed proposal records that merge commit.
board.deploy.unmatchedTitle.description: Tooltip of the "could not be matched" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column. {{sha}} is the short code of the running version.

board.divider.private.description: Label of a divider in the Workshop board's "Underway" column, above the viewer's own agent sessions that nobody else can see.

board.divider.privateTitle.text: Only you can see your active sessions here. Their code is public.
board.divider.privateTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Yours · not shared" divider in the Workshop board's "Underway" column.

board.divider.visible.description: Label of a divider in the Workshop board's "Underway" column, above the viewer's own agent sessions that everyone can see.

board.divider.visibleTitle.text: Visible to everyone, including a live preview of your changes.
board.divider.visibleTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Yours · visible" divider in the Workshop board's "Underway" column.

board.divider.others.description: Label of a divider in the Workshop board's "Underway" column, above agent sessions that belong to other people.

board.divider.othersTitle.text: Agent sessions other people have made visible.
board.divider.othersTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Others" divider in the Workshop board's "Underway" column.

board.sessionNote.priority_one.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session card below is not filtered by priority.
board.sessionNote.priority_one.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by priority and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.priority_other.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session cards below are not filtered by priority.
board.sessionNote.priority_other.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by priority and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.category_one.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session card below is not filtered by category.
board.sessionNote.category_one.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by category and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.category_other.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session cards below are not filtered by category.
board.sessionNote.category_other.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by category and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.assignee_one.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session card below is not filtered by assignee.
board.sessionNote.assignee_one.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by assignee and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.assignee_other.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session cards below are not filtered by assignee.
board.sessionNote.assignee_other.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by assignee and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.priorityCategory_one.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session card below is not filtered by priority or category.
board.sessionNote.priorityCategory_one.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by priority or category and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.priorityCategory_other.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session cards below are not filtered by priority or category.
board.sessionNote.priorityCategory_other.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by priority or category and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.priorityAssignee_one.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session card below is not filtered by priority or assignee.
board.sessionNote.priorityAssignee_one.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by priority or assignee and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.priorityAssignee_other.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session cards below are not filtered by priority or assignee.
board.sessionNote.priorityAssignee_other.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by priority or assignee and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.categoryAssignee_one.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session card below is not filtered by category or assignee.
board.sessionNote.categoryAssignee_one.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by category or assignee and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.categoryAssignee_other.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session cards below are not filtered by category or assignee.
board.sessionNote.categoryAssignee_other.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by category or assignee and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.all_one.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session card below is not filtered by priority, category or assignee.
board.sessionNote.all_one.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by priority, category or assignee and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

board.sessionNote.all_other.text: Agent sessions don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} session cards below are not filtered by priority, category or assignee.
board.sessionNote.all_other.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by priority, category or assignee and agent session cards are shown anyway, because sessions have none of those. {{count}} is how many session cards are below.

request.fallbackTitle.description: Stands in for the title of a request (a filed issue) linked to a change when the title is not known. {{number}} is the issue's number.

request.ref.closedBy.description: Small heading on a request's page (a request is a filed issue) over the link to the change that deals with it. Used when that change was merged and the request is closed; the change's reference follows.

request.ref.addressedBy.description: Small heading on a request's page (a request is a filed issue) over the link to the change that deals with it. Used when that change was merged and the request is still open; the change's reference follows.

request.ref.waiting.description: Small heading on a request's page (a request is a filed issue) over the link to the change that deals with it. Used when that change is up for a vote.

request.ref.underway.description: Small heading on a request's page (a request is a filed issue) over the link to the change that deals with it. Used when that change is still being built.

request.ref.changeLabel.description: Short label on the link from a request's page to the change that deals with it, used when the change has no pull request number to show. A noun.

request.ref.pullRequestTitle.description: Stands in for the title of the change linked from a request's page when the change has no title. {{number}} is its pull request number on GitHub.

request.ref.changeTitle.description: Stands in for the title of the change linked from a request's page when it has neither a title nor a pull request number. "Change" is a noun; {{id}} is the change's number in Homeroom.

request.actions.stopWorking.description: Button on a request's page for the person who said they would work on it: withdraws that claim.

request.actions.stopWorkingTitle.text: Stop working on this so somebody else can pick it up
request.actions.stopWorkingTitle.description: Tooltip on the Stop working on this button of a request.

request.actions.claim.description: Button on a request's page: tells everyone that this person will work on the request. "It" is the request.

request.actions.claimTitle.text: Let everyone know you'll work on this. It's not a promise of progress
request.actions.claimTitle.description: Tooltip on the Claim it button of a request. It ends without a full stop.

request.actions.bountied.description: Label of the disabled kudos button on a request when this person has already pledged kudos for it. Keep the star at the start.

request.actions.pledgeKudos.description: Button on a request's page: promises kudos (thank-you points) to whoever builds the change that fulfils the request. "Pledge" is a verb.

request.actions.pledgeKudosTitle.text: Pledge kudos to whoever's change makes this happen
request.actions.pledgeKudosTitle.description: Tooltip on the Pledge kudos button of a request.

request.actions.closeProposed.description: Label of the disabled button on a request when a vote to close the request is already open. "Close" is a noun here: the closing of the request has been proposed.

request.actions.closeProposedTitle.text: Closing this request is waiting for approval
request.actions.closeProposedTitle.description: Tooltip on the disabled Close proposed button of a request.

request.actions.proposeReopen.description: Button on a closed request's page: asks the group to vote on reopening the request. "Reopening" is a verb, to make the request open again.

request.actions.proposeReopenTitle.text: Ask the group to reopen this request. If they approve, it's open again
request.actions.proposeReopenTitle.description: Tooltip on the Propose reopening button of a closed request. It ends without a full stop.

request.actions.reopenProposed.description: Label of the disabled button on a closed request when a vote to reopen it is already open. "Reopen" is a noun here: the reopening has been proposed.

request.actions.reopenProposedTitle.text: Reopening this request is waiting for approval
request.actions.reopenProposedTitle.description: Tooltip on the disabled Reopen proposed button of a closed request.

request.actions.proposeClose.description: Button on a request's page: asks the group to vote on closing the request. "Close" is a verb, to mark the request as finished.

request.actions.proposeCloseTitle.text: Ask the group to close this request. If they approve, it's closed
request.actions.proposeCloseTitle.description: Tooltip on the Propose to close button of a request. It ends without a full stop.

request.comments.unknownAuthor.description: Shown in place of the author's name on a comment on a request's page when the comment has no known author. Lower case, as a name would sit there.

request.closedBand.whenByVote.description: The whole text of the band at the top of a closed request's page (a request is a filed issue), when the group voted to close it. "Closed" is an adjective describing the request. {{date}} is a short date or relative time, for example Oct 5 or 3d ago. <0></0> is the status word, drawn bold; <1></1> and <3></3> are separator dots hidden from screen readers; <2></2> holds the date and <4></4> the words saying how it was closed. Keep every tag, in the order your language reads.

request.closedBand.whenByAdmin.description: The whole text of the band at the top of a closed request's page (a request is a filed issue), when an administrator closed it. "Closed" is an adjective describing the request. {{date}} is a short date or relative time, for example Oct 5 or 3d ago. <0></0> is the status word, drawn bold; <1></1> and <3></3> are separator dots hidden from screen readers; <2></2> holds the date and <4></4> the words saying how it was closed. Keep every tag, in the order your language reads.

request.closedBand.byVote.description: The whole text of the band at the top of a closed request's page (a request is a filed issue), when the group voted to close it and the date is not known. "Closed" is an adjective describing the request. <0></0> is the status word, drawn bold; <1></1> is a separator dot hidden from screen readers; <2></2> holds the words saying how it was closed. Keep every tag, in the order your language reads.

request.closedBand.byAdmin.description: The whole text of the band at the top of a closed request's page (a request is a filed issue), when an administrator closed it and the date is not known. "Closed" is an adjective describing the request. <0></0> is the status word, drawn bold; <1></1> is a separator dot hidden from screen readers; <2></2> holds the words saying how it was closed. Keep every tag, in the order your language reads.

page.about.request.description: Heading over the description on a request's page (a request is a filed issue).

page.about.change.description: Heading over the description on a change's page (a change is work on the project that is being built, voted on or already live). "Change" is a noun.

page.about.proposal.description: Heading over the description on the page of a proposal to change a project's settings or rules.

page.about.generic.description: Heading over the description on a board item's page when the kind of item is not known.

page.hero.kind.description: Small upper-case word at the top of a change's page saying what kind of page it is. A noun. A status may follow it after a middle dot.

page.hero.status.visibleToGroup.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The change is still being built and its owner has shared it with the project's members.

page.hero.status.notShared.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The change is still being built and only its owner can see it.

page.hero.status.merging.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The change was approved and is being merged into the project.

page.hero.status.goingLive.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The change was merged and the new version of the app is being deployed.

page.hero.status.notLiveYet.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The change was merged and the deployment of the new version failed or is stuck.

page.hero.status.live.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The change was merged and is part of the running app. An adjective.

page.hero.status.closed.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The change was withdrawn or rejected. An adjective describing the change.

page.hero.status.goingLiveIncludedIn.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The new version is being deployed. It was not merged on its own: its work went in as part of another change. {{number}} is that change's pull request number.

page.hero.status.goingLiveIncludedInAnot.text: Going live, included in another change
page.hero.status.goingLiveIncludedInAnot.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The new version is being deployed. It was not merged on its own: its work went in as part of another change.

page.hero.status.notLiveYetIncludedIn.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The deployment failed or is stuck. It was not merged on its own: its work went in as part of another change. {{number}} is that change's pull request number.

page.hero.status.notLiveYetIncludedInAno.text: Not live yet, included in another change
page.hero.status.notLiveYetIncludedInAno.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The deployment failed or is stuck. It was not merged on its own: its work went in as part of another change.

page.hero.status.liveIncludedIn.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The change is part of the running app. It was not merged on its own: its work went in as part of another change. {{number}} is that change's pull request number.

page.hero.status.liveIncludedInAnother.description: Status beside the word "Change" at the top of a change's page. The change is part of the running app. It was not merged on its own: its work went in as part of another change.

page.hero.authorBot.description: Author shown in the by-line under a change's title when the platform's assistant built the change. "Homeroom bot" is the assistant's name.

page.hero.verb.started.description: Lower-case verb in the by-line under a change's title, between the author's name and how long ago, as in "maya · {verb} 5h ago". Past tense. The author began the change and is still building it.

page.hero.verb.imported.description: Lower-case verb in the by-line under a change's title, between the author's name and how long ago, as in "maya · {verb} 5h ago". Past tense. The change was brought in from a pull request on GitHub.

page.hero.verb.made.description: Lower-case verb in the by-line under a change's title, between the author's name and how long ago, as in "maya · {verb} 5h ago". Past tense. Homeroom bot built the change.

page.hero.verb.proposed.description: Lower-case verb in the by-line under a change's title, between the author's name and how long ago, as in "maya · {verb} 5h ago". Past tense. The author put the change up for a vote.

page.hero.provenance.importedBy.description: One fact at the end of the by-line under a change's title, after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. The change came from a pull request on GitHub; {{author}} is its author's GitHub username.

page.hero.provenance.imported.description: One fact at the end of the by-line under a change's title, after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. The change came from a pull request on GitHub whose author is not known.

page.hero.provenance.builtWith.description: One fact at the end of the by-line under a change's title, after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. {{agent}} is the name of the coding agent the change was made with, for example Claude Code.

page.hero.provenance.maintenance.description: One fact at the end of the by-line under a change's title, after a middle dot, so it starts in lower case. The change was made by Homeroom itself to keep the project working, not by a member.

page.includedIn.heading.description: Small heading on the page of a merged change whose work was released inside another change; a link to that other change follows.

page.includedIn.changeLabel.description: Short label on the link to the change that this change went live as part of, used when that change has no pull request number to show. A noun.

page.includedIn.pullRequestTitle.description: Stands in for the title of the change that this change went live as part of, when it has no title. {{number}} is its pull request number on GitHub.

page.includedIn.changeTitle.description: Stands in for the title of the change that this change went live as part of, when it has neither a title nor a pull request number. "Change" is a noun; {{id}} is its number in Homeroom.

page.menu.askForChanges.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of the page of a proposal that Homeroom bot built: opens this person's chat with Homeroom bot to ask it to alter the proposal. "Changes" is a noun: alterations.

page.menu.askForChangesTitle.text: Ask Homeroom bot to change this, in your chat with it
page.menu.askForChangesTitle.description: Tooltip on the Ask for changes row in the ⋯ menu of a proposal's page. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant; "change" is a verb.

page.menu.buildOwnerTitle.text: Open the agent session behind this change
page.menu.buildOwnerTitle.description: Tooltip on the row, in the ⋯ menu of a person's own change, that opens the agent session where the change is built. "Open" is a verb; "change" is a noun.

page.menu.buildReadTitle.text: Read the agent session that built this change
page.menu.buildReadTitle.description: Tooltip on the row, in the ⋯ menu of somebody else's change, that opens the published record of the agent session that built it.

page.actions.openApp.description: Button on the page of a change that is live: opens the running app. "Open" is a verb.

page.actions.syncWithMain.description: Button on a person's own change: brings the change up to date with "main", the project's current code. "Sync" is a verb; "main" is the name of the code branch and stays in English.

page.actions.syncing.description: Label of the Sync with main button on a change's page while the sync is running.

page.actions.retryPreview.description: Button on the Testing card of a change's page when its preview (a running test copy of the app) failed to start: tries to start it again. "Retry" is a verb.

page.actions.submitForReview.description: Main button on a person's own change that is still being built: puts the change up for the group's vote.

page.actions.submitting.description: Label of the Submit for review button on a change's page while the change is being submitted.

page.actions.notReady.text: This change cannot be submitted yet. Try again in a moment.
page.actions.notReady.description: Brief notice shown when a change could not be put up for a vote because the platform was not ready for it. "Change" is a noun.

page.actions.failed.text: The action could not be completed.
page.actions.failed.description: Brief notice shown when syncing a change or submitting it for review failed and the server gave no reason.

page.actions.synced.description: Brief notice shown after a change was brought up to date with "main", the project's current code. "main" is the name of the code branch and stays in English.

page.actions.networkError.description: Brief notice shown when syncing a change or submitting it for review failed because the server could not be reached.

page.menu.details.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a change's page: opens the technical details of the change.

page.menu.detailsTitle.text: The pull request, its steps and checks, and its description
page.menu.detailsTitle.description: Tooltip on the Details row in the ⋯ menu of a change's page, listing what the details hold.

page.menu.editDescription.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a person's own change: lets them rewrite the change's description.

page.menu.openOnGitHub.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's page, for a request that is an issue on GitHub: opens the issue on GitHub in a new tab. "Open" is a verb.

page.build.continueInSession.description: Button on a person's own change that was started from a coding agent: opens that agent session.

page.build.continueBuilding.description: Button on a person's own change that is still being built: opens the session where it is built. "Building" is a verb.

page.build.openBuild.description: Button on a person's own change that is up for a vote or finished: opens the session where it was built. "Open" is a verb and "build" a noun.

page.build.readBuild.description: Button on somebody else's change whose author published the session it was built in: opens that record to read. "Build" is a noun.

page.sample.note.text: This is a display-only sample. To try editing a description, open "[Preview sample] Your editable change" in your sessions.
page.sample.note.description: Note on the page of a made-up sample change on a test build of Homeroom. "[Preview sample] Your editable change" is the title of another sample; keep it as written.

page.summary.missingDescription.text: No short summary has been added yet. The current description is below.
page.summary.missingDescription.description: Shown in place of the summary on the page of a change that has a full description and no short summary or plan; the description is folded under this line.

page.summary.missing.text: No change summary has been added yet.
page.summary.missing.description: Shown in place of the summary on a change that has no summary and no description. "Change" is a noun.

page.discussion.shareFirst.text: Make this change visible to the group to start a discussion. Only you can see the agent workspace here unless you share it. Its code is public.
page.discussion.shareFirst.description: Shown in place of the discussion on a person's own change that they have not shared with the project's members yet. "Change" is a noun.

page.steps.actor.auto.description: The whole text of a small grey note shown in its own element beside a step on a change's page, saying who completes that step: nobody, the platform does it by itself. It is not joined to any other words.

page.steps.actor.author.description: The whole text of a small grey note shown in its own element beside a step on a change's page, saying who completes that step: the person who made the change. It is not joined to any other words.

page.steps.actor.admin.description: The whole text of a small grey note shown in its own element beside a step on a change's page, saying who completes that step: an administrator of the project. It is not joined to any other words.

page.steps.actor.group.description: The whole text of a small grey note shown in its own element beside a step on a change's page, saying who completes that step: the project's members, by voting. It is not joined to any other words.

page.steps.label.yourApproval.description: Name of the voting step on a change's page in a project where this person's approval alone decides.

page.steps.label.vote.description: Name of the voting step on a change's page. A noun: the group's vote on the change.

page.steps.headline.goingLive.description: Headline over the steps on the page of a change that was merged while the new version of the app is still being deployed.

page.steps.headline.releaseBlocked.description: Headline over the steps on the page of a change that was merged, but whose automatic release failed one of its steps (for example a security check), so it is not live and will not be until that is fixed.

page.steps.headline.live.description: Headline over the steps on the page of a merged change that is part of the running app. An adjective.

page.steps.headline.liveIncludedIn.description: Headline over the steps on the page of a change that is part of the running app because its work went in as part of another change. {{number}} is that change's pull request number.

page.steps.headline.liveIncludedInAnothe.description: Headline over the steps on the page of a change that is part of the running app because its work went in as part of another change whose number is not known.

page.steps.headline.standing.description: Headline over the steps on a change's page when there is no summary of what it still needs. "It" is the change.

page.draft.gate.review.description: Name of a step in the list of what a change still needs before it goes live, on the page of a change that is still being built. This step is done once the author puts the change up for a vote.

page.draft.gate.reviewDetail.description: Short line under the headline "Nothing needs you" on the page of a change that has not been put up for a vote, naming the step that is under way or that Homeroom does on its own: the step "Submitted for review". Shown alone on its own line; lower case in English.

page.draft.gate.approvals.description: Name of a step in the list of what a change still needs before it goes live, on the page of a change that is still being built. The group's votes on the change. A noun.

page.draft.gate.integration.description: Name of a step in the list of what a change still needs before it goes live, on the page of a change that is still being built. The change's code fits together with "main", the project's current code; "main" is the name of the code branch and stays in English.

page.draft.gate.integrationDetail.description: Short line under the headline "Nothing needs you" on the page of a change that has not been put up for a vote, naming the step that is under way or that Homeroom does on its own: the step "No conflicts with main". Shown alone on its own line; lower case in English.

page.draft.gate.checks.description: Name of a step in the list of what a change still needs before it goes live, on the page of a change that is still being built. The automated tests run on the change. A noun.

page.draft.gate.checksDetail.description: Short line under the headline "Nothing needs you" on the page of a change that has not been put up for a vote, naming the step that is under way or that Homeroom does on its own: the step "Checks". Shown alone on its own line; lower case in English.

page.draft.gate.github.description: Name of a step in the list of what a change still needs before it goes live, on the page of a change that is still being built. The change is combined into the project's code. A noun.

page.draft.gate.githubDetail.description: Short line under the headline "Nothing needs you" on the page of a change that has not been put up for a vote, naming the step that is under way or that Homeroom does on its own: the step "Merge". Shown alone on its own line; lower case in English.

page.draft.line.submitting.description: Short line under a step on the page of a change that is still being built. Under "Submitted for review" while the change is being put up for a vote.

page.draft.line.notSubmitted.description: Short line under a step on the page of a change that is still being built. Under "Submitted for review", for someone other than the author.

page.draft.line.conflictFiles_one.description: Short line under a step on the page of a change that is still being built. Under "No conflicts with main": the change and the project's current code alter the same lines. {{count}} is the number of files affected.

page.draft.line.conflictFiles_other.description: Short line under a step on the page of a change that is still being built. Under "No conflicts with main": the change and the project's current code alter the same lines. {{count}} is the number of files affected.

page.draft.line.conflict.description: Short line under a step on the page of a change that is still being built. Under "No conflicts with main" when the change clashes with the project's current code and the files are not known. "main" is the name of the code branch and stays in English.

page.draft.line.notMeasured.description: Short line under a step on the page of a change that is still being built. Under "No conflicts with main" when the platform has not checked yet whether the change fits the project's current code.

page.draft.line.checksAfterSync.description: Short line under a step on the page of a change that is still being built. Under "Checks": the automated tests start once the change has been brought up to date with the project's current code.

page.draft.line.checksNotRun.description: Short line under a step on the page of a change that is still being built. Under "Checks" when the automated tests have not been started.

vote.names.loading.description: Shown on the voting step of a change's page while the list of who voted is being fetched.

vote.names.none.description: Shown on the voting step of a change's page when nobody has voted.

vote.names.no.description: Line on the voting step of a change's page when everybody who voted voted against. "No" is the vote; {{names}} is the list of their usernames.

vote.names.yesAndNo.description: Line on the voting step of a change's page listing who voted. {{yes}} is the usernames of those who voted yes, shown without a label; "No" is the vote against and {{no}} the usernames of those who cast it.

vote.button.yes.description: The Yes vote button on a proposal's card. {{tally}} is the number of Yes votes so far, for example "3", or "2✓ +1" where votes from approvers and advisory votes are counted separately.

vote.button.no.description: The No vote button on a proposal's card. {{tally}} is the number of No votes so far, for example "1", or "1✓ +2" where votes from approvers and advisory votes are counted separately.

page.checks.build.built.description: Value shown beside the build on the checks step of a change's page once the preview has been built. Past participle: the app was built.

page.checks.build.building.description: Value shown beside the build on the checks step of a change's page while the preview is being built and the current stage is not known.

page.checks.note.previewDidNotStart.description: Note on the checks step of a change's page when its preview (a running test copy of the app) failed to start. {{error}} is the technical error text, in English.

page.checks.note.broken.text: The staging build or the test run itself broke, so the platform can't confirm the app works.
page.checks.note.broken.description: Note on the checks step of a change's page when the automated tests could not be carried out at all. "Staging build" is the test copy of the app.

page.submission.failing.note.text: Its checks are failing. You can submit it now; it can merge only after a fix passes them.
page.submission.failing.note.description: Note and tooltip on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. The automated tests fail. "It" is the change.

page.submission.failing.short.text: Ready · checks must pass before it merges
page.submission.failing.short.description: Short line under the "Submitted for review" step on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. The automated tests fail.

page.submission.error.note.text: Its checks could not run. You can submit it now; it can merge only once they run and pass.
page.submission.error.note.description: Note and tooltip on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. The automated tests could not be run.

page.submission.error.short.text: Ready · checks must run before it merges
page.submission.error.short.description: Short line under the "Submitted for review" step on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. The automated tests could not be run.

page.submission.uploaded.note.text: A commit was uploaded but has not been submitted for checks yet. Ask the agent to submit it first.
page.submission.uploaded.note.description: Note and tooltip on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. A coding agent uploaded code and has not handed it in for testing. "Commit" is a saved revision of the code.

page.submission.uploaded.short.text: The agent has not submitted its commit yet
page.submission.uploaded.short.description: Short line under the "Submitted for review" step on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. "Commit" is a saved revision of the code.

page.submission.empty.note.text: There are no committed changes to submit yet. Ask the agent to make a change first.
page.submission.empty.note.description: Note and tooltip on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. Nothing has been saved to the change yet.

page.submission.empty.short.description: Short line under the "Submitted for review" step on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. No code has been saved to the change.

page.submission.previewClosed.note.text: Ready to submit for review. Its preview was closed while idle; submitting rebuilds it and runs the checks again.
page.submission.previewClosed.note.description: Note and tooltip on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. The tests passed and the preview has since been shut down.

page.submission.previewClosed.short.description: Short line under the "Submitted for review" step on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. The preview has been shut down and will be rebuilt.

page.submission.ready.note.description: Note and tooltip on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. The tests passed.

page.submission.ready.short.description: Short line under the "Submitted for review" step on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote, when nothing stands in the way. An adjective describing the change.

page.submission.running.note.text: You can submit it now. Its checks keep running, and it can merge only once they pass.
page.submission.running.note.description: Note and tooltip on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. The automated tests are still running.

page.submission.running.shortDeferred.text: Ready · checks run after the sync
page.submission.running.shortDeferred.description: Short line under the "Submitted for review" step on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. The tests start once the change is brought up to date with the project's current code.

page.submission.running.shortRunning.description: Short line under the "Submitted for review" step on a person's own change that is still being built, about putting it up for a vote. The automated tests have not finished.

page.ledger.preview.label.description: Label of the row about the change's preview (a running test copy of the app) in the list of facts under Details on a change's page. A noun.

page.ledger.preview.failed.text: <0>Failed.</0> The submitted preview did not start.
page.ledger.preview.failed.description: Text of the Preview row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page when the preview failed to start and no reason is known. <0></0> draws the verdict bold and red.

page.ledger.preview.failedWith.text: <0>Failed.</0> The submitted preview did not start: {{error}}
page.ledger.preview.failedWith.description: Text of the Preview row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page when the preview failed to start. <0></0> draws the verdict bold and red; {{error}} is the technical error text, in English.

page.ledger.checks.label.description: Label of the row about the automated tests in the list of facts under Details on a change's page. A noun.

page.ledger.checks.none.text: No check results have been recorded yet.
page.ledger.checks.none.description: Text of the Checks row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page when no automated test has reported a result.

page.ledger.checks.failing.text: <0>Failing.</0> Required checks need attention before this change can merge.
page.ledger.checks.failing.description: Text of the Checks row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page on a change still being built whose automated tests fail. <0></0> draws the verdict bold and red.

page.ledger.main.label.description: Label of the row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page that says how the change compares with "main", the project's current code. "Main" is the name of the code branch.

page.ledger.main.behind_one.description: Text of the Main row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page: the project's current code has moved on since the change was started. {{count}} is how many commits (saved revisions) it is behind; "main" is the name of the code branch and stays in English.

page.ledger.main.behind_other.description: Text of the Main row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page: the project's current code has moved on since the change was started. {{count}} is how many commits (saved revisions) it is behind; "main" is the name of the code branch and stays in English.
