page.ledger.main.upToDate.description: Text of the Main row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page when the change is based on the project's current code. "main" is the name of the code branch and stays in English.

page.ledger.main.unverified.text: Main freshness has not been verified yet.
page.ledger.main.unverified.description: Text of the Main row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page when the platform has not checked yet whether the change is based on the project's current code.

page.ledger.main.movedAhead.description: Text of the Main row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page when the project's current code has changed since the change was started and the number of commits is not known.

page.ledger.main.forkNote.text: The author must update this branch in their fork, then push the changes.
page.ledger.main.forkNote.description: Smaller note under the Main row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page on a change whose code lives in the author's own copy (fork) of the repository, so Homeroom cannot update it. "Push" is the git verb.

page.ledger.votes.label.description: Label of the row about the group's votes in the list of facts under Details on a change's page. A noun.

page.ledger.review.label.description: Label of the row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page, on a change still being built, that says whether it can be put up for a vote. A noun.

page.ledger.review.submitting.description: Text of the Review row in the list of facts under Details on a change's page while the change is being put up for a vote.

feed.loadFailed.text: Couldn't load the feed right now.
feed.loadFailed.description: Shown in place of a project's board when its items could not be fetched and nothing was loaded before.

feed.comment.earlier_one.description: Line above the newest replies shown under a request's card in the feed, saying how many older replies are not shown. {{count}} is that number.

feed.comment.earlier_other.description: Line above the newest replies shown under a request's card in the feed, saying how many older replies are not shown. {{count}} is that number.

feed.comment.unknownAuthor.description: Shown in place of the author's name on a reply under a request's card when the reply has no known author. Lower case, as a name would sit there.

feed.comment.botTag.description: Small tag after the author's name on a reply under a request's card, marking that an automated account wrote the reply, not a person.

feed.comment.specTitled.description: Line at the end of a reply the Homeroom bot wrote under a request, naming the written plan it attached. {{title}} is that plan's title.

feed.comment.spec.description: Line at the end of a reply the Homeroom bot wrote under a request, saying it attached a written plan that has no title.

feed.comment.showMore.description: Button under a long reply on a request's card in the feed that is cut off after a few lines: shows the whole reply.

feed.comment.showLess.description: Button under a long reply on a request's card in the feed after it was expanded: cuts it back to a few lines.

visuals.fallbackClaim.description: Stands in for the description of a visible change in the before/after screenshots of a change, when the author gave none. It names the pair of screenshots.

explore.title.text: Open an agent session with a message about this change ready to edit and send
explore.title.description: Tooltip on the Explore in a coding agent button of a proposal. "Open" is a verb; "change" is a noun.

explore.seed.pr.text: Let's explore PR {{number}} in this app: "{{title}}".
explore.seed.pr.description: First line of the message Homeroom writes for the person to send to an AI coding agent when they press Explore in a coding agent on a proposal. They can edit it before sending. Keep the straight double quotes around the title. {{number}} is the pull request number and {{title}} its title.

explore.seed.prBy.text: Let's explore PR {{number}} in this app: "{{title}}" by {{author}}.
explore.seed.prBy.description: First line of the message Homeroom writes for the person to send to an AI coding agent when they press Explore in a coding agent on a proposal. They can edit it before sending. Keep the straight double quotes around the title. {{number}} is the pull request number, {{title}} its title and {{author}} the username of its author.

explore.seed.prUntitled.description: Stands in for the title, inside the quotes, in the message written for a coding agent about a pull request that has no title. {{number}} is the pull request number.

explore.seed.proposal.text: Let's explore the proposal "{{title}}" in this app.
explore.seed.proposal.description: First line of the message Homeroom writes for the person to send to an AI coding agent when they press Explore in a coding agent on a proposal. They can edit it before sending. Keep the straight double quotes around the title. Used when the proposal has no pull request number. {{title}} is its title.

explore.seed.proposalBy.text: Let's explore the proposal "{{title}}" in this app by {{author}}.
explore.seed.proposalBy.description: First line of the message Homeroom writes for the person to send to an AI coding agent when they press Explore in a coding agent on a proposal. They can edit it before sending. Keep the straight double quotes around the title. Used when the proposal has no pull request number. {{title}} is its title and {{author}} the username of its author.

explore.seed.proposalUntitled.description: Stands in for the title, inside the quotes, in the message written for a coding agent about a proposal that has no title. Lower case.

explore.seed.prLink.description: Line in the message written for a coding agent about a proposal, giving the address of its pull request on GitHub. {{url}} is that address.

explore.seed.changeLink.description: Line in the message written for a coding agent about a proposal that has no pull request on GitHub, giving the address of the change's own page in Homeroom. {{url}} is that address.

explore.seed.linkedIssues.description: Line in the message written for a coding agent about a proposal, listing the requests it is linked to. {{issues}} is their numbers, for example "#12, #15".

explore.seed.merged.description: Line in the message written for a coding agent about a proposal that has already been merged into the project.

explore.seed.merging.text: This proposal is currently being merged.
explore.seed.merging.description: Line in the message written for a coding agent about a proposal that is being merged into the project right now.

explore.seed.tail.text: Please read it and explain in plain terms what it changes, how it works, and anything risky or worth checking. Just explain it for now, don't change any code or open a PR.
explore.seed.tail.description: Last paragraph of the message Homeroom writes for the person to send to an AI coding agent about a proposal: what the agent is asked to do. "PR" is a pull request.

workshop.category.fallbackName.description: Stands in for a category's name on the Workshop board when the category a filter names is no longer in the list, for example in the filter chip "Category: Category". A noun: a group of related requests and changes.

workshop.weeks.thisWeek.description: Heading of the newest card in the Workshop's week-by-week summary of a project: the card that says what has happened in the current calendar week.

workshop.lane.review.description: Heading of a group of cards inside one category on a project's Workshop tab: the changes that have been put up for a vote and are not approved yet.

workshop.lane.underway.description: Heading of a group of cards inside one category on a project's Workshop tab: requests and changes somebody is working on now.

workshop.lane.open.description: Heading of a group of cards inside one category on a project's Workshop tab: requests nobody has started on. An adjective describing the requests, not the verb.

workshop.lane.shipped.description: Heading of a group of cards inside one category on a project's Workshop tab: the changes that were merged and went live during the last seven days.

workshop.ungrouped.name.description: Name of the last group on the Workshop tab's "By category" view, holding the cards that none of the automatically drafted categories includes yet.

workshop.ungrouped.description.text: Items the categories do not name yet.
workshop.ungrouped.description.description: Line under the "Not yet grouped" heading on the Workshop tab, explaining that the cards below are the ones no category lists yet.

workshop.ungrouped.everything.description: Name of the only group on the Workshop tab's "By category" view when no categories have been drafted for the project yet, so every card is listed together.

workshop.ungrouped.placingName.description: Name of the last group on the Workshop tab's "By category" view when every card in it is new and is being sorted into a category automatically right now.

workshop.ungrouped.placingDescription.text: New cards are placed into a category within a minute or two of arriving.
workshop.ungrouped.placingDescription.description: Line under the "Being placed" heading on the Workshop tab, telling the reader the cards below will move into a category shortly without anyone doing anything.

workshop.ungrouped.somePlacing_one.text: Cards the categories do not cover yet; {{count}} of them is being placed now. They count towards the next re-draft.
workshop.ungrouped.somePlacing_one.description: Line under the "Not yet grouped" heading on the Workshop tab when some of its cards are being sorted into a category automatically right now. {{count}} is how many of them. "Re-draft" is the next time the categories themselves are rewritten automatically.

workshop.ungrouped.somePlacing_other.text: Cards the categories do not cover yet; {{count}} of them are being placed now. They count towards the next re-draft.
workshop.ungrouped.somePlacing_other.description: Line under the "Not yet grouped" heading on the Workshop tab when some of its cards are being sorted into a category automatically right now. {{count}} is how many of them. "Re-draft" is the next time the categories themselves are rewritten automatically.

workshop.ungrouped.notCovered.text: Cards the categories do not cover yet. They count towards the next re-draft of the categories.
workshop.ungrouped.notCovered.description: Line under the "Not yet grouped" heading on the Workshop tab when none of its cards is being sorted right now. "Re-draft" is the next time the categories are rewritten automatically.

workshop.queue.voteAsk.description: The question shown above the Yes and No buttons on a "Needs you" card for a proposal the viewer has not voted on. "Go in" means be merged into the project.

workshop.row.tag.checksPassed.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a change: all of its automatic checks have passed.

workshop.row.tag.live.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a change that was approved and is now part of the running project. An adjective.

workshop.row.tag.waitingForVotes.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a request: a change made for it is up for a vote.

workshop.row.tag.beingWorkedOn.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a request: somebody's change for it is being built right now.

workshop.row.tag.started.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a request: work on it was begun and is not running at the moment. A past participle describing the request.

workshop.row.tag.pickedUp.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a request: somebody has taken it on and has not started building yet.

workshop.row.tag.autoSolving.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a request: Homeroom's agent is working on it by itself, without a person driving.

workshop.row.tag.needsAnswer.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a request: the agent working on it has asked a question and waits for somebody to reply.

workshop.row.tag.draftReady.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a request: the agent has finished a first draft of a change for it, ready to be looked at.

workshop.row.tag.changeBeingWorkedOn.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a change that is still being made: its agent is working right now.

workshop.row.tag.changeStarted.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a change that is still being made: it was begun and nothing is running on it at the moment. A past participle describing the change.

workshop.row.tag.previewReady.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a change that is still being made, beside an eye glyph: a preview build of it can be opened and tried.

workshop.row.tag.previewReadyVote.description: Small status tag on a row in the lists of a project's Workshop tab (Your work, Since your last visit and a week's page). On a change that is up for a vote, beside an eye glyph: a preview build of it can be opened and tried before voting.

countdown.daysHours.description: Short countdown on a proposal's card showing roughly how long until its voting window ends, for example "~2d 5h". {{days}} and {{hours}} are numbers; "d" and "h" abbreviate days and hours. Keep the leading "~" (about).

countdown.days.description: Short countdown on a proposal's card showing roughly how many whole days until its voting window ends, for example "~2d". "d" abbreviates days. Keep the leading "~" (about). {{days}} is the number of days.

countdown.hoursMinutes.description: Short countdown on a proposal's card showing roughly how long until its voting window ends, for example "~3h 20m". "h" and "m" abbreviate hours and minutes. Keep the leading "~" (about). {{hours}} and {{minutes}} are the numbers of hours and minutes.

countdown.hours.description: Short countdown on a proposal's card showing roughly how many whole hours until its voting window ends, for example "~3h". "h" abbreviates hours. Keep the leading "~" (about). {{hours}} is the number of hours.

countdown.minutes.description: Short countdown on a proposal's card showing roughly how many minutes until its voting window ends, for example "~12m". "m" abbreviates minutes. Keep the leading "~" (about). {{minutes}} is the number of minutes.

session.fallbackTitle.description: Title shown on an agent session's card when the session has no title, pull request title or branch name. {{id}} is the session's number. A "session" is one working conversation with a coding agent.

session.prFallbackTitle.description: Stands in for an imported pull request's title, in the dialog that asks whether to archive it, when the pull request has no title. {{number}} is its number on GitHub. "PR" abbreviates pull request.

session.venueTitle.description: Tooltip of the chip on an agent session's card that says where the session is being built. {{venue}} is the name of that place and {{blurb}} a short sentence describing it.

session.failing.names.description: Line on the viewer's own agent session card naming the automated checks that are failing. {{checks}} is one or two check names.

session.failing.namesAndMore_one.description: Line on the viewer's own agent session card naming the automated checks that are failing. {{checks}} is the first two check names and {{count}} how many more are failing.

session.failing.namesAndMore_other.description: Line on the viewer's own agent session card naming the automated checks that are failing. {{checks}} is the first two check names and {{count}} how many more are failing.

session.failing.reason.description: One line of the tooltip on a session card's "Failing: …" text. {{check}} is the name of a failing automated check and {{reason}} why it failed.

session.failing.reasonAdvisory.description: One line of the tooltip on a session card's "Failing: …" text, for a check that is advisory: it failed but does not block the merge. {{check}} is the check's name and {{reason}} why it failed.

session.chip.working.description: Status chip with a spinner on an agent session's card while the AI agent is busy working in that session.

session.chip.importedPr.description: Chip on a session card marking that the change was imported from an existing GitHub pull request, not built in Homeroom. "PR" abbreviates pull request.

session.menu.archivePr.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of an imported pull request's card: closes the pull request on GitHub and archives its card. "Archive" is a verb.

session.menu.archivePrTitle.text: Close this imported pull request and archive its card
session.menu.archivePrTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Archive PR" item in the ⋯ menu of an imported pull request's card.

session.menu.viewPr.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of an agent session's card, for a session whose pull request is on GitHub: opens it on GitHub in a new tab.

session.menu.viewCode.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of an agent session's card, for a session whose code is on Homeroom's own git host rather than GitHub: opens that code in a new tab. "View" is a verb.

session.menu.stopSharingChat.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own agent session card when others can read the session's chat. It states that and, when pressed, stops others reading it.

session.menu.stopSharingChatTitle.text: Stop others reading this chat (they keep the card and the discussion)
session.menu.stopSharingChatTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Chat shared. Stop sharing" item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own agent session card.

session.menu.shareChat.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own agent session card: lets everyone read the conversation with the agent. "Share" is a verb.

session.menu.shareChatTitle.text: Let everyone read this chat, read-only. They can't reply in it, and can't see your costs or uploaded files
session.menu.shareChatTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Share chat" item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own agent session card.

session.menu.openDiscussion.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own agent session card: opens the public discussion thread about that session. "Open" is a verb.

session.menu.openDiscussionCount_one.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own agent session card: opens the public discussion thread about that session. {{count}} is how many messages it has. "Open" is a verb.

session.menu.openDiscussionCount_other.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own agent session card: opens the public discussion thread about that session. {{count}} is how many messages it has. "Open" is a verb.

session.menu.openDiscussionTitle.text: Open the public discussion on this session
session.menu.openDiscussionTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Open public discussion" item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own agent session card.

session.menu.viewChecks.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of an agent session's card: opens the results of the automated checks that ran on the session's change.

session.menu.rerunChecks.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of an agent session's card: runs the automated checks on the session's change again.

session.menu.archive.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own agent session card: archives the session. A verb.

session.menu.archiveTitle.text: Archive this session (closes the PR, frees the slot)
session.menu.archiveTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Archive" item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own agent session card. "The slot" is one of the limited number of sessions a person may have open at once. "PR" abbreviates pull request.

session.mine.importedBy.text: Imported by {{author}} · not waiting for approval yet
session.mine.importedBy.description: Line under the title of the viewer's own card for an imported pull request that has not been put up for a vote. {{author}} is the GitHub name of the pull request's author.

session.mine.importedByUnknown.text: Imported by unknown author · not waiting for approval yet
session.mine.importedByUnknown.description: Line under the title of the viewer's own card for an imported pull request that has not been put up for a vote, when the pull request's author is not known.

session.mine.visibleChatReadable.description: Line under the title of the viewer's own agent session card when everyone can see the session and also read its chat.

session.mine.visible.description: Line under the title of the viewer's own agent session card when everyone can see the session but not read its chat.

session.mine.private.text: Only you can see this here. Its code is public.
session.mine.private.description: Line under the title of the viewer's own agent session card when the session is not shared with the group.

session.mine.workingTitle.description: Tooltip of the viewer's own agent session card while the AI agent is busy. {{title}} is the session's title.

session.actions.askForApproval.description: Button on the viewer's own card for an imported pull request: puts the change up for the group's vote.

session.actions.askForApprovalTitle.text: Ask the group to approve this imported change
session.actions.askForApprovalTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Ask for approval" button on the viewer's own card for an imported pull request.

session.actions.hide.description: Button on the viewer's own agent session card when the session is visible to everyone: makes it private again. A verb.

session.actions.hideTitle.text: Make this session private again (removes it from everyone's In progress area, and stops anyone reading the chat)
session.actions.hideTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Hide" button on the viewer's own agent session card.

session.actions.makeVisible.description: Button on the viewer's own agent session card when only they can see the session: shows it to everyone in the project.

session.actions.makeVisibleTitle.text: Show this session in everyone's In progress area. Others can comment and open its live preview, but can't read your chat unless you also share it
session.actions.makeVisibleTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Make visible" button on the viewer's own agent session card.

session.shared.working.description: Line under the title of another person's agent session card. {{owner}} is that person's account name.

session.shared.workingSomeone.description: Line under the title of another person's agent session card when that person's name is not known. It starts in lower case because a name normally stands there.

session.shared.imported.text: Imported pull request by {{author}} · imported by {{owner}}
session.shared.imported.description: Line under the title of a card for a pull request imported from GitHub. {{author}} is the GitHub name of whoever wrote the pull request and {{owner}} the account name of the person who imported it.

session.shared.importedBySomeone.text: Imported pull request by {{author}} · imported by someone
session.shared.importedBySomeone.description: Line under the title of a card for a pull request imported from GitHub when the importer is not known. {{author}} is the GitHub name of whoever wrote the pull request.

session.shared.importedUnknownAuthor.text: Imported pull request by unknown author · imported by {{owner}}
session.shared.importedUnknownAuthor.description: Line under the title of a card for a pull request imported from GitHub when its author is not known. {{owner}} is the account name of the person who imported it.

session.shared.importedUnknownBoth.text: Imported pull request by unknown author · imported by someone
session.shared.importedUnknownBoth.description: Line under the title of a card for a pull request imported from GitHub when neither its author nor its importer is known.

session.visibility.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when making an agent session visible to everyone, or hiding it again, was refused by the server without an explanation. {{status}} is the HTTP status number, for example 500.

session.visibility.failed.description: Toast shown when making an agent session visible to everyone, or hiding it again, could not be sent. {{error}} is the technical error message.

session.shareChat.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when sharing an agent session's chat with everyone, or stopping that, was refused by the server without an explanation. {{status}} is the HTTP status number, for example 500.

session.shareChat.failed.description: Toast shown when sharing an agent session's chat with everyone, or stopping that, could not be sent. {{error}} is the technical error message.

session.shareChat.confirmTitle.description: Title of the dialog that asks the owner of an agent session to confirm before its chat is made readable by everyone.

session.shareChat.confirmMessage.text: Anyone who can see this app will be able to read the whole conversation. your messages, the AI's replies, and what the coding agent did. They can't reply in your chat, and they can't see your costs or your uploaded files. You can turn this off at any time.
session.shareChat.confirmMessage.description: Body of the dialog that asks the owner of an agent session to confirm before its chat is made readable by everyone. It says what others will and will not be able to see.

session.shareChat.confirmLabel.description: Confirm button of the dialog that asks whether to let everyone read an agent session's chat. "Share" is a verb.

session.unarchive.failed.description: Toast shown when restoring an archived agent session failed and the server gave no explanation.

session.unarchive.failedWith.description: Toast shown when restoring an archived agent session could not be sent. {{error}} is the technical error message.

session.unarchive.restoredTitle.description: Title of the notice shown after an archived agent session was restored but the AI no longer remembers the earlier conversation.

session.unarchive.restoredMessage.text: Claude's memory had already been cleared, so this picks up as a fresh chat on the same branch.
session.unarchive.restoredMessage.description: Body of the "Session restored" notice. Claude is the name of the AI and stays as it is. "Branch" is the line of code changes the session was working on.

session.archive.confirmTitle.description: Title of the dialog that asks the person to confirm archiving an agent session or an imported pull request. {{title}} is its title. "Archive" is a verb.

session.archive.confirmMessageImported.text: This closes the imported pull request on GitHub and archives its card. The source branch is kept.
session.archive.confirmMessageImported.description: Body of the dialog that asks the person to confirm archiving an imported pull request.

session.archive.confirmMessage.text: This closes the PR and frees the slot. You can Unarchive it later to restore it (chat memory is kept for 30 days).
session.archive.confirmMessage.description: Body of the dialog that asks the person to confirm archiving their agent session. "The slot" is one of the limited number of sessions a person may have open. "Unarchive" is the name of the button that restores it. "PR" abbreviates pull request.

session.archive.confirmLabel.description: Confirm button of the dialog that asks whether to archive an agent session or an imported pull request. A verb.

session.archive.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when archiving an agent session was refused by the server without an explanation. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

session.archive.failedWith.description: Toast shown when archiving an agent session could not be sent. {{error}} is the technical error message.

archiveUndo.archived_one.description: Bottom notice shown right after a person archives one of their agent sessions on a project's board, with an Undo button beside it. {{title}} is the session's title. {{count}} (1 here) is how many archives can be undone in a row, newest first.

archiveUndo.archived_other.description: Bottom notice shown right after a person archives an agent session when earlier archives can still be undone too, with an Undo button beside it. {{title}} is the session's title; {{count}} is how many can be undone in a row, newest first, this one included.

archiveUndo.withdrawn_one.description: Bottom notice shown right after a person withdraws their own proposal from the vote, with an Undo button beside it. {{title}} is the proposal's title. {{count}} (1 here) is how many withdrawals or archives can be undone in a row, newest first.

archiveUndo.withdrawn_other.description: Bottom notice shown right after a person withdraws their own proposal when earlier archives or withdrawals can still be undone too, with an Undo button beside it. {{title}} is the proposal's title; {{count}} is how many can be undone in a row, newest first, this one included.

archiveUndo.restored_one.description: Bottom notice shown after Undo brought an archived or withdrawn session back, while earlier ones can still be undone; an Undo button stays beside it. {{title}} is the session's title; {{count}} is how many more can be undone.

archiveUndo.restored_other.description: Bottom notice shown after Undo brought an archived or withdrawn session back, while earlier ones can still be undone; an Undo button stays beside it. {{title}} is the session's title; {{count}} is how many more can be undone.

archiveUndo.restoredLast.description: Bottom notice shown after Undo brought the last archived or withdrawn session back, with nothing left to undo and no button. {{title}} is the session's title.

archiveUndo.undo.description: Button on the bottom notice shown after archiving or withdrawing an agent session: brings the most recent one back. A verb.

transcript.readSession.description: Label of the section on a change's page that expands to show the conversation between the author and the coding agent, which the author chose to share.

transcript.pageTitle.description: Heading of the page that shows a shared conversation between a person and a coding agent, read-only.

transcript.readOnlyTag.description: Small tag after the heading of a shared agent session's page, marking that the viewer can read the conversation but not write in it.

transcript.loading.description: Shown in place of a shared agent session's conversation while it is being fetched.

transcript.notShared.text: This chat is no longer shared.
transcript.notShared.description: Shown in place of a shared agent session's conversation when its owner has stopped sharing it.

transcript.loadFailedHttp.description: Shown in place of a shared agent session's conversation when the server refused to send it. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

transcript.loadFailedWith.description: Shown in place of a shared agent session's conversation when it could not be fetched. {{error}} is the technical error message.

explicit.fallback.sentence.text: This change needs a Yes from another member.
explicit.fallback.sentence.description: Sentence explaining why a proposal that changes a protected setting cannot merge on its own approval: somebody other than its author must vote Yes. "Yes" is the name of the vote button.

explicit.fallback.line.description: Short line under the "A Yes from another member" step of a proposal's list of steps, saying why the step applies. No full stop.

explicit.lead.admins.text: It changes who runs this app.
explicit.lead.admins.description: First sentence of the tooltip and note on a proposal that needs explicit approval, saying why: it changes the list of people who administer the app.

explicit.lead.governance.text: It changes how changes are approved.
explicit.lead.governance.description: First sentence of the tooltip and note on a proposal that needs explicit approval, saying why: it changes the rule for how changes are approved.

explicit.lead.visibility.text: It changes who can see this app.
explicit.lead.visibility.description: First sentence of the tooltip and note on a proposal that needs explicit approval, saying why: it changes who is allowed to see the app.

explicit.lead.platformEnv.text: It changes this app’s platform settings.
explicit.lead.platformEnv.description: First sentence of the tooltip and note on a proposal that needs explicit approval, saying why: it changes the settings the platform holds for the app.

explicit.lead.secrets.description: First sentence of the tooltip and note on a proposal that needs explicit approval, saying why: it changes the app's secret keys.

explicit.lead.changesProtected.description: First sentence of the tooltip and note on a proposal that needs explicit approval, when which setting it changes is not known.

explicit.lockTitle.text: {{reason}} It won’t merge on a timer: it needs real Yes votes to reach the app’s normal threshold, and it can still be voted down.
explicit.lockTitle.description: Tooltip of the lock mark on a proposal that needs explicit approval. {{reason}} is a whole sentence saying why, for example "It changes who can vote." "On a timer" refers to proposals normally being approved automatically when a waiting period ends.

explicit.note.full.text: {{reason}} It won't merge on a timer. {{votes}} It can still be voted down, and it still closes on the usual schedule if nobody engages.
explicit.note.full.description: Note on the page of a proposal that needs explicit approval. {{reason}} is a whole sentence saying why, and {{votes}} a whole sentence saying how many Yes votes it has and needs.

explicit.note.hasVotesNoMember.text: It has the Yes votes it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but none of them is from another member yet.
explicit.note.hasVotesNoMember.description: Sentence inside the note on a proposal that needs explicit approval. {{yes}} is the number of Yes votes it has and {{required}} the number it needs. "Another member" is anyone other than the author.

explicit.note.hasVotes.text: It has the Yes votes it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}) and will merge as soon as the usual checks and conflict gates clear.
explicit.note.hasVotes.description: Sentence inside the note on a proposal that needs explicit approval. {{yes}} is the number of Yes votes it has and {{required}} the number it needs. "Gates" are the remaining automatic conditions before a merge.

explicit.note.needsVotes_one.text: It needs {{count}} real Yes vote and has {{yes}} so far.
explicit.note.needsVotes_one.description: Sentence inside the note on a proposal that needs explicit approval. {{count}} is the number of Yes votes it needs and {{yes}} the number it has.

explicit.note.needsVotes_other.text: It needs {{count}} real Yes votes and has {{yes}} so far.
explicit.note.needsVotes_other.description: Sentence inside the note on a proposal that needs explicit approval. {{count}} is the number of Yes votes it needs and {{yes}} the number it has.

explicit.adminMerge.plain.text: Admin: merge this PR right now, bypassing the vote majority
explicit.adminMerge.plain.description: Tooltip of the "Admin merge" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu, shown to administrators only. "PR" abbreviates pull request.

explicit.adminMerge.admins.text: Admin: merge this change to who runs this app right now, without the vote or another member’s Yes
explicit.adminMerge.admins.description: Tooltip of the "Admin merge" item in the ⋯ menu of a proposal that changes a protected setting: the list of people who administer the app. Shown to administrators only.

explicit.adminMerge.governance.text: Admin: merge this change to how changes are approved right now, without the vote or another member’s Yes
explicit.adminMerge.governance.description: Tooltip of the "Admin merge" item in the ⋯ menu of a proposal that changes a protected setting: the rule for how changes are approved. Shown to administrators only.

explicit.adminMerge.visibility.text: Admin: merge this change to who can see this app right now, without the vote or another member’s Yes
explicit.adminMerge.visibility.description: Tooltip of the "Admin merge" item in the ⋯ menu of a proposal that changes a protected setting: who is allowed to see the app. Shown to administrators only.

explicit.adminMerge.platformEnv.text: Admin: merge this change to this app’s platform settings right now, without the vote or another member’s Yes
explicit.adminMerge.platformEnv.description: Tooltip of the "Admin merge" item in the ⋯ menu of a proposal that changes a protected setting: the settings the platform holds for the app. Shown to administrators only.

explicit.adminMerge.secrets.text: Admin: merge this change to this app’s keys right now, without the vote or another member’s Yes
explicit.adminMerge.secrets.description: Tooltip of the "Admin merge" item in the ⋯ menu of a proposal that changes a protected setting: the app's secret keys. Shown to administrators only.

explicit.adminMerge.protected.text: Admin: merge this change to a protected setting right now, without the vote or another member’s Yes
explicit.adminMerge.protected.description: Tooltip of the "Admin merge" item in the ⋯ menu of a proposal that changes a protected setting, when which setting is not known.

step.adminYes.text: Needs one admin to vote yes
step.adminYes.description: Line under the "Admin approval" step in a proposal's list of steps, while no administrator has voted Yes yet.

step.shots.failed.description: Line under the "Before & after screenshots" step in a proposal's list of steps when the automatic before-and-after screenshots could not be taken.

step.shots.taking.description: Line under the "Before & after screenshots" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automatic before-and-after screenshots are being taken.

step.env.needsValues.description: Line under the "Platform variables" step in a proposal's list of steps when the change needs configuration values that an administrator has not set, and their names are not known.

step.env.setOne.description: Line under the "Platform variables" step in a proposal's list of steps, telling an administrator which configuration value to set. {{name}} is the variable's name, for example STRIPE_KEY. "Set" is an imperative verb.

step.env.setMany.description: Line under the "Platform variables" step in a proposal's list of steps, telling an administrator which configuration values to set. {{names}} is a comma-separated list of variable names and {{last}} the final one. "Set" is an imperative verb.

step.main.passThrough.text: Red, but this change can merge
step.main.passThrough.description: Line under the "Main is healthy" step in a proposal's list of steps. "Red" means the tests on the project's main branch are failing; this change is allowed to merge anyway.

step.main.confirming.description: Line under the "Main is healthy" step in a proposal's list of steps while a test failure on the main branch is being run again to confirm it.

step.main.red.description: Line under the "Main is healthy" step in a proposal's list of steps: the tests on the project's main branch are failing, so merges are paused.

step.main.redSince.description: Line under the "Main is healthy" step in a proposal's list of steps: the tests on the main branch are failing. {{sha}} is the short code of the version where they started failing.

step.main.redTest.description: Line under the "Main is healthy" step in a proposal's list of steps: the tests on the main branch are failing. {{test}} is the name of the failing test.

step.main.redSinceTest.description: Line under the "Main is healthy" step in a proposal's list of steps: the tests on the main branch are failing. {{sha}} is the short code of the version where they started failing and {{test}} the name of the failing test.

step.main.checking.description: Line under the "Main is healthy" step in a proposal's list of steps while the tests are running on the most recent merge.

step.main.resumed.description: Line under the "Main is healthy" step in a proposal's list of steps: the tests on the main branch are failing, but an administrator has allowed merges to continue.

step.github.resolving.description: Line under the "Merge" step in a proposal's list of steps when GitHub refused to merge the change and Homeroom is fixing the cause automatically.

step.github.manualSync.text: GitHub refused · needs a manual sync
step.github.manualSync.description: Line under the "Merge" step in a proposal's list of steps when GitHub refused to merge the change and a person has to bring it up to date with main by hand.

step.integration.notMeasured.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps before Homeroom has checked whether the change conflicts with the main branch.

step.integration.resolvingFiles_one.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps while a conflict with the main branch is being resolved automatically. {{count}} is how many files conflict.

step.integration.resolvingFiles_other.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps while a conflict with the main branch is being resolved automatically. {{count}} is how many files conflict.

step.integration.resolvingMain.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps while a conflict with the main branch is being resolved automatically and the number of files is not known.

step.checks.afterSync.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps: the automated checks will run once the change has been brought up to date with the main branch.

step.checks.skipped.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when the automated checks were not needed and did not run.

step.checks.passed.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when the automated checks passed and no count is available.

step.checks.passedOlder.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when the automated checks passed, but against an earlier version of the main branch.

step.checks.somePassed_one.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps. {{passed}} is how many automated checks passed and {{count}} how many ran.

step.checks.somePassed_other.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps. {{passed}} is how many automated checks passed and {{count}} how many ran.

step.checks.somePassedOlder_one.text: {{passed}} of {{count}} passed · on an older main
step.checks.somePassedOlder_one.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps, when the checks ran against an earlier version of the main branch. {{passed}} is how many automated checks passed and {{count}} how many ran.

step.checks.somePassedOlder_other.text: {{passed}} of {{count}} passed · on an older main
step.checks.somePassedOlder_other.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps, when the checks ran against an earlier version of the main branch. {{passed}} is how many automated checks passed and {{count}} how many ran.

step.checks.allPassed_one.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when every automated check passed. {{count}} is how many ran.

step.checks.allPassed_other.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when every automated check passed. {{count}} is how many ran.

step.checks.allPassedOlder_one.text: All {{count}} passed · on an older main
step.checks.allPassedOlder_one.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when every automated check passed, but against an earlier version of the main branch. {{count}} is how many ran.

step.checks.allPassedOlder_other.text: All {{count}} passed · on an older main
step.checks.allPassedOlder_other.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when every automated check passed, but against an earlier version of the main branch. {{count}} is how many ran.

step.checks.couldNotRun.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when the automated checks could not be run at all.

step.checks.failing.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when automated checks are failing and no count is available.

step.checks.someFailed_one.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps. {{failed}} is how many automated checks failed and {{count}} how many ran.

step.checks.someFailed_other.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps. {{failed}} is how many automated checks failed and {{count}} how many ran.

step.checks.starting.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps just before the automated checks begin.

step.checks.willRunAgain.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when the last run broke and the automated checks are about to be retried.

step.checks.buildingStep.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the preview copy of the app is being built. {{step}} is the build stage it is on and {{steps}} the number of stages.

step.checks.waiting.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks wait their turn to run; only a few proposals are checked at a time.

step.checks.waitingNext.text: Waiting for a slot · next in line
step.checks.waitingNext.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks wait their turn and this proposal is the next to run.

step.checks.waitingAhead_one.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks wait their turn. {{count}} is how many other proposals run before this one.

step.checks.waitingAhead_other.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks wait their turn. {{count}} is how many other proposals run before this one.

step.checks.runningOf.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks run. {{ran}} is how many have finished and {{expected}} how many there are.

step.checks.runningSoFar.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks run and the total is not known. {{ran}} is how many have finished.

step.checks.building.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the preview copy of the app is being built, before the checks run.

step.checks.running.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks are running and no progress is known.

step.resume.label.description: Button beside the "Main is healthy" step in a proposal's list of steps, shown to administrators when merges are paused because the main branch's tests fail: lets merges continue anyway.

step.resume.title.text: Main’s unit suite is failing at this commit. Resume merges on the app anyway; the pause returns if a later merge fails the suite again.
step.resume.title.description: Tooltip of the "Resume merges" button. The "unit suite" is the project's automated tests.

step.resume.resuming.description: Label of the "Resume merges" button while the request is being sent.

step.resume.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when the server refused to resume merges and gave no explanation. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

step.resume.failedWith.description: Toast shown when the request to resume merges could not be sent. {{error}} is the technical error message.

step.resume.done.text: Merges resumed. Anything ready merges on the next pass.
step.resume.done.description: Toast shown after an administrator resumed merges on a project. "The next pass" is the next time Homeroom looks for approved changes to merge, usually within a minute.

step.resume.pending.text: Resuming merges. Homeroom has the request and lifts the pause shortly.
step.resume.pending.description: Toast shown after an administrator asked to resume merges on a project and Homeroom accepted the request but has not applied it yet; the pause shows until it does.

step.headline.live.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when every step is done: the change is merged and running.

step.headline.checking.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps while Homeroom is still working out which steps the change has to pass.

step.headline.merging.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps while the change is being merged right now.

step.headline.blocked.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when an automatic step has failed and the change cannot move on by itself.

step.headline.nothingNeedsYou.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is automatic or already in progress, so the viewer has nothing to do.

step.headline.waitingAuthor.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is something the change's author must do, shown to other people.

step.headline.waitingYouAuthor.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is something the change's author must do, shown to the author.

step.headline.waitingAdmin.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is something an administrator must do, shown to people who are not administrators.

step.headline.waitingYouAdmin.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is something an administrator must do, shown to an administrator.

step.headline.waitingGroup.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is the group's vote and the viewer has already voted.

step.headline.waitingYourApproval.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is the group's vote and the viewer has not voted yet.

step.headline.waiting.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step waits on somebody Homeroom cannot name.

step.integration.manualSyncFiles_one.text: Conflict in {{count}} file · needs a manual sync
step.integration.manualSyncFiles_one.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and it could not be resolved automatically, so a person has to bring the change up to date with main by hand.

step.integration.manualSyncFiles_other.text: Conflict in {{count}} files · needs a manual sync

step.integration.manualSyncMain.text: Conflict with main · needs a manual sync
step.integration.manualSyncMain.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch, and it could not be resolved automatically, so a person has to bring the change up to date with main by hand.

step.integration.mergeForkFiles_one.text: Conflict in {{count}} file · merge main into your fork

step.integration.mergeForkMain.text: Conflict with main · merge main into your fork
step.integration.mergeForkMain.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch, and the viewer wrote the change in their own fork (copy) of the repository and has to merge main into it themselves.

step.integration.checksFirstFiles_other.text: Conflict in {{count}} files · fix the checks first

step.integration.checksFirstMain.text: Conflict with main · fix the checks first

step.integration.checksRerunFiles_one.text: Conflict in {{count}} file · re-run the checks first

step.integration.checksRerunFiles_other.text: Conflict in {{count}} files · re-run the checks first

step.integration.checksRerunMain.text: Conflict with main · re-run the checks first

step.integration.queuedFiles_one.text: Conflict in {{count}} file · queued to fix
step.integration.queuedFiles_one.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and it is waiting its turn to be resolved automatically.

step.integration.queuedFiles_other.text: Conflict in {{count}} files · queued to fix

step.integration.queuedMain.text: Conflict with main · queued to fix
step.integration.queuedMain.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch, and it is waiting its turn to be resolved automatically.

proposal.menu.adminMerge.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu, shown to administrators: merges the change immediately without waiting for the vote.

proposal.menu.openSession.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own proposal: opens the agent session that built the change. "Open" is a verb.

proposal.menu.openSessionTitle.text: Open the agent session behind this change
proposal.menu.openSessionTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Open session" item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own proposal.

proposal.menu.moveBack.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own proposal: takes it out of the vote and returns it to the "Underway" column so they can keep working on it.

proposal.menu.moveBackTitle.text: Take this proposal out of review to keep working on it (clears its votes, keeps the PR open)
proposal.menu.moveBackTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Move back to Underway" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu. "PR" abbreviates pull request.

proposal.menu.withdraw.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own proposal: withdraws the proposal entirely. A verb.

proposal.menu.withdrawTitle.text: Withdraw this proposal (closes the PR, removes it from the vote panel)
proposal.menu.withdrawTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Withdraw" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu. "PR" abbreviates pull request.

proposal.menu.undo.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of a merged change: opens a new proposal that reverses it. A verb.

proposal.menu.undoTitle.text: Open a revert PR for this merge. It still needs a merge vote to land.
proposal.menu.undoTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Undo" item in a merged change's ⋯ menu. A "revert PR" is a pull request that reverses the change; "to land" means to be merged.

proposal.menu.kudosOwnChange.text: You can’t give kudos to your own change
proposal.menu.kudosOwnChange.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Give kudos" item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own proposal. "Kudos" is Homeroom's way of thanking an author.

proposal.menu.kudosViaBounty.text: Credited via a bounty award, so it can’t be retracted
proposal.menu.kudosViaBounty.description: Tooltip of the disabled kudos item in a proposal's ⋯ menu when the viewer's kudos went to the author automatically as a bounty they had pledged.

proposal.menu.retractKudos.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu when the viewer has given kudos to the change and nobody else has: takes their kudos back.

proposal.menu.retractKudosCount_one.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu when the viewer has given kudos to the change: takes their kudos back. {{count}} is how many kudos the change has.

proposal.menu.retractKudosCount_other.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu when the viewer has given kudos to the change: takes their kudos back. {{count}} is how many kudos the change has.

proposal.menu.giveKudos.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu: thanks the author of the change, when it has no kudos yet.

proposal.menu.giveKudosCount_one.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu: thanks the author of the change. {{count}} is how many kudos the change has.

proposal.menu.giveKudosCount_other.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu: thanks the author of the change. {{count}} is how many kudos the change has.

proposal.menu.retractKudosTitle.text: You gave kudos to this change. This retracts it
proposal.menu.retractKudosTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Retract kudos" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu.

proposal.menu.giveKudosTitle.text: Thank the author of this change
proposal.menu.giveKudosTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Give kudos" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu.

proposal.menu.explore.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu: opens an agent session with a message about this change ready to send, so the viewer can ask the agent to explain it.

proposal.menu.retryPreview.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu when building its preview copy of the app failed: tries the build again.

proposal.menu.retryPreviewTitle.text: Try building this proposal's staging preview again
proposal.menu.retryPreviewTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Retry preview" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu. The "staging preview" is the trial copy of the app with the change applied.

proposal.menu.beforeAfter.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu: opens the proposal with its before-and-after screenshots shown.

proposal.menu.beforeAfterTitle.text: Open the declared changes and their before & after screenshots
proposal.menu.beforeAfterTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Before & after" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu. "Declared changes" are the visible changes the author listed; "screenshots" are the pictures Homeroom takes of what a proposal changes.

proposal.menu.screenshots.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu, for an older proposal whose screenshots were captured the earlier way: opens the proposal with them expanded.

proposal.menu.screenshotsTitle.text: Open this proposal and expand its before/after captures
proposal.menu.screenshotsTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Before/after screenshots" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu.

proposal.menu.share.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu: opens a picker to send the proposal's card to a chat or a discussion. "Share" is a verb.

proposal.menu.shareTitle.text: Share this proposal card to a chat or a discussion
proposal.menu.shareTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Share to…" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu.

proposal.menu.viewPr.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu, for a proposal whose pull request is on GitHub: opens it on GitHub in a new tab.

proposal.menu.viewCode.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu, for a proposal whose code is on Homeroom's own git host rather than GitHub: opens that code in a new tab. "View" is a verb.

proposal.details.viewPr.description: Link in the details section of a proposal's page, for a proposal whose pull request is on GitHub: opens it on GitHub.

proposal.details.viewCode.description: Link in the details section of a proposal's page, for a proposal whose code is on Homeroom's own git host rather than GitHub: opens that code. "View" is a verb.

proposal.details.importedBy.description: Fact in the details section of a proposal's page for a change imported from GitHub. {{username}} is the account name of the person who imported it, shown in bold.

proposal.details.proposedBy.description: Fact in the details section of a proposal's page. {{username}} is the account name of the person who put the change up for a vote, shown in bold.

proposal.details.previewBuilding.text: A staging preview is being built for this proposal. It usually takes a few minutes, and a Preview button appears as soon as it's ready. Automated checks run against that preview, so they'll still be pending until then.
proposal.details.previewBuilding.description: Note in the details section of a proposal's page while the trial copy of the app is being built. "Preview" is the name of a button.

proposal.details.previewFailed.text: The staging preview couldn't be built, so there's nothing to preview and the automated checks can't run: {{error}}
proposal.details.previewFailed.description: Warning in the details section of a proposal's page when building the trial copy of the app failed. {{error}} is the technical error message.

proposal.details.lockedNote.text: App is locked, so it also needs at least one admin yes before it merges.
proposal.details.lockedNote.description: Note in the details section of a proposal's page on a project whose administrators have locked it: besides the vote, an administrator must vote Yes.

ledger.label.conflict.description: Label of the row on a proposal's page that says whether the change conflicts with the project's main branch.

ledger.label.checks.description: Label of the row on a proposal's page that reports the automated checks run on the change. A plural noun.

ledger.label.env.description: Label of the row on a proposal's page about configuration values an administrator has to set before the change can merge.

ledger.label.console.description: Label of the row on a proposal's page that reports errors the app logged in the browser console during the automated checks.

ledger.label.preview.description: Label of the row on a proposal's page about the trial copy of the app built with the change. A noun.

ledger.label.note.description: Label of a row on a proposal's page that carries a general remark with no more specific label. A noun.

ledger.label.votes.description: Label of the row on a proposal's page that shows who has voted and how many Yes votes are needed. A plural noun.

ledger.checks.lastRun.description: Small text beside the "Checks" label on a proposal's page. {{when}} is how long ago the automated checks last ran, for example "3h ago".

ledger.checks.passingOne.text: <0>Passing.</0> The one check passed on this build.
ledger.checks.passingOne.description: Text of the "Checks" row on a proposal's page when the change has a single automated check and it passed. The verdict inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.checks.passingAll_one.text: <0>Passing.</0> All {{count}} check passed on this build.
ledger.checks.passingAll_one.description: Text of the "Checks" row on a proposal's page when every automated check passed. {{count}} is how many there are. The verdict inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.checks.passingAll_other.text: <0>Passing.</0> All {{count}} checks passed on this build.
ledger.checks.passingAll_other.description: Text of the "Checks" row on a proposal's page when every automated check passed. {{count}} is how many there are. The verdict inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.checks.passingAdvisory_one.text: <0>Passing.</0> Every merge-blocking check passed on this build. {{count}} check that only advise did not.
ledger.checks.passingAdvisory_one.description: Text of the "Checks" row on a proposal's page when all checks that can block a merge passed but some advisory ones failed. {{count}} is how many advisory checks failed. The verdict inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.checks.passingAdvisory_other.text: <0>Passing.</0> Every merge-blocking check passed on this build. {{count}} checks that only advise did not.
ledger.checks.passingAdvisory_other.description: Text of the "Checks" row on a proposal's page when all checks that can block a merge passed but some advisory ones failed. {{count}} is how many advisory checks failed. The verdict inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.checks.waiting.text: <0>Waiting.</0> They run again by themselves once the branch is up to date. Nothing to do here.
ledger.checks.waiting.description: Text of the "Checks" row on a proposal's page when failing checks are out of date because the change must first be brought up to date with main. "They" are the checks. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.behind.commits_one.description: Small text beside the label of the row on a proposal's page that says the change is behind the main branch. {{count}} is how many commits (saved code changes) behind it is.

ledger.behind.commits_other.description: Small text beside the label of the row on a proposal's page that says the change is behind the main branch. {{count}} is how many commits (saved code changes) behind it is.

ledger.votes.needed.description: Small text beside the "Votes" label on a proposal's page. {{yes}} is the number of Yes votes so far and {{required}} the number needed to approve the change.

ledger.sync.label.description: Label of the first step on a proposal's page when the change has to be brought up to date with the project's main branch before it can merge.

ledger.sync.subNamed.description: Small text beside "Sync with main" on a proposal's page when a person has to do the sync by hand: it names who, and that it is needed now. {{username}} is the author's account name.

ledger.sync.subAuthor.description: Small text beside "Sync with main" on a proposal's page when the change's author has to do the sync by hand and their name is not known.

ledger.sync.fact.moved_one.description: A complete counted fact used inside the sentences of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page, where the sentence has {{moved}} (for example "Main has moved 3 commits ahead, and 2 files changed on both sides, so …"). It has its own plural forms because the sentence holds two different counts. {{count}} is how many commits the project's main branch has gained since this change was started. No full stop: the sentence around it supplies the punctuation.

ledger.sync.fact.moved_other.description: A complete counted fact used inside the sentences of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page, where the sentence has {{moved}} (for example "Main has moved 3 commits ahead, and 2 files changed on both sides, so …"). It has its own plural forms because the sentence holds two different counts. {{count}} is how many commits the project's main branch has gained since this change was started. No full stop: the sentence around it supplies the punctuation.

ledger.sync.fact.overlap_one.description: A complete counted fact used inside the sentences of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page, where the sentence has {{overlap}} (for example "Main has moved 3 commits ahead, and 2 files changed on both sides, so …"). It has its own plural forms because the sentence holds two different counts. {{count}} is how many files were edited both in this change and on main. It follows other words in the sentence, so it does not start with a capital unless your language requires one. No full stop.

ledger.sync.fact.overlap_other.description: A complete counted fact used inside the sentences of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page, where the sentence has {{overlap}} (for example "Main has moved 3 commits ahead, and 2 files changed on both sides, so …"). It has its own plural forms because the sentence holds two different counts. {{count}} is how many files were edited both in this change and on main. It follows other words in the sentence, so it does not start with a capital unless your language requires one. No full stop.

ledger.sync.blocked.commitsAndFiles.text: <0>Blocked.</0> {{moved}}, and {{overlap}}, so the automatic sync cannot finish this one.
ledger.sync.blocked.commitsAndFiles.description: Text of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page when a person has to resolve the conflict by hand. {{moved}} is the complete fact about how far the main branch has moved (changes:ledger.sync.fact.moved, for example "Main has moved 3 commits ahead") and {{overlap}} the complete fact about the files edited on both sides (changes:ledger.sync.fact.overlap, for example "2 files changed on both sides"); each already carries its own number in the right plural form. Place the two wherever your language needs them. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.sync.blocked.commitsLines_one.text: <0>Blocked.</0> Main has moved {{count}} commit ahead, and the two changes touch the same lines, so the automatic sync cannot finish this one.
ledger.sync.blocked.commitsLines_one.description: Text of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page when a person has to resolve the conflict by hand. {{count}} is how many commits the project's main branch has gained since this change was started. Used when the conflicting files are not known. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.sync.blocked.commitsLines_other.text: <0>Blocked.</0> Main has moved {{count}} commits ahead, and the two changes touch the same lines, so the automatic sync cannot finish this one.

Used when the conflicting files are not known. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.sync.blocked.aheadFiles_one.text: <0>Blocked.</0> Main has moved ahead, and {{count}} file changed on both sides, so the automatic sync cannot finish this one.
ledger.sync.blocked.aheadFiles_one.description: Text of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page when a person has to resolve the conflict by hand. Used when the number of new commits on the main branch is not known. {{count}} is how many files were edited both in this change and on main. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.sync.blocked.aheadLines.description: Text of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page when a person has to resolve the conflict by hand. votingHelp.dialogLabel.description: Accessible name of the small pop-up that explains how a proposal is voted on and merged, opened from the help mark on a proposal's page.

votingHelp.sentences.description: Joins two whole sentences into the paragraph shown in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page. {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next sentence. Only the space between sentences is translated.

votingHelp.tally.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page giving the current vote count. {{yes}} and {{no}} are numbers; "Yes" and "No" are the names of the two votes.

votingHelp.merged.text: This proposal has already merged into the app.
votingHelp.merged.description: The whole text of the voting help pop-up on the page of a proposal that has been merged.

votingHelp.merging.text: This passed and is being merged into the app right now.
votingHelp.merging.description: The whole text of the voting help pop-up on the page of a proposal that was approved and is being merged at this moment.

votingHelp.noTimer_one.text: It won’t merge on a timer: it needs {{count}} actual Yes vote.
votingHelp.noTimer_one.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up for a proposal that needs explicit approval: it is not approved automatically when a waiting period ends. {{count}} is how many Yes votes it needs.

votingHelp.noTimer_other.text: It won’t merge on a timer: it needs {{count}} actual Yes votes.
votingHelp.noTimer_other.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up for a proposal that needs explicit approval: it is not approved automatically when a waiting period ends. {{count}} is how many Yes votes it needs.

votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.conflictFail.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: automatic conflict resolution failed, so the proposer must resolve it before it can merge.
votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.conflictFail.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them but cannot merge because Homeroom tried to resolve the conflict with the project's main version and could not, so the person who proposed the change has to. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed. "It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.resolving.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: conflicts with the main app are being reconciled automatically before it can merge.
votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.resolving.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them but cannot merge because Homeroom is resolving the conflict with the project's main version by itself right now. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed. "It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.conflict.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: it conflicts with the main app, so its creator has to sync with main and resolve them before it can merge.
votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.conflict.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them but cannot merge because the change conflicts with the project's main version and its author has to bring it up to date ("sync with main") and resolve the conflicts. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed. "It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.checksFailin.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: its automated checks are failing, so it can’t merge until they pass.
votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.checksFailin.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them but cannot merge because the proposal's automated checks (tests) are failing. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed. "It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.requiresInvited_one.text: This app requires at least {{count}} approval from its invited approvers. Currently {{yes}} of {{count}}.
