votingHelp.setAside.text: More No than Yes, and not enough support yet. It will be set aside in {{time}} unless support arrives.
votingHelp.setAside.description: Text in the voting help pop-up when a proposal is losing the vote. {{time}} is a short countdown such as "~2d 5h". "Set aside" means the proposal is closed without merging.

votingHelp.needs.text: It needs {{required}} of {{active}} active testers to vote Yes.
votingHelp.needs.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up. {{required}} is how many Yes votes the proposal needs and {{active}} how many active members the project has. "Testers" are the project's members.

votingHelp.enoughGoesLive.text: There are enough Yes votes ({{yes}} of {{required}}). It goes live in {{time}} unless someone objects.
votingHelp.enoughGoesLive.description: Text in the voting help pop-up when the proposal has its votes and is waiting out the objection period. {{yes}} is the number of Yes votes, {{required}} the number needed and {{time}} a short countdown such as "~3h 20m".

votingHelp.supportGoesLive.text: It has support ({{yes}} of {{required}} needed) and nobody has objected. It goes live in {{time}} unless the vote changes. Quiet is taken as a nod, so speak up if something bothers you.
votingHelp.supportGoesLive.description: Text in the voting help pop-up when a proposal has some Yes votes, no objections, and will be approved when the waiting period ends. {{yes}} is the number of Yes votes, {{required}} the number that would approve it outright and {{time}} a short countdown such as "~3h 20m".

votingHelp.contested.text: It needs a conversation. Enough people have objected that the timer is off, so it now needs a clear majority of Yes votes to pass.
votingHelp.contested.description: Text in the voting help pop-up when enough members voted No that the proposal will no longer be approved automatically.

votingHelp.advisory_one.text: {{count}} advisory vote from a non-approver is recorded but doesn’t count.
votingHelp.advisory_one.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a project where only invited approvers' votes count. {{count}} is how many votes came from people who are not approvers.

votingHelp.advisory_other.text: {{count}} advisory votes from non-approvers are recorded but don’t count.
votingHelp.advisory_other.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a project where only invited approvers' votes count. {{count}} is how many votes came from people who are not approvers.

remedy.leadThenRest.description: How the two sentences of a proposal's conflict note are put together. {{lead}} is a complete sentence about what Homeroom does on its own, and {{rest}} is a complete sentence about what a person can do (it may contain words in bold). Both are placed exactly where they stand here, so a language may reorder them or change what stands between them.

remedy.lead.mayNotRun.text: Automatic resolution may not run for this proposal.
remedy.lead.mayNotRun.description: First sentence of the note on a proposal's page about a conflict with the main branch, when Homeroom may not be able to resolve it by itself.

remedy.lead.resolvingNow.text: The platform is resolving it now.
remedy.lead.resolvingNow.description: First sentence of the note on a proposal's page about a conflict with the main branch, while Homeroom is resolving it. "It" is the conflict.

remedy.lead.triedAndFailed.text: The platform tried to resolve it and could not.
remedy.lead.triedAndFailed.description: First sentence of the note on a proposal's page about a conflict with the main branch that Homeroom failed to resolve. "It" is the conflict.

remedy.lead.afterVote.text: The platform resolves it once the vote passes.
remedy.lead.afterVote.description: First sentence of the note on a proposal's page about a conflict with the main branch that Homeroom will resolve after the group approves the change. "It" is the conflict.

remedy.lead.automatic.description: First sentence of the note on a proposal's page about a conflict with the main branch that Homeroom will resolve by itself. "It" is the conflict.

remedy.lead.nextMerge.text: Homeroom keeps this branch itself and will try to resolve it automatically at the next merge attempt.
remedy.lead.nextMerge.description: First sentence of the note on an imported proposal's page about a conflict with the main branch, when the code lives in the project's own repository. "It" is the conflict.

remedy.rest.resolveInChat.text: <0>{{creator}}</0> needs to resolve it: run "Sync with main" from the session's dev-chat.
remedy.rest.resolveInChat.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page after automatic resolution failed. "Sync with main" is the name of a command; "dev-chat" is the chat with the coding agent. <0>{{creator}}</0> is the account name of the change's author, shown in bold.

remedy.rest.resolveInChatUnnamed.text: <0>the proposal’s creator</0> needs to resolve it: run "Sync with main" from the session's dev-chat.
remedy.rest.resolveInChatUnnamed.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page after automatic resolution failed. "Sync with main" is the name of a command; "dev-chat" is the chat with the coding agent. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.rest.needsSync.text: <0>{{creator}}</0> needs to bring it up to date: open the agent session and run "Sync with main".
remedy.rest.needsSync.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page when the author must bring the change up to date with main. "Sync with main" is the name of a command. <0>{{creator}}</0> is the account name of the change's author, shown in bold.

remedy.rest.needsSyncUnnamed.text: <0>the proposal’s creator</0> needs to bring it up to date: open the agent session and run "Sync with main".
remedy.rest.needsSyncUnnamed.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page when the author must bring the change up to date with main. "Sync with main" is the name of a command. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.rest.nobody.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page while Homeroom is resolving the conflict by itself.

remedy.rest.canSyncSooner.text: <0>{{creator}}</0> can bring it up to date sooner: open the agent session and run "Sync with main".
remedy.rest.canSyncSooner.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page when Homeroom will resolve the conflict after the vote, but the author may do it earlier. "Sync with main" is the name of a command. <0>{{creator}}</0> is the account name of the change's author, shown in bold.

remedy.rest.canSyncSoonerUnnamed.text: <0>the proposal’s creator</0> can bring it up to date sooner: open the agent session and run "Sync with main".
remedy.rest.canSyncSoonerUnnamed.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page when Homeroom will resolve the conflict after the vote, but the author may do it earlier. "Sync with main" is the name of a command. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.rest.canAlsoSyncSooner.text: <0>{{creator}}</0> can also bring it up to date sooner: open the agent session and run "Sync with main".
remedy.rest.canAlsoSyncSooner.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page when Homeroom will resolve the conflict automatically, but the author may do it earlier. "Sync with main" is the name of a command. <0>{{creator}}</0> is the account name of the change's author, shown in bold.

remedy.rest.canAlsoSyncSoonerUnnamed.text: <0>the proposal’s creator</0> can also bring it up to date sooner: open the agent session and run "Sync with main".
remedy.rest.canAlsoSyncSoonerUnnamed.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page when Homeroom will resolve the conflict automatically, but the author may do it earlier. "Sync with main" is the name of a command. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.rest.resubmit.text: <0>{{creator}}</0> needs to bring the branch up to date with main in the coding agent that wrote it, then submit it again as an update to this proposal. Homeroom keeps this branch itself, so the merge is retried once the update lands.
remedy.rest.resubmit.description: Text of the conflict note on an imported proposal's page after automatic resolution failed, when the code lives in the project's own repository. <0>{{creator}}</0> is the account name of the change's author, shown in bold.

remedy.rest.resubmitUnnamed.text: <0>the proposal’s creator</0> needs to bring the branch up to date with main in the coding agent that wrote it, then submit it again as an update to this proposal. Homeroom keeps this branch itself, so the merge is retried once the update lands.
remedy.rest.resubmitUnnamed.description: Text of the conflict note on an imported proposal's page after automatic resolution failed, when the code lives in the project's own repository. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.rest.resubmitIfFails.text: If that fails, <0>{{creator}}</0> needs to bring the branch up to date with main in the coding agent that wrote it and submit it again as an update to this proposal.
remedy.rest.resubmitIfFails.description: Sentence in the conflict note on an imported proposal's page, after the sentence saying Homeroom will try to resolve the conflict at the next merge attempt. <0>{{creator}}</0> is the account name of the change's author, shown in bold.

remedy.rest.resubmitIfFailsUnnamed.text: If that fails, <0>the proposal’s creator</0> needs to bring the branch up to date with main in the coding agent that wrote it and submit it again as an update to this proposal.
remedy.rest.resubmitIfFailsUnnamed.description: Sentence in the conflict note on an imported proposal's page, after the sentence saying Homeroom will try to resolve the conflict at the next merge attempt. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.rest.fork.text: This branch lives in <0>{{creator}}</0>’s own fork, which Homeroom cannot write to, so it cannot sync it itself. <1>{{creator}}</1> needs to merge main into the branch and push it; the proposal follows the push.
remedy.rest.fork.description: Text of the conflict note on an imported proposal's page when the code lives in its author's own copy (fork) of the repository. {{creator}} is the author's account name, shown in bold both times.

remedy.rest.forkUnnamed.text: This branch lives in <0>the proposal’s creator</0>’s own fork, which Homeroom cannot write to, so it cannot sync it itself. <1>the proposal’s creator</1> needs to merge main into the branch and push it; the proposal follows the push.
remedy.rest.forkUnnamed.description: Text of the conflict note on an imported proposal's page when the code lives in its author's own copy (fork) of the repository. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold both times and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.detail.failed.text: The change’s owner needs to resolve it from their agent session.
remedy.detail.failed.description: Short explanation, in a tooltip, of why a proposal is blocked after automatic conflict resolution failed. "It" is the conflict with the main branch.

remedy.detail.conflict.text: Its creator needs to bring it up to date from their agent session ("Sync with main").
remedy.detail.conflict.description: Short explanation, in a tooltip, of why a proposal that conflicts with the main branch is blocked. "Sync with main" is the name of a command.

remedy.label.text: Needs author to sync with main
remedy.label.description: Short status label on a proposal that conflicts with the main branch when its author has to bring it up to date by hand.

conflictNote.files.description: Line above the list of file names in the conflict note on a proposal's page.

conflictNote.lastAttempt.description: Line in the conflict note on a proposal's page. {{when}} is how long ago Homeroom last tried to merge or resolve it, for example "3h ago".

conflictNote.headingFailed.description: Heading of the conflict note on a proposal's page when Homeroom tried to resolve a conflict with the main branch and could not.

conflictNote.headingConflict.text: A merge was attempted, but this proposal conflicts with main.
conflictNote.headingConflict.description: Heading of the conflict note on a proposal's page when a merge was tried and the change conflicts with the main branch.

mergeability.explanation.text: Main has moved on since this was written, and the two changes touch the same lines. It cannot merge until somebody reconciles them.
mergeability.explanation.description: First line of the note on a proposal's page that warns, before any merge is tried, that the change would conflict with the main branch.

mergeability.files.description: Line above the list of files that were edited both in the proposal and on the main branch, in the conflict warning on a proposal's page.

mergeability.filesSample.text: That is a sample of the files, and some of them may merge cleanly.
mergeability.filesSample.description: Line under the list of files in the conflict warning on a proposal's page, when the list is incomplete.

mergeability.filesHint.text: Some of those may still merge cleanly. They are where to look first.
mergeability.filesHint.description: Line under the list of files in the conflict warning on a proposal's page, when the list is complete.

mergeability.checked.description: Line in the conflict warning on a proposal's page. {{when}} is how long ago Homeroom checked whether the change merges, for example "3h ago".

mergeability.heading.text: This proposal no longer merges into main on its own.
mergeability.heading.description: Heading of the note on a proposal's page that warns the change would conflict with the main branch.

envNote.errorHeading.description: Heading of a note on a proposal's page when Homeroom could not verify that the configuration values the change needs are set.

envNote.errorBody.text: This does not block the merge. The check is re-run when votes reach the threshold.
envNote.errorBody.description: Body of the note on a proposal's page shown when the platform variables could not be checked.

envNote.missingHeading.text: ⚠ New platform variables have no value set. Merge is blocked.
envNote.missingHeading.description: Heading of a warning on a proposal's page when the change adds configuration values that nobody has set. Keep the leading ⚠ and the space after it.

envNote.deployWithout_one.text: Deploying without it would restart the platform missing configuration it now expects.
envNote.deployWithout_one.description: Line in the warning about unset platform variables on a proposal's page. {{count}} is how many variables are missing; "it" (or "them") refers to those values.

envNote.deployWithout_other.text: Deploying without them would restart the platform missing configuration it now expects.
envNote.deployWithout_other.description: Line in the warning about unset platform variables on a proposal's page. {{count}} is how many variables are missing; "it" (or "them") refers to those values.

envNote.setAndVote_one.text: No rebuild needed. Set the value and vote again.
envNote.setAndVote_one.description: Line in the warning about unset platform variables on a proposal's page, telling an administrator what to do. {{count}} is how many values are missing.

envNote.setAndVote_other.text: No rebuild needed. Set the values and vote again.
envNote.setAndVote_other.description: Line in the warning about unset platform variables on a proposal's page, telling an administrator what to do. {{count}} is how many values are missing.

envNote.setNow.description: Button in the warning about unset platform variables on a proposal's page, shown to administrators: opens the panel where the values are set.

envNote.proposeValue.description: Button in the warning about unset platform variables on a proposal's page, shown to people who are not administrators: opens the panel where they can suggest a value.

envNote.added.text: This proposal adds {{names}}, already set and ready for the deploy.
envNote.added.description: Line on a proposal's page when the change adds configuration values and all of them are set. {{names}} is a comma-separated list of the variables' names.

envNote.carried_one.text: {{names}} carries its value with this proposal, applied when it merges.
envNote.carried_one.description: Line on a proposal's page about configuration values whose values travel with the proposal. {{names}} is a comma-separated list of {{count}} variable names.

envNote.carried_other.text: {{names}} carry their values with this proposal, applied when it merges.
envNote.carried_other.description: Line on a proposal's page about configuration values whose values travel with the proposal. {{names}} is a comma-separated list of {{count}} variable names.

envNote.okHeading.description: Heading of a note on a proposal's page when the configuration values the change adds are all set. Keep the leading ✓ and the space after it.

consoleNote.intro.text: The staging preview logged these console errors when it loaded:
consoleNote.intro.description: Line above the list of errors in the warning on a proposal's page that the trial copy of the app reported errors in the browser console.

consoleNote.detected.text: Console errors were detected on the staging preview.
consoleNote.detected.description: Line in the console-errors warning on a proposal's page when the errors themselves are not available to list.

consoleNote.lastChecked.description: Line in the console-errors warning on a proposal's page. {{when}} is how long ago the check ran, for example "3h ago".

consoleNote.fix.text: Pushing a fix rebuilds the preview and re-runs the check. The warning clears if the errors are gone.
consoleNote.fix.description: Last line of the console-errors warning on a proposal's page, telling the author how to clear it.

consoleNote.heading.text: ⚠ This change may break the app.
consoleNote.heading.description: Heading of the warning on a proposal's page that the trial copy of the app reported errors in the browser console. Keep the leading ⚠ and the space after it.

recheck.running.description: Label of the "Re-run checks" button on a proposal or session while the request to run the automated checks again is in progress.

recheck.label.description: Button on a proposal or an agent session whose automated checks did not pass: runs them again.

recheck.title.text: Rebuild the staging preview if needed and re-run the automated tests
recheck.title.description: Tooltip of the "Re-run checks" button on a proposal or an agent session.

recheck.botFixing.text: Homeroom bot is fixing this. Re-running now would restart its fix.
recheck.botFixing.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Re-run checks" button on a change's page while Homeroom bot, the change's author, is fixing the checks that failed on it.

progress.checks.sub.ofExpected_one.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{expected}} how many there are in all. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sub.ofExpected_other.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{expected}} how many there are in all. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sub.ofExpectedFailed_one.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed, {{failed}} how many failed and {{expected}} how many there are in all. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sub.ofExpectedFailed_oth.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed, {{failed}} how many failed and {{expected}} how many there are in all. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sub.soFar_one.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sub.soFar_other.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sentence.ofExpected_one.text: {{count}} of {{expected}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed.
progress.checks.sentence.ofExpected_one.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{expected}} how many checks there are in all.

progress.checks.sentence.ofExpected_othe.text: {{count}} of {{expected}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed.
progress.checks.sentence.ofExpected_othe.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{expected}} how many checks there are in all.

progress.checks.sentence.ofExpectedFaile.text: {{count}} of {{expected}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed, {{failed}} failed.
progress.checks.sentence.ofExpectedFaile.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed, {{failed}} how many failed and {{expected}} how many checks there are in all.

progress.checks.sentence.ofExpectedFaile.text: {{count}} of {{expected}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed, {{failed}} failed.
progress.checks.sentence.ofExpectedFaile.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed, {{failed}} how many failed and {{expected}} how many checks there are in all.

progress.checks.sentence.soFar_one.text: {{count}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed.
progress.checks.sentence.soFar_one.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed.

progress.checks.sentence.soFar_other.text: {{count}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed.
progress.checks.sentence.soFar_other.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed.

Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{failed}} how many failed.

Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{failed}} how many failed.

progress.duration.seconds.description: A short length of time under one minute, for example "20s", used inside the lines that say how long a step of building a proposal's preview took. {{seconds}} is a whole number; "s" abbreviates seconds.

progress.duration.minutesSeconds.description: A length of time of a minute or more, for example "9m 40s", used inside the lines that say how long a step of building a proposal's preview took. {{minutes}} and {{seconds}} are whole numbers; "m" and "s" abbreviate minutes and seconds.

progress.build.label.fetch.description: Name of one of the five steps in the row that shows a proposal's preview being built, on the proposal's page. This step is fetching the proposal's branch of code. It is an imperative-style step name, all lower case.

progress.build.label.fetchTemplate.description: Name of one of the five steps in the row that shows a proposal's preview being built, on the proposal's page. This step is fetching the proposal's branch of code. It is an imperative-style step name, all lower case. "(from template)" says the step was quick because it reused a ready-made template instead of starting from nothing.

progress.build.label.fetchWaited.text: fetch branch (waited for an earlier run)
progress.build.label.fetchWaited.description: Name of one of the five steps in the row that shows a proposal's preview being built, on the proposal's page. This step is fetching the proposal's branch of code. It is an imperative-style step name, all lower case. "(waited for an earlier run)" says the step is finished and took long because it waited for an earlier run of the same proposal's checks.

progress.build.done.fetch.description: One item in the list of finished steps after "Preview build:" or "Preview built in 20s:" in the checks note on a proposal's page: the step of fetching the proposal's branch of code is finished. {{duration}} is how long it took, for example "3s". Items are joined with commas, so it starts in lower case.

progress.build.done.fetchTemplate.description: One item in the list of finished steps after "Preview build:" or "Preview built in 20s:" in the checks note on a proposal's page: the step of fetching the proposal's branch of code is finished. {{duration}} is how long it took, for example "3s". Items are joined with commas, so it starts in lower case. "from template" says it reused a ready-made template.

progress.build.now.fetch.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its preview is being built: the step running now is fetching the proposal's branch of code. No step has finished yet.

progress.build.nowAfter.fetch.text: Preview build: {{steps}}, now fetching the branch.
progress.build.nowAfter.fetch.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its preview is being built: the step running now is fetching the proposal's branch of code. {{steps}} is the list of finished steps with their times, for example "branch fetched (3s), image built (40s)".

progress.build.sub.fetch.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its preview is being built: the step running now is fetching the proposal's branch of code. "build" is a noun here, the building of the preview; the line starts in lower case.

progress.build.label.image.description: Name of one of the five steps in the row that shows a proposal's preview being built, on the proposal's page. This step is building the container image the preview runs from. It is an imperative-style step name, all lower case.

progress.build.label.imageTemplate.description: Name of one of the five steps in the row that shows a proposal's preview being built, on the proposal's page. This step is building the container image the preview runs from. It is an imperative-style step name, all lower case. "(from template)" says the step was quick because it reused a ready-made template instead of starting from nothing.

progress.build.label.imageWaited.text: build image (waited for an earlier run)
progress.build.label.imageWaited.description: Name of one of the five steps in the row that shows a proposal's preview being built, on the proposal's page. This step is building the container image the preview runs from. It is an imperative-style step name, all lower case. "(waited for an earlier run)" says the step is finished and took long because it waited for an earlier run of the same proposal's checks.

progress.build.done.image.description: One item in the list of finished steps after "Preview build:" or "Preview built in 20s:" in the checks note on a proposal's page: the step of building the container image the preview runs from is finished. {{duration}} is how long it took, for example "3s". Items are joined with commas, so it starts in lower case.

progress.build.done.imageTemplate.description: One item in the list of finished steps after "Preview build:" or "Preview built in 20s:" in the checks note on a proposal's page: the step of building the container image the preview runs from is finished. {{duration}} is how long it took, for example "3s". Items are joined with commas, so it starts in lower case. "from template" says it reused a ready-made template.

progress.build.now.image.text: Preview build: building the preview image.
progress.build.now.image.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its preview is being built: the step running now is building the container image the preview runs from. No step has finished yet.

progress.build.nowAfter.image.text: Preview build: {{steps}}, now building the preview image.
progress.build.nowAfter.image.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its preview is being built: the step running now is building the container image the preview runs from. {{steps}} is the list of finished steps with their times, for example "branch fetched (3s), image built (40s)".

progress.build.sub.image.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its preview is being built: the step running now is building the container image the preview runs from. "build" is a noun here, the building of the preview; the line starts in lower case.

progress.build.label.clone.description: Name of one of the five steps in the row that shows a proposal's preview being built, on the proposal's page. This step is making the preview's copy of the app's database. It is an imperative-style step name, all lower case.

progress.build.label.cloneTemplate.description: Name of one of the five steps in the row that shows a proposal's preview being built, on the proposal's page. This step is making the preview's copy of the app's database. It is an imperative-style step name, all lower case. "(from template)" says the step was quick because it reused a ready-made template instead of starting from nothing.

progress.build.label.cloneWaited.text: clone database (waited for an earlier run)
progress.build.label.cloneWaited.description: Name of one of the five steps in the row that shows a proposal's preview being built, on the proposal's page. checks.none.heading.description: Heading of the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when the change is still being worked on and its automated checks have never run.

checks.none.body.text: Checks run once the agent commits a change: a staging preview is built, then the automated tests run against it.
checks.none.body.description: Body of the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page under "No checks yet": says when the automated checks will first run. "Checks run" is a statement (the checks will run), not a command; "the agent" is the AI coding agent working on the change.

checks.starting.heading.description: Heading of the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page, beside a spinner, when a first run of the automated checks is about to begin.

checks.starting.body.text: The staging preview is being prepared, then automated tests run against it. Merge is blocked until all tests pass.
checks.starting.body.description: Body of the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page under "Checks are starting…". "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app.

checks.starting.stuck.text: If this has been stuck for a while, the platform re-runs the checks automatically, or re-run them now.
checks.starting.stuck.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when the checks have been "starting" for over ten minutes; a "Re-run checks" button follows it. "re-run them now" addresses the reader.

checks.deferred.heading.text: Checks deferred until this merges cleanly.
checks.deferred.heading.description: Heading of the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when the preview was built but the tests were put off because the proposal conflicts with the main line of code. "this" is the proposal.

checks.deferred.body.text: This proposal conflicts with main, so its preview was built but the automated tests were not run: they would judge a tree that cannot merge. They run automatically once it merges cleanly, and the merge waits for them.
checks.deferred.body.description: Body of the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when the tests were put off. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is; "a tree" is a version of the code.

checks.deferred.builtWhen.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when the tests were put off: when the preview was built. {{when}} is a relative time such as "5 minutes ago".

checks.deferred.rerun.text: To test this head as it stands anyway, re-run the checks.
checks.deferred.rerun.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when the tests were put off; a "Re-run checks" button follows it. "this head" is the proposal's latest commit.

checks.pending.waitingSince.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page while the run waits its turn for a free slot. {{when}} is a relative time such as "4 minutes ago".

checks.pending.started.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page while the automated checks are running: when this run began. {{when}} is a relative time such as "4 minutes ago".

checks.pending.movedConflict_one.text: Main has moved {{count}} commit ahead and this proposal conflicts with it. This run is judged against the commit before that, so when the platform resolves the conflict the run starts again on the resolved commit.
checks.pending.movedConflict_one.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page while the checks are running and the project's main line of code ("main", kept as it is) has gained {{count}} commits that this proposal conflicts with. "run" is a noun: this run of the checks.

checks.pending.movedConflict_other.text: Main has moved {{count}} commits ahead and this proposal conflicts with it. This run is judged against the commit before that, so when the platform resolves the conflict the run starts again on the resolved commit.
checks.pending.movedConflict_other.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page while the checks are running and the project's main line of code ("main", kept as it is) has gained {{count}} commits that this proposal conflicts with. "run" is a noun: this run of the checks.

checks.pending.movedClean_one.text: Main has moved {{count}} commit ahead. That does not restart this run: a proposal that still merges cleanly merges as it stands.
checks.pending.movedClean_one.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page while the checks are running and the project's main line of code ("main", kept as it is) has gained {{count}} commits that this proposal does not conflict with. "run" is a noun: this run of the checks.

checks.pending.movedClean_other.text: Main has moved {{count}} commits ahead. That does not restart this run: a proposal that still merges cleanly merges as it stands.
checks.pending.movedClean_other.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page while the checks are running and the project's main line of code ("main", kept as it is) has gained {{count}} commits that this proposal does not conflict with. "run" is a noun: this run of the checks.

checks.pending.stuck.text: If this has been running for a while, the platform re-runs the checks automatically, or re-run them now.
checks.pending.stuck.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when a run of the checks has been going for over ten minutes; a "Re-run checks" button follows it. "re-run them now" addresses the reader.

checks.pending.left_one.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page while the automated checks run: how much longer they should take, from this project's usual time. {{count}} is the estimated number of minutes.

checks.pending.left_other.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page while the automated checks run: how much longer they should take, from this project's usual time. {{count}} is the estimated number of minutes.

checks.pending.leftUnder.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page while the automated checks run: under a minute should remain.

checks.pending.longer_one.text: This is taking longer than usual (usually about {{count}} minute).
checks.pending.longer_one.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when a run has gone past its usual total time. {{count}} is how many minutes a whole run usually takes here.

checks.pending.longer_other.text: This is taking longer than usual (usually about {{count}} minutes).
checks.pending.longer_other.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when a run has gone past its usual total time. {{count}} is how many minutes a whole run usually takes here.

checks.pending.wait_one.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page while a run waits for a free slot: how long its wait should be. {{count}} is the estimated number of minutes.

checks.pending.wait_other.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page while a run waits for a free slot: how long its wait should be. {{count}} is the estimated number of minutes.

checks.pending.waitLonger.text: This wait is longer than usual.
checks.pending.waitLonger.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when a run has waited for a free slot longer than its rough wait suggested.

checks.pending.rough.text: A rough estimate from other projects, since this one has few finished runs.
checks.pending.rough.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when the time shown is borrowed from recent runs across Homeroom: the project has too few finished runs of its own.

checks.error.heading.description: Heading of the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when the automated checks could not be run at all (the build or the test run broke). Keep the warning sign.

checks.error.generic.text: The staging build or the test run itself broke, so the platform can't confirm the app works.
checks.error.generic.description: Body of the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page under "Checks couldn't run." when no more specific reason was recorded.

checks.error.blocked.text: Merge is blocked until checks pass. Pushing a fix rebuilds the preview and re-runs the checks.
checks.error.blocked.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page under "Checks couldn't run.". "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app. "Pushing a fix" is uploading a corrected commit.

checks.skipped.heading.description: Heading of the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page when the automated checks were left out on purpose because there was nothing for them to test.

checks.skipped.withReason.text: Checks were skipped: {{reason}}. It can still go live.
checks.skipped.withReason.description: Body of the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page under "Checks skipped.". {{reason}} is the reason the platform recorded, in its own words, without a full stop. "It" is the change; "go live" means be merged and running.

checks.skipped.nothingToTest.text: Checks were skipped: there was nothing to test. It can still go live.
checks.skipped.nothingToTest.description: Body of the checks note on a proposal's or agent session's page under "Checks skipped." when no reason was recorded. "It" is the change; "go live" means be merged and running.

checks.reason.failedRuns_one.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build.
checks.reason.failedRuns_one.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more).

checks.reason.failedRuns_other.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build.
checks.reason.failedRuns_other.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more).

checks.reason.failedThenPassed_one.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build, then passed when re-run.
checks.reason.failedThenPassed_one.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more). The check passed in the end.

checks.reason.failedThenPassed_other.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build, then passed when re-run.
checks.reason.failedThenPassed_other.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more). The check passed in the end.

checks.reason.failedRunsWith_one.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build. {{reason}}
checks.reason.failedRunsWith_one.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more). {{reason}} is the failure message the check itself wrote, shown as it is.

checks.reason.failedRunsWith_other.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build. {{reason}}
checks.reason.failedRunsWith_other.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more). {{reason}} is the failure message the check itself wrote, shown as it is.

checks.reason.failedThenPassedWith_one.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build, then passed when re-run. {{reason}}
checks.reason.failedThenPassedWith_one.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more). The check passed in the end. {{reason}} is the failure message the check itself wrote, shown as it is.

checks.reason.failedThenPassedWith_other.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build, then passed when re-run. {{reason}}
checks.reason.failedThenPassedWith_other.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more). The check passed in the end. {{reason}} is the failure message the check itself wrote, shown as it is.

checks.reason.earlyBurst.text: Failed early in the run together with other checks, then passed every re-run. This often means the test environment was not ready yet, but check that this change does not break the screen this check opens.
checks.reason.earlyBurst.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that failed in a burst of failures in the first seconds of the test run and then passed every time it was run again on a fresh page. Says the environment is a likely cause but not a proven one, and asks the author to check the screen anyway.

checks.reason.earlyBurstWith.text: Failed early in the run together with other checks, then passed every re-run. This often means the test environment was not ready yet, but check that this change does not break the screen this check opens. {{reason}}
checks.reason.earlyBurstWith.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that failed in a burst of failures in the first seconds of the test run and then passed every time it was run again on a fresh page. Says the environment is a likely cause but not a proven one, and asks the author to check the screen anyway. {{reason}} is the failure message the check itself wrote, shown as it is.

checks.note.freshLoad.text: This check needed a fresh load after an address change: fix the navigation (an address change must draw what a fresh load of that address draws).
checks.note.freshLoad.description: Advice under one automated check that this proposal adds or changes, in its opened details. The checks reach several screens of one page by changing the address after the # sign; this check only passed after the page was loaded again from scratch. Tells the author to fix the app's navigation so that changing the address shows the same screen a fresh load of that address shows. Advisory: the check's result is unchanged.

verdict.summary.checks_one.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many automated checks ran.

verdict.summary.checks_other.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many automated checks ran.

verdict.summary.passed_one.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many checks passed.

verdict.summary.passed_other.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many checks passed.

verdict.summary.blocking_one.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many failed checks stop the change from being merged.

verdict.summary.blocking_other.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many failed checks stop the change from being merged.

verdict.summary.advisory_one.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many failed checks are advisory: they are reported but do not stop the merge.

verdict.summary.advisory_other.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many failed checks are advisory: they are reported but do not stop the merge.

verdict.heading.failed.text: ⚠ Some checks failed. Merge is blocked until they pass.
verdict.heading.failed.description: Heading of the check results on a proposal's page when at least one check that gates the merge failed. Keep the warning sign. "Merge" is the noun.

verdict.heading.blockingPassed.text: ✓ Every merge-blocking check passed on the staging build.
verdict.heading.blockingPassed.description: Heading of the check results on a proposal's page when every check that gates the merge passed and only advisory checks failed. Keep the check mark. "the staging build" is the preview built from the proposal.

verdict.heading.allPassed.text: ✓ All checks passed on the staging build.
verdict.heading.allPassed.description: Heading of the check results on a proposal's page when every check passed. Keep the check mark. "the staging build" is the preview built from the proposal.

verdict.advisoryNote.text: Advisory checks have not yet passed on a change that merged, so they report without blocking. Fix one, and once the fix merges it guards every change after it.
verdict.advisoryNote.description: Note under a proposal's check results explaining what an advisory check is: a check that has never passed on a merged change, so its failures do not block. Once a change that makes it pass merges, it blocks every later change that fails it.

verdict.lastChecked.description: Small print under a proposal's check results: when the checks last ran. {{when}} is a relative time such as "3 hours ago".

verdict.fixNote.text: Pushing a fix rebuilds the preview and re-runs the checks. The block clears when they pass.
verdict.fixNote.description: Small print under a proposal's failed check results. "Pushing a fix" is uploading a corrected commit; "The block" is the block on merging.

verdict.row.unnamedCheck.description: Stands in for a check's name in a proposal's list of check results when the check has no name. A noun, lower case.

verdict.row.unnamedTest.description: Stands in for a unit test's name above its captured error text in a proposal's check results, when the test has no name. A noun, lower case.

checks.baseNote.these.agoConflict_one.text: These ran against main as it was {{count}} commit ago, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. It now conflicts with main; resolving the conflict re-runs them on the resolved commit.
checks.baseNote.these.agoConflict_one.description: Note under a proposal's check results when they were earned against an older state of the main line of code. "These" and "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. The proposal now conflicts with main.

checks.baseNote.these.agoConflict_other.text: These ran against main as it was {{count}} commits ago, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. It now conflicts with main; resolving the conflict re-runs them on the resolved commit.
checks.baseNote.these.agoConflict_other.description: Note under a proposal's check results when they were earned against an older state of the main line of code. "These" and "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. The proposal now conflicts with main.

checks.baseNote.these.movedConflict.text: These ran against a version of main that has since moved on, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. It now conflicts with main; resolving the conflict re-runs them on the resolved commit.
checks.baseNote.these.movedConflict.description: Note under a proposal's check results when they were earned against an older state of the main line of code. "These" and "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. Used when it is not known how far main has moved. The proposal now conflicts with main.

checks.baseNote.these.agoClean_one.text: These ran against main as it was {{count}} commit ago, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. That does not hold the merge: a proposal that still merges cleanly merges as it stands, and the platform runs the app’s tests on main again straight after.
checks.baseNote.these.agoClean_one.description: Note under a proposal's check results when they were earned against an older state of the main line of code. "These" and "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. The proposal still merges cleanly, so nothing holds it.

checks.baseNote.these.agoClean_other.text: These ran against main as it was {{count}} commits ago, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. That does not hold the merge: a proposal that still merges cleanly merges as it stands, and the platform runs the app’s tests on main again straight after.
checks.baseNote.these.agoClean_other.description: Note under a proposal's check results when they were earned against an older state of the main line of code. "These" and "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. The proposal still merges cleanly, so nothing holds it.

That does not hold the merge: a proposal that still merges cleanly merges as it stands, and the platform runs the app’s tests on main again straight after.
checks.baseNote.these.movedClean.description: Note under a proposal's check results when they were earned against an older state of the main line of code. "These" and "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. Used when it is not known how far main has moved. The proposal still merges cleanly, so nothing holds it.

checks.baseNote.passedBut.agoConflict_on.text: The checks passed, but ran against main as it was {{count}} commit ago, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. It now conflicts with main; resolving the conflict re-runs them on the resolved commit.
checks.baseNote.passedBut.agoConflict_on.description: Tooltip of the "older main" tag on a proposal's card when its checks passed against an older state of the main line of code. "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. The proposal now conflicts with main.

checks.baseNote.passedBut.agoConflict_ot.text: The checks passed, but ran against main as it was {{count}} commits ago, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. It now conflicts with main; resolving the conflict re-runs them on the resolved commit.

"they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. The proposal still merges cleanly, so nothing holds it.

"they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. The proposal still merges cleanly, so nothing holds it.

That does not hold the merge: a proposal that still merges cleanly merges as it stands, and the platform runs the app’s tests on main again straight after.
checks.baseNote.passedBut.movedClean.description: Tooltip of the "older main" tag on a proposal's card when its checks passed against an older state of the main line of code. "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. Used when it is not known how far main has moved. The proposal still merges cleanly, so nothing holds it.

checks.phase.building.title.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note, on its card's status chip and in the "Tested" line of its page: the proposal's preview is still being built.

checks.phase.building.detail.text: The change is being built and a preview copy of the app’s data is being made.
checks.phase.building.detail.description: Tooltip of the checks status chip on a proposal's or session's card, explaining the status: the proposal's preview is still being built.

checks.phase.building.blocked.text: The change is being built and a preview copy of the app’s data is being made. Merge is blocked until all tests pass.
checks.phase.building.blocked.description: First line of the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are in progress: the proposal's preview is still being built. "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app.

checks.phase.testing.title.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note, on its card's status chip and in the "Tested" line of its page: the preview is built and the tests are running.

checks.phase.testing.detail.text: The preview is up and the automated tests are running against it.
checks.phase.testing.detail.description: Tooltip of the checks status chip on a proposal's or session's card, explaining the status: the preview is built and the tests are running.

checks.phase.testing.blocked.text: The preview is up and the automated tests are running against it. Merge is blocked until all tests pass.
checks.phase.testing.blocked.description: First line of the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are in progress: the preview is built and the tests are running. "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app.

checks.phase.queued.title.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note, on its card's status chip and in the "Tested" line of its page: the preview is built and the run waits its turn, because only a few proposals' checks run at once. "slot" is a free place to run.

checks.phase.queued.detail.text: The preview is up. Homeroom runs a few proposals’ checks at a time so they don’t slow each other down, and these start on their own when a slot frees up.
checks.phase.queued.detail.description: Tooltip of the checks status chip on a proposal's or session's card, explaining the status: the preview is built and the run waits its turn, because only a few proposals' checks run at once. "Homeroom" is the product's name; "these" are the checks.

checks.phase.queued.blocked.text: The preview is up. Homeroom runs a few proposals’ checks at a time so they don’t slow each other down, and these start on their own when a slot frees up. Merge is blocked until all tests pass.
checks.phase.queued.blocked.description: First line of the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are in progress: the preview is built and the run waits its turn, because only a few proposals' checks run at once. "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app. "Homeroom" is the product's name; "these" are the checks.

checks.phase.deferred.title.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note, on its card's status chip and in the "Tested" line of its page: the preview is built but the tests were put off because the proposal conflicts with the main line of code ("main", kept as it is).

checks.phase.deferred.detail.text: The preview is up, but the tests were not run: this proposal conflicts with main, and they would judge a tree that cannot merge. They run once it merges cleanly.
checks.phase.deferred.detail.description: Tooltip of the checks status chip on a proposal's or session's card, explaining the status: the preview is built but the tests were put off because the proposal conflicts with the main line of code ("main", kept as it is).

checks.phase.deferred.blocked.text: The preview is up, but the tests were not run: this proposal conflicts with main, and they would judge a tree that cannot merge. They run once it merges cleanly. Merge is blocked until all tests pass.
checks.phase.deferred.blocked.description: First line of the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are in progress: the preview is built but the tests were put off because the proposal conflicts with the main line of code ("main", kept as it is). "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app.

checks.phase.other.title.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note, on its card's status chip and in the "Tested" line of its page: the checks are running and the stage is not known.

checks.phase.other.detail.text: The staging build is being tested.
checks.phase.other.detail.description: Tooltip of the checks status chip on a proposal's or session's card, explaining the status: the checks are running and the stage is not known.

checks.phase.other.blocked.text: The staging build is being tested. Merge is blocked until all tests pass.
checks.phase.other.blocked.description: First line of the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are in progress: the checks are running and the stage is not known. "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app.

checks.phase.queued.titleNext.text: Waiting for a checks slot (next in line)
checks.phase.queued.titleNext.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note and on its card: the run waits its turn for a free slot and no other run is ahead of it.

checks.phase.queued.titleAhead_one.text: Waiting for a checks slot ({{count}} ahead)
checks.phase.queued.titleAhead_one.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note and on its card: the run waits its turn for a free slot. {{count}} is how many other runs are ahead of it in line.

checks.phase.queued.titleAhead_other.text: Waiting for a checks slot ({{count}} ahead)
checks.phase.queued.titleAhead_other.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note and on its card: the run waits its turn for a free slot. {{count}} is how many other runs are ahead of it in line.

checks.trigger.proposalOpen.text: Triggered by this proposal being opened.
checks.trigger.proposalOpen.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: the proposal was opened (created).

checks.trigger.commitPush.text: Triggered by a new commit on this proposal.
checks.trigger.commitPush.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: new code was added to the proposal.

checks.trigger.syncMain.text: Triggered by this proposal being updated from main.
checks.trigger.syncMain.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: the proposal was brought up to date with the main line of code ("main", kept as it is).

checks.trigger.prImport.text: Triggered by a new commit on the imported pull request.
checks.trigger.prImport.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: new code arrived on the GitHub pull request this proposal was imported from.

checks.trigger.manualRecheck.text: Triggered by someone asking for a re-run.
checks.trigger.manualRecheck.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: a person pressed "Re-run checks".

checks.trigger.promoteKick.text: Triggered by this proposal being put to a vote.
checks.trigger.promoteKick.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: the proposal was put up for a vote.

checks.trigger.bootReconcile.text: Restarted by the platform after it came back up.
checks.trigger.bootReconcile.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: the platform restarted and picked the run up again.

checks.trigger.stuckSweep.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: the platform noticed the earlier run was stuck and started it again.

checks.trigger.fleetMaintenance.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: routine maintenance of the platform.

checks.recheck.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when asking to run a proposal's automated checks again failed and the server gave no message. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

checks.recheck.failedWith.description: Toast shown when asking to run a proposal's automated checks again failed. {{error}} is the error's own message, shown as it is.

checks.recheck.unavailable.text: Re-running checks is unavailable in this preview.
checks.recheck.unavailable.description: Toast shown when "Re-run checks" is pressed inside a staging preview of Homeroom itself, where checks cannot be run.

checks.recheck.stillRunning.text: These checks are still running, so they were not started again. The result will show here when they finish.
checks.recheck.stillRunning.description: Toast shown after "Re-run checks" is pressed while a run of the same commit's checks has not finished yet.

governance.apply.closingIssue.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the request (issue) is being closed. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.closingIssueSlow.text: Closing issue, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.closingIssueSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the request (issue) is being closed. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.reopeningIssue.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on reopening a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the request (issue) is being reopened. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.reopeningIssueSlow.text: Reopening the issue, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.reopeningIssueSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on reopening a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the request (issue) is being reopened. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.envVar.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: a change to one of the app's environment variables is being applied. "env-var" is short for environment variable. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.envVarSlow.text: Applying env-var change, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.envVarSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: a change to one of the app's environment variables is being applied. "env-var" is short for environment variable. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.rename.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the app is being renamed. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.renameSlow.text: Renaming app, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.renameSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the app is being renamed. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.campaign.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: a maintenance campaign (one change rolled out to many apps) is being started. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.campaignSlow.text: Starting campaign, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.campaignSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: a maintenance campaign (one change rolled out to many apps) is being started. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.illustration.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the app's featured illustration is being replaced. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.illustrationSlow.text: Updating illustration, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.illustrationSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the app's featured illustration is being replaced. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.other.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the decision is being applied; used when the kind of proposal is not known. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.otherSlow.text: Applying, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.otherSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the decision is being applied; used when the kind of proposal is not known. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.closingIssueNumber.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the request (issue) with number {{number}} is being closed. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.closingIssueNumberSlow.text: Closing issue #{{number}}, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.closingIssueNumberSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the request (issue) with number {{number}} is being closed. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.failed.closeLabel.text: Close didn't complete. Try voting again
governance.failed.closeLabel.description: Status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) when the vote passed but closing the request failed. "Close" is a noun here: the act of closing the request.

governance.failed.label.description: Status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) when the vote passed but carrying out the decision failed.

governance.failed.titleWith.description: Tooltip of the "Didn't complete" chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request). "The apply" is a noun: carrying out the decision. {{error}} is the server's own error message.

governance.failed.title.text: The apply didn't finish. Voting again re-drives it.
governance.failed.title.description: Tooltip of the "Didn't complete" chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request), when no error message came back. "The apply" is a noun: carrying out the decision; "re-drives it" means starts it again.

governance.stalled.closeLabel.description: Status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) when closing the request has run for over a minute with no answer. "Refresh" tells the reader to reload the page.

governance.stalled.label.description: Status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) when carrying out the decision has run for over a minute with no answer. "Refresh" tells the reader to reload the page.

governance.stalled.title.text: This is taking much longer than usual. The apply may still be running on the server. Refresh to see where it landed.
governance.stalled.title.description: Tooltip of the "Still closing" / "Still applying" chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request). "The apply" is a noun: carrying out the decision.

governance.slow.title.text: Still working. GitHub can be slow to accept the close; nothing is lost while this runs.
governance.slow.title.description: Tooltip of the status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) once carrying out the decision has taken more than a few seconds. "the close" is a noun: closing the request. "GitHub" is the service's name.

governance.applying.closeTitle.text: The vote passed. The issue is being closed here and on GitHub.
governance.applying.closeTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Closing issue…" chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request). "here" is Homeroom; "GitHub" is the service's name.

governance.applying.title.text: The vote passed. This change is being applied.
governance.applying.title.description: Tooltip of the "Applying…" chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request). "This change" is the change to a setting that was voted on.

governance.pending.closeLabel.description: Status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) when the vote passed but the request has not been closed yet, some minutes later. "Close" is a noun: the closing of the request.

governance.pending.label.description: Status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) when the vote passed but the decision has not been carried out yet, some minutes later. "Apply" is a noun: the carrying out.

governance.pending.title.text: The vote passed, but the change hasn't gone through yet. The platform retries automatically.
governance.pending.title.description: Tooltip of the "Close pending" / "Apply pending" chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request).

governance.title.rename.description: Title of a governance proposal's card that asks the group to rename the app. {{name}} is the proposed new name.

governance.title.closeIssue.description: Title of a governance proposal's card that asks the group to close a request. "Close" is a verb. {{number}} is the request's number (or "?" when unknown) and {{title}} its title.

governance.title.reopenIssue.description: Title of a governance proposal's card that asks the group to reopen a closed request. "Reopen" is a verb. {{number}} is the request's number (or "?" when unknown) and {{title}} its title.

governance.meta.kind.description: First item on the small line under a governance proposal's title on its card: says what kind of thing the card is, a vote on a setting or on closing a request and not on code.

governance.meta.closedByAdminWhen.description: Item on the small line under a settled governance proposal's title: an admin closed it. {{when}} is a relative time such as "3h ago". Lower case, it follows other items.

governance.meta.closedByVoteWhen.description: Item on the small line under a settled governance proposal's title: the group's vote closed it. {{when}} is a relative time such as "3h ago". Lower case, it follows other items.

governance.meta.closedByAdmin.description: Item on the small line under a settled governance proposal's title, when the time is not known: an admin closed it. Lower case, it follows other items.

governance.meta.closedByVote.description: Item on the small line under a settled governance proposal's title, when the time is not known: the group's vote closed it. Lower case, it follows other items.

governance.vote.yes.description: Button on a governance proposal's card: votes in favour. {{tally}} is the number of Yes votes so far, sometimes with a mark such as "2✓".

governance.vote.no.description: Button on a governance proposal's card: votes against. {{tally}} is the number of No votes so far, sometimes with a mark such as "2✓".

governance.menu.adminMerge.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a governance proposal's card, shown to admins: carries out the decision now without waiting for the vote. "merge" is the verb used across Homeroom for an admin forcing a decision through.

governance.menu.adminMergeTitle.text: Admin: apply this change right now, bypassing the vote majority
governance.menu.adminMergeTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Admin merge" row in a governance proposal's ⋯ menu. "Admin:" marks it as an admin-only action.

governance.menu.viewCampaign.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a maintenance-campaign proposal's card, shown to admins: opens the campaign's dashboard. A campaign is one change rolled out to many apps.

governance.menu.viewCampaignTitle.description: Tooltip of the "View campaign" row in a governance proposal's ⋯ menu. "Open" is a verb.

governance.menu.withdraw.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a governance proposal's card, shown to the person who made it: takes the proposal back so it is no longer voted on. A verb.

governance.menu.withdrawTitle.text: Withdraw this proposal (removes it from the vote panel)
governance.menu.withdrawTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Withdraw" row in a governance proposal's ⋯ menu.

governance.card.openTitle.description: Tooltip of a governance proposal's card in the Workshop list; pressing the card opens its page. "Open" is a verb.

governance.closes.title.description: Small heading inside About this proposal on a proposal to close a request, over the closed request's title, who asked and its words.

governance.roster.yes_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a governance proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.
