governance.roster.yes_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a governance proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

governance.roster.no_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a governance proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

governance.roster.no_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a governance proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

governance.withdraw.title.description: Title of the dialog confirming that the person wants to take back a governance proposal they made.

governance.withdraw.message.text: This removes it from the vote panel and stops the vote. You can propose it again later.
governance.withdraw.message.description: Body of the dialog confirming the withdrawal of a governance proposal.

governance.withdraw.confirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog that withdraws a governance proposal. A verb.

governance.withdraw.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when withdrawing a governance proposal failed and the server gave no message. "Withdraw" is a noun here: the withdrawal. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

governance.withdraw.failedWith.description: Toast shown when withdrawing a governance proposal failed. "Withdraw" is a noun here: the withdrawal. {{error}} is the error's own message.

vote.roster.yes.all_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

vote.roster.yes.all_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

vote.roster.yes.approvers_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{count}} is how many approvers voted this way, and the check mark means "approver". Keep the check mark.

vote.roster.yes.approvers_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{count}} is how many approvers voted this way, and the check mark means "approver". Keep the check mark.

vote.roster.yes.approversAdvisory_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{approvers}} is how many approvers voted this way (the check mark means "approver", keep it) and {{count}} how many other people did, whose votes are advisory and do not count.

vote.roster.yes.approversAdvisory_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{approvers}} is how many approvers voted this way (the check mark means "approver", keep it) and {{count}} how many other people did, whose votes are advisory and do not count.

vote.roster.no.all_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

vote.roster.no.all_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

vote.roster.no.approvers_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{count}} is how many approvers voted this way, and the check mark means "approver". Keep the check mark.

vote.roster.no.approvers_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{count}} is how many approvers voted this way, and the check mark means "approver". Keep the check mark.

vote.roster.no.approversAdvisory_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{approvers}} is how many approvers voted this way (the check mark means "approver", keep it) and {{count}} how many other people did, whose votes are advisory and do not count.

vote.roster.no.approversAdvisory_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{approvers}} is how many approvers voted this way (the check mark means "approver", keep it) and {{count}} how many other people did, whose votes are advisory and do not count.

vote.roster.earlier.yes_one.text: Earlier version: {{yes}} said yes. Not counted until they take another look.
vote.roster.earlier.yes_one.description: Line under the list of voters on a proposal's page, about people who voted before the proposal was changed. Their votes are set aside until they vote again on the new version. {{count}} is how many such people there are in all. {{yes}} lists them by @username.

vote.roster.earlier.yes_other.text: Earlier version: {{yes}} said yes. Not counted until they take another look.
vote.roster.earlier.yes_other.description: Line under the list of voters on a proposal's page, about people who voted before the proposal was changed. Their votes are set aside until they vote again on the new version. {{count}} is how many such people there are in all. {{yes}} lists them by @username.

vote.roster.earlier.no_one.text: Earlier version: {{no}} said no. Not counted until they take another look.
vote.roster.earlier.no_one.description: Line under the list of voters on a proposal's page, about people who voted before the proposal was changed. Their votes are set aside until they vote again on the new version. {{count}} is how many such people there are in all. {{no}} lists them by @username.

vote.roster.earlier.no_other.text: Earlier version: {{no}} said no. Not counted until they take another look.
vote.roster.earlier.no_other.description: Line under the list of voters on a proposal's page, about people who voted before the proposal was changed. Their votes are set aside until they vote again on the new version. {{count}} is how many such people there are in all. {{no}} lists them by @username.

vote.roster.earlier.both_one.text: Earlier version: {{yes}} said yes; {{no}} said no. Not counted until they take another look.
vote.roster.earlier.both_one.description: Line under the list of voters on a proposal's page, about people who voted before the proposal was changed. Their votes are set aside until they vote again on the new version. {{count}} is how many such people there are in all. {{yes}} lists by @username those who had voted Yes and {{no}} those who had voted No.

vote.roster.earlier.both_other.text: Earlier version: {{yes}} said yes; {{no}} said no. Not counted until they take another look.
vote.roster.earlier.both_other.description: Line under the list of voters on a proposal's page, about people who voted before the proposal was changed. Their votes are set aside until they vote again on the new version. {{count}} is how many such people there are in all. {{yes}} lists by @username those who had voted Yes and {{no}} those who had voted No.

proposal.askApproval.sharing.description: Label of the "Ask for approval" button on an imported pull request's card while the request to put it up for a vote is being sent.

proposal.askApproval.failedHttp.text: Could not ask for approval on this change (HTTP {{status}}).
proposal.askApproval.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when putting an imported change up for a vote failed and the server gave no message. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

proposal.askApproval.failedWith.text: Could not ask for approval on this change: {{error}}
proposal.askApproval.failedWith.description: Toast shown when putting an imported change up for a vote failed. {{error}} is the error's own message.

proposal.withdraw.title.description: Title of the dialog confirming that the person wants to take back their own proposal (a change put up for a vote).

proposal.withdraw.message.text: This closes PR {{number}} and removes it from the vote panel. You can propose it again later.
proposal.withdraw.message.description: Body of the dialog confirming the withdrawal of a proposal. "PR" is a GitHub pull request; {{number}} is its number.

proposal.withdraw.confirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog that withdraws the person's own proposal. A verb.

proposal.withdraw.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when withdrawing a proposal failed and the server gave no message. "Withdraw" is a noun here: the withdrawal. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

proposal.withdraw.failedWith.description: Toast shown when withdrawing a proposal failed. "Withdraw" is a noun here: the withdrawal. {{error}} is the error's own message.

proposal.moveBack.title.description: Title of the dialog confirming that the person wants to take their own proposal out of the vote and keep working on it. "Underway" is the name of the board column for changes still being worked on.

proposal.moveBack.message.text: This takes PR {{number}} out of review so you can keep working on it. Its votes are cleared and it cannot be merged until you propose it again. The pull request stays open.
proposal.moveBack.message.description: Body of the dialog confirming that a proposal goes back to Underway. "PR" is a GitHub pull request; {{number}} is its number.

proposal.moveBack.confirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog that takes a proposal out of the vote and back to the Underway column.

proposal.moveBack.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when taking a proposal back to Underway failed and the server gave no message. "it" is the proposal. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

proposal.moveBack.failedWith.description: Toast shown when taking a proposal back to Underway failed. "it" is the proposal. {{error}} is the error's own message.

attributes.priority.high.description: One of the three priorities people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's priority chip (after a flag glyph) and as an option in the priority picker. The most urgent.

attributes.priority.medium.description: One of the three priorities people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's priority chip (after a flag glyph) and as an option in the priority picker. The middle one.

attributes.priority.low.description: One of the three priorities people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's priority chip (after a flag glyph) and as an option in the priority picker. The least urgent.

attributes.category.feature.description: One of the six built-in categories of work people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's category chip, in the category picker and in the board's category filter. Something new the app would do.

attributes.category.bug.description: One of the six built-in categories of work people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's category chip, in the category picker and in the board's category filter. Something that is broken.

attributes.category.improvement.description: One of the six built-in categories of work people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's category chip, in the category picker and in the board's category filter. Making something that exists better.

attributes.category.design.description: One of the six built-in categories of work people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's category chip, in the category picker and in the board's category filter. How the app looks and feels.

attributes.category.docs.description: One of the six built-in categories of work people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's category chip, in the category picker and in the board's category filter. Documentation; short for "documents".

attributes.category.chore.description: One of the six built-in categories of work people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's category chip, in the category picker and in the board's category filter. Routine upkeep that changes nothing people see.

attributes.chip.setPriority.description: Chip on a request's or proposal's page, after a flag glyph, when nobody has voted a priority for it yet; pressing it opens the priority picker.

attributes.chip.setCategory.description: Chip on a request's or proposal's page when it has no category yet; pressing it opens the category picker.

attributes.chip.unassigned.description: Chip on a request's or proposal's page when nobody has been suggested to take the work; pressing it opens the picker of people.

attributes.chip.priorityTitle.description: Tooltip of the priority chip on a request's or proposal's card.

attributes.chip.categoryTitle.description: Tooltip of the category chip on a request's or proposal's card.

attributes.chip.categoryPlacedTitle.text: Placed automatically. Tap to vote for a different category
attributes.chip.categoryPlacedTitle.description: Tooltip of the category chip on a card whose category was chosen by Homeroom's AI and not by a vote.

attributes.chip.assigneeTitle.text: Suggest or vote on who should take this
attributes.chip.assigneeTitle.description: Tooltip of the chip that shows who a request or proposal is assigned to. "take this" means take on the work.

attributes.chip.assignTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Unassigned" chip on a request's or proposal's page.

attributes.menu.setPriority.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's or proposal's card: opens the picker of priorities. Shown when the card has no priority yet. Keep the ellipsis.

attributes.menu.changePriority.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's or proposal's card: opens the picker of priorities. Shown when the card already has one. "Change" is a verb. Keep the ellipsis.

attributes.menu.priorityTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Set priority…" / "Change priority…" row in a card's ⋯ menu.

attributes.menu.setCategory.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's or proposal's card: opens the picker of categories. Shown when the card has no category yet. Keep the ellipsis.

attributes.menu.changeCategory.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's or proposal's card: opens the picker of categories. Shown when the card already has one. "Change" is a verb. Keep the ellipsis.

attributes.menu.categoryTitle.text: Vote on which category this card belongs to
attributes.menu.categoryTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Set category…" / "Change category…" row in a card's ⋯ menu.

attributes.menu.assign.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's or proposal's card: opens the picker of people. Shown when nobody is assigned to the work yet. Keep the ellipsis.

attributes.menu.changeAssignee.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's or proposal's card: opens the picker of people. Shown when somebody is already assigned. "Change" is a verb; the assignee is the person who takes the work. Keep the ellipsis.

attributes.menu.assigneeTitle.text: Suggest or vote on who should take this
attributes.menu.assigneeTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Assign someone…" / "Change assignee…" row in a card's ⋯ menu. "take this" means take on the work.

attributes.picker.priorityHead.description: Heading of the small picker that opens from a card's priority chip, above the three priorities to vote for.

attributes.picker.categoryHead.description: Heading of the small picker that opens from a card's category chip, above the built-in categories to vote for.

attributes.picker.customHead.description: Heading in the category picker above the categories this project's members typed themselves, under the built-in ones.

attributes.picker.categoryPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the text box at the bottom of the category picker, where a person types a new category name.

attributes.picker.assigneeHead.description: Heading of the small picker that opens from a card's assignee chip, above the people suggested for the work.

attributes.picker.noSuggestions.description: Line in the assignee picker when nobody has been suggested for the work yet.

attributes.picker.namePlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the text box at the bottom of the assignee picker, where a person types a username.

attributes.vote.saveFailed.description: Toast shown when a vote for a card's priority, category or assignee could not be saved and the server gave no message.

attributes.vote.saveFailedWith.description: Toast shown when a vote for a card's priority, category or assignee could not be saved. {{error}} is the error's own message.

attributes.vote.removeFailed.description: Toast shown when taking back a vote for a card's priority, category or assignee failed and the server gave no message.

attributes.vote.removeFailedWith.description: Toast shown when taking back a vote for a card's priority, category or assignee failed. {{error}} is the error's own message.

proposal.undo.title.description: Title of the dialog confirming that the person wants to undo a change that is already merged and live.

proposal.undo.message.text:
This opens a revert PR that backs out this merged change.

It still needs a merge vote to land. Undoing is a proposal the group votes on, just like any other change.
proposal.undo.message.description: Body of the dialog confirming an undo of a merged change, two paragraphs: keep the blank line between them. "revert PR" is a GitHub pull request that reverses the change; "to land" means to be merged.

proposal.undo.confirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog that undoes a merged change. "Open" is a verb: create the pull request that reverses the change.

proposal.undo.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when undoing a merged change failed and the server gave no message. "Undo" is a noun here. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

proposal.undo.failedWith.description: Toast shown when undoing a merged change failed. "Undo" is a noun here. {{error}} is the error's own message.

governance.adminApply.closeTitleNumber.description: Title of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote; the proposal is to close a request. "Close" is a verb. {{number}} is the request's number.

governance.adminApply.closeTitle.description: Title of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote; the proposal is to close a request whose number is not known. "Close" is a verb.

governance.adminApply.campaignTitle.description: Title of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote; the proposal is a maintenance campaign, one change rolled out to many apps.

governance.adminApply.illustrationTitle.description: Title of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote; the proposal replaces the app's featured illustration.

governance.adminApply.envVarTitle.description: Title of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote; the proposal changes one of the app's environment variables ("env-var").

governance.adminApply.closeMessage.text:
This bypasses the active-user vote majority and closes the issue right now, here and on GitHub.

Use only when you're confident the change should ship. The override is announced in group chat with your username.
governance.adminApply.closeMessage.description: Body of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, two paragraphs (keep the blank line); the proposal is to close a request. "here" is Homeroom; "GitHub" is the service's name; "should ship" means should take effect.

governance.adminApply.campaignMessage.text:
This bypasses the platform vote and starts the campaign right now: an AI will open one maintenance PR per app across the fleet.

Use only when you're confident the change should ship. The override is announced in group chat with your username.
governance.adminApply.campaignMessage.description: Body of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, two paragraphs (keep the blank line); the proposal is a maintenance campaign. "PR" is a pull request; "the fleet" is all the apps on the platform.

governance.adminApply.illustrationMessag.text:
This bypasses the active-user vote majority and changes the featured illustration on Discover right now.

Use only when you're confident the change should ship. The override is announced in group chat with your username.
governance.adminApply.illustrationMessag.description: Body of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, two paragraphs (keep the blank line); the proposal replaces the app's featured illustration. "Discover" is the name of the screen where apps are found.

governance.adminApply.envVarMessage.text:
This bypasses the active-user vote majority and applies the proposed secret change right now (the app redeploys with the new value).

Use only when you're confident the change should ship. The override is announced in group chat with your username.
governance.adminApply.envVarMessage.description: Body of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, two paragraphs (keep the blank line); the proposal changes a secret environment variable of the app.

governance.adminApply.closeConfirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, for a proposal to close a request. "Close" is a verb: close the request.

governance.adminApply.campaignConfirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, for a maintenance campaign: starts the campaign.

governance.adminApply.applyConfirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, for a change to a setting or illustration: applies the change.

governance.adminApply.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when an admin's attempt to carry out a governance proposal at once failed and the server gave no message. "Admin apply" is a noun: the admin's forced apply. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

governance.adminApply.failedWith.description: Toast shown when an admin's attempt to carry out a governance proposal at once failed. "Admin apply" is a noun. {{error}} is the error's own message.

issue.card.kudosTitle.description: Tooltip of the star and number on a request's card: how many kudos (the platform's thanks points) people have promised to whoever makes the request happen.

issue.card.autoTitlePending.description: Item on the small line under a request's title on its card: the title shown is a stand-in and an AI-written one is on its way. Lower case, it follows other items.

issue.card.icon.generating.text: A proposal is being generated for this issue
issue.card.icon.generating.description: Tooltip of the pulsing icon on a request's card while an AI drafts a proposal (a change to vote on) for it.

issue.card.icon.mine.text: You have a session for this issue. Go to it.
issue.card.icon.mine.description: Tooltip of the icon on a request's card when the viewer already has a working session started from it.

issue.card.icon.ready.text: Proposal ready. Review it to start a session
issue.card.icon.ready.description: Tooltip of the icon on a request's card when an AI-drafted proposal for it is ready to look at.

issue.card.closing.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a request's card once the vote to close it has passed and it is being closed. Keep the ellipsis.

issue.card.closeProposed.description: Status chip on a request's card while a proposal to close it is being voted on. "Close" is a noun: closing the request has been proposed.

issue.card.closeProposedTitle.text: Closing this request is waiting for approval
issue.card.closeProposedTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Close proposed" chip on a request's card.

issue.card.closed.description: Status chip on the card of a request that is closed (finished or dismissed). Describes the request.

issue.card.closedWhen.description: Tooltip of the "Closed" chip on a request's card. {{when}} is a relative time such as "3 days ago".

issue.card.closedTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Closed" chip on a request's card when the time it was closed is not known.

issue.card.openTitle.description: Tooltip of a request's card in the Workshop list; pressing the card opens the request's page. "Open" is a verb.

issue.action.seeProgress.description: Main button on a request's card in the Workshop list, shown to the person Homeroom bot is building the request for: opens the request's page at the bot's progress card.

issue.action.seePlan.description: Main button on a request's card in the Workshop list while Homeroom bot's plan for it waits for Build it: opens the request's page at the plan, where its Build it button is. Any member may press Build it there.

issue.action.seePlanTitle.text: Open the plan on this request, where you can build it
issue.action.seePlanTitle.description: Tooltip of the "See the plan" button on a request's card in the Workshop list.

issue.action.seeProgressTitle.text: Open this request, where its progress is
issue.action.seeProgressTitle.description: Tooltip of the "See progress" button on a request's card in the Workshop list. "Open" is a verb.

issue.action.botOnIt.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): disabled, shown to other people while the request waits in Homeroom bot's queue. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's builder bot; "is on it" means it has taken the job.

issue.action.botHeld.description: Main button on a request's card: disabled, shown while Homeroom bot waits to build the request because it already has as many changes up for a vote on this project as it may.

issue.action.botHeldTitle.text: Homeroom bot starts when one of its changes here is voted in or closed
issue.action.botHeldTitle.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Homeroom bot will build this" button on a request's card. "Here" is the project.

issue.action.botReading.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): disabled, shown while Homeroom bot is reading the request before building. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's builder bot. Keep the ellipsis.

issue.action.botBuilding.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): disabled, shown while Homeroom bot is building what the request asks for. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's builder bot. Keep the ellipsis.

issue.action.botReadingTitle.text: The Homeroom bot is reading this request now
issue.action.botReadingTitle.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Homeroom bot is reading…" button on a request's card.

issue.action.botBuildingTitle.text: The Homeroom bot is building this request now
issue.action.botBuildingTitle.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Homeroom bot is on it" / "Homeroom bot is building…" button on a request's card.

issue.action.generating.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): disabled, shown while an automatic AI run drafts a change (to vote on) for the request. Keep the ellipsis.

issue.action.generatingTitle.text: A headless AI session is working on this request
issue.action.generatingTitle.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Drafting a change…" button on a request's card. "headless" means the AI session runs on its own with nobody chatting with it.

issue.action.generatingTitleBy.text: A headless AI session is working on this request (started by {{username}})
issue.action.generatingTitleBy.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Drafting a change…" button on a request's card. "headless" means the AI session runs on its own. {{username}} is the person who started it.

issue.action.goToSession.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): opens the working session the viewer already started from this request's AI-drafted proposal.

issue.action.goToSessionTitle.text: You already started a session from this request. Open it
issue.action.goToSessionTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Go to session" button on a request's card. "Open it" is an instruction.

issue.action.answer.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): shown when an automatic AI run stopped to ask a question; opens the place to answer it, after which the run tries again.

issue.action.answerMineTitle.text: Your auto-solve run is waiting on an answer. Open its session to read the question and reply
issue.action.answerMineTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Answer & regenerate" button on a request's card, for the person who started the run. An auto-solve run is an automatic AI attempt at the request. "Open" is a verb.

issue.action.answerOthersTitle.text: This auto-solve run has a question. Answer it on this request
issue.action.answerOthersTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Answer & regenerate" button on a request's card, for people who did not start the run. An auto-solve run is an automatic AI attempt at the request.

issue.action.startWork.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): starts a working session with an AI agent on the request.

issue.action.runFinished.spec.text: An auto-solve run finished here (it drafted a plan). Start an agent session on this request
issue.action.runFinished.spec.description: Tooltip of the "Start work" button on a request's card after an automatic AI run (an auto-solve run) finished on it; the words in parentheses say what the run produced: a written plan.

issue.action.runFinished.code.text: An auto-solve run finished here (it pushed a code change). Start an agent session on this request
issue.action.runFinished.code.description: Tooltip of the "Start work" button on a request's card after an automatic AI run (an auto-solve run) finished on it; the words in parentheses say what the run produced: a code change.

issue.action.runFinished.specCode.text: An auto-solve run finished here (it drafted a plan and pushed a code change). Start an agent session on this request
issue.action.runFinished.specCode.description: Tooltip of the "Start work" button on a request's card after an automatic AI run (an auto-solve run) finished on it; the words in parentheses say what the run produced: a written plan and a code change.

issue.action.runFinished.other.text: An auto-solve run finished here (it finished a run). Start an agent session on this request
issue.action.runFinished.other.description: Tooltip of the "Start work" button on a request's card after an automatic AI run (an auto-solve run) finished on it; the words in parentheses say what the run produced: nothing more specific is known.

issue.action.askBot.text: Ask Homeroom bot to build this
issue.action.askBot.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): asks the platform's builder bot, named Homeroom bot, to build what the request asks for.

issue.action.startMore.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): shown when the viewer already has a session on this request; starts another one.

issue.action.startMoreTitle.text: Start another agent session on this request
issue.action.startMoreTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Start more work" button on a request's card. An agent session is a working conversation with an AI coding agent.

issue.action.workWithBot.text: Work on this with Homeroom bot
issue.action.workWithBot.description: Main button on a request's card and page (a request is a filed issue), where nobody is building it yet: opens a thread only the viewer can see, in their chat with Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant), about this request, to talk it through and plan it. "Work on" is a verb.

issue.action.workWithBotTitle.text: Talk it through and plan it with Homeroom bot, in a thread only you can see
issue.action.workWithBotTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Work on this with Homeroom bot" button on a request's card and page. Homeroom bot is the platform's assistant.

issue.action.letBotBuild.text: Let the bot build it now
issue.action.letBotBuild.description: Main button on a request's card and page while Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) waits for the viewer's plan, because they are working on their own request with it in a private thread: tells the bot to go ahead without a plan. "Build" is a verb.

issue.action.letBotBuildTitle.text: Homeroom bot starts on it without waiting for your plan
issue.action.letBotBuildTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Let the bot build it now" button on a request's card and page. Homeroom bot is the platform's assistant.

issue.action.stopWorking.description: Second button on a request's card in the Workshop list, shown to someone who said they are working on it: takes their name off it.

issue.action.stopWorkingTitle.text: Stop working on this so somebody else can pick it up
issue.action.stopWorkingTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Stop working on this" button on a request's card.

issue.action.claim.description: Second button on a request's card in the Workshop list: tells everyone the viewer will work on the request. "It" is the request.

issue.action.claimTitle.text: Let everyone know you'll work on this. It's not a promise of progress. It clears itself after about 7 days with no activity; talking about it in the request's thread keeps it going.
issue.action.claimTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Claim it" button on a request's card. "It" is the mark that says the viewer is working on the request.

issue.bot.hint_one.text: Usually ready to try in about {{count}} minutes.
issue.bot.hint_one.description: Line under (and tooltip of) the "Ask Homeroom bot to build this" button on a request: how long the bot usually takes before there is something to try. {{count}} is a number of minutes.

issue.bot.hint_other.text: Usually ready to try in about {{count}} minutes.
issue.bot.hint_other.description: Line under (and tooltip of) the "Ask Homeroom bot to build this" button on a request: how long the bot usually takes before there is something to try. {{count}} is a number of minutes.

issue.bot.askFailedHttp.text: Couldn't ask Homeroom bot just now (HTTP {{status}}).
issue.bot.askFailedHttp.description: Toast shown when asking Homeroom bot to build a request failed and the server gave no message. "Homeroom bot" is the bot's name. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

issue.bot.askFailedWith.text: Couldn't ask Homeroom bot just now: {{error}}
issue.bot.askFailedWith.description: Toast shown when asking Homeroom bot to build a request failed. "Homeroom bot" is the bot's name. {{error}} is the error's own message.

issue.bot.threadFailed.text: The thread with Homeroom bot could not be started just now. Try again in a minute.
issue.bot.threadFailed.description: Toast when "Work on this with Homeroom bot" on a request could not open its private thread with Homeroom bot, the platform's assistant.

issue.bot.letBuildDone.text: Homeroom bot no longer waits for your plan.
issue.bot.letBuildDone.description: Toast after "Let the bot build it now" on a request: Homeroom bot, the platform's assistant, may now pick the request up without a plan.

issue.bot.letBuildFailed.text: That did not go through. Try again in a minute.
issue.bot.letBuildFailed.description: Toast when "Let the bot build it now" on a request failed.

issue.bot.onItMine.text: Homeroom bot is on it. Its card is in your chat with it.
issue.bot.onItMine.description: Toast shown after the viewer asked Homeroom bot to build a request for them. "is on it" means it has taken the job; "Its card" is the request's card, and "it" at the end is the bot.

issue.bot.onIt.description: Toast shown after Homeroom bot was asked to build a request. "is on it" means it has taken the job.

issue.menu.startMore.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: starts another working session on the request after an automatic AI run finished on it.

issue.menu.buildNow.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: starts a session where the viewer builds the request with an AI coding agent, instead of asking Homeroom bot. "Build" is a verb.

issue.menu.buildInSession.text: Build it in an agent session
issue.menu.buildInSession.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: starts a session where the viewer builds the request with an AI coding agent, instead of working on it with Homeroom bot. An agent session is a working conversation with an AI coding agent. "Build" is a verb.

issue.menu.alreadyBountied.text: You already placed a bounty on this issue
issue.menu.alreadyBountied.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Bountied" row in a request's ⋯ menu. A bounty is kudos (thanks points) promised to whoever makes the request happen.

issue.menu.allowanceSpent.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Pledge kudos" row in a request's ⋯ menu, when the viewer has no kudos left to promise this week.

issue.menu.bountied.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: disabled, shown when the viewer has already promised kudos on this request.

issue.menu.pledgeKudos.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: promises kudos (thanks points) to whoever makes the request happen. "Pledge" is a verb.

issue.menu.pledgeKudosTitle.text: Pledge kudos to whoever’s change makes this happen
issue.menu.pledgeKudosTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Pledge kudos" row in a request's ⋯ menu. "change" is a noun: the change that fulfils the request.

issue.menu.stopWorking.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: shown to someone who said they are working on the request; takes their name off it.

issue.menu.stopWorkingTitle.text: Stop working on this so somebody else can pick it up
issue.menu.stopWorkingTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Stop working on this" row in a request's ⋯ menu.

issue.menu.claim.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: tells everyone the viewer will work on the request. "It" is the request.

issue.menu.claimTitle.text: Let everyone know you’ll work on this. It’s not a promise of progress. It clears itself after about 7 days with no activity; talking about it in the request’s thread keeps it going.
issue.menu.claimTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Claim it" row in a request's ⋯ menu. "It" is the mark that says the viewer is working on the request.

issue.menu.closing.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: disabled, shown once the vote to close the request has passed and it is being closed. Keep the ellipsis.

issue.menu.closeProposed.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: disabled, shown while a proposal to close the request is being voted on. "Close" is a noun: closing has been proposed.

issue.menu.closeProposedTitle.text: Closing this request is waiting for approval
issue.menu.closeProposedTitle.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Close proposed" row in a request's ⋯ menu.

issue.menu.proposeReopen.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a closed request's card: opens the dialog that asks the group to vote on reopening the request.

issue.menu.proposeReopenTitle.text: Ask the group to reopen this request. If they approve, it's open again
issue.menu.proposeReopenTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Propose reopening" row in a closed request's ⋯ menu.

issue.menu.reopenProposed.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a closed request's card: disabled, shown while a proposal to reopen the request is being voted on.

issue.menu.reopenProposedTitle.text: Reopening this request is waiting for approval
issue.menu.reopenProposedTitle.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Reopen proposed" row in a closed request's ⋯ menu.

issue.menu.proposeClose.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: opens the dialog that asks the group to vote on closing the request.

issue.menu.proposeCloseTitle.text: Ask the group to close this request. If they approve, it's closed
issue.menu.proposeCloseTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Propose to close" row in a request's ⋯ menu.

issue.menu.share.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: opens the picker of chats and discussions to send a link to this request to. "Share" is a verb. Keep the ellipsis.

issue.menu.shareTitle.text: Share this request to a chat or a discussion
issue.menu.shareTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Share to…" row in a request's ⋯ menu.

issue.menu.openOnGithub.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: opens the request's issue page on GitHub in a new tab. "Open" is a verb; "GitHub" is the service's name.

issue.title.updateFailed.description: Error line under the box where a request's author edits its title, when saving failed and the server gave no message.

issue.title.networkError.description: Error line under the box where a request's author edits its title, when the save could not reach the server.

proposal.title.updateFailed.description: Error line under the box where a change's author edits its title on the change's page, when saving failed and the server gave no message.

proposal.title.networkError.description: Error line under the box where a change's author edits its title on the change's page, when the save could not reach the server.

proposal.merged.fallbackTitle.description: Title of the card of a merged change in the Workshop's completed list when the change has no title. "Change" is a noun. {{username}} is its author.

proposal.merged.prTitle.description: Tooltip of the title on the card of a merged change in the Workshop's completed list when the change has no title: its GitHub pull request, abbreviated "PR". {{number}} is the pull request's number.

proposal.merged.revertTitle.text: This PR is itself a revert
proposal.merged.revertTitle.description: Tooltip of the "↩ revert" mark on the card of a merged change in the Workshop's completed list: this change undoes an earlier one. "PR" is a GitHub pull request.

proposal.merged.revert.description: Mark on the small line of the card of a merged change in the Workshop's completed list when the change itself undoes an earlier change. A noun, lower case; keep the arrow.

proposal.merged.undoneBy.description: Link on the small line of the card of a merged change in the Workshop's completed list: a later change, pull request {{number}}, reversed this one and is merged. Keep "PR#" joined to the number.

proposal.merged.revertMerging.description: Link on the small line of the card of a merged change in the Workshop's completed list: the change that reverses this one, pull request {{number}}, is being merged right now. "Revert" is a noun. Keep "PR#" joined to the number.

proposal.merged.revertInVote.description: Link on the small line of the card of a merged change in the Workshop's completed list: the change that reverses this one, pull request {{number}}, is being voted on. "Revert" is a noun. Keep "PR#" joined to the number.

proposal.merged.openTitle.description: Tooltip of the card of a merged change in the Workshop's completed list; pressing the card opens the change's page. "Open" is a verb.

governance.done.title.description: Title of the card, in the Workshop's completed list, of a governance proposal that closed a request. "Close" is a verb. {{number}} is the request's number and {{title}} its title.

governance.done.fallbackTitle.description: Title of the card, in the Workshop's completed list, of a governance proposal that closed a request when neither the request's number nor a title is known. "Close" is a verb.

governance.done.closedByAdmin.description: Item on the small line of the card, in the Workshop's completed list, of a governance proposal that closed a request, when the time is not known: an admin closed the request. Lower case, it follows other items.

governance.done.closedByVote.description: Item on the small line of the card, in the Workshop's completed list, of a governance proposal that closed a request, when the time is not known: the group's vote closed the request. Lower case, it follows other items.

governance.done.closedByAdminWhen.description: Item on the small line of the card, in the Workshop's completed list, of a governance proposal that closed a request: an admin closed the request. {{when}} is a relative time such as "3d ago". Lower case, it follows other items.

governance.done.closedByVoteWhen.description: Item on the small line of the card, in the Workshop's completed list, of a governance proposal that closed a request: the group's vote closed the request. {{when}} is a relative time such as "3d ago". Lower case, it follows other items.

governance.done.kind.description: First item on the small line of the card, in the Workshop's completed list, of a governance proposal that closed a request: says what kind of thing the card is, the closing of a request. "close" is a noun.

governance.done.openTitle.description: Tooltip of the card, in the Workshop's completed list, of a governance proposal that closed a request; pressing the card opens the proposal's page. "Open" is a verb.

issue.bounty.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when promising kudos on a request (a bounty) failed and the server gave no message. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

issue.bounty.failedWith.description: Toast shown when promising kudos on a request (a bounty) failed. {{error}} is the error's own message.

issue.claim.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when "Claim it" on a request failed and the server gave no message. "pick this up" means take on the request. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

issue.claim.failedWith.description: Toast shown when "Claim it" on a request failed. "pick this up" means take on the request. {{error}} is the error's own message.

issue.claim.you.description: Stands in for the viewer's username in the list of people working on a request, in the rare case their account is not loaded. Lower case.

issue.claim.clearFailedHttp.description: Toast shown when "Stop working on this" on a request failed and the server gave no message. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

issue.claim.clearFailedWith.description: Toast shown when "Stop working on this" on a request failed. {{error}} is the error's own message.

issue.autoRun.setupLoading.text: Coding-agent setup is still loading. Try again.
issue.autoRun.setupLoading.description: Toast shown when an automatic AI run that drafts a proposal for a request ("Generate proposal") was asked for before the page finished loading the viewer's coding-agent settings.

issue.autoRun.openRouterModelsFailed.description: Toast shown before an automatic AI run that drafts a proposal for a request ("Generate proposal") when the list of AI models from OpenRouter (a service's name) could not be loaded and the server gave no message.

issue.autoRun.modelListFailed.text: Could not load the model list.
issue.autoRun.modelListFailed.description: Toast shown before an automatic AI run that drafts a proposal for a request ("Generate proposal") when the list of AI models could not be loaded and the server gave no message.

issue.autoRun.modelListRetry.text: Couldn't load the model list. Try again.
issue.autoRun.modelListRetry.description: Toast shown before an automatic AI run that drafts a proposal for a request ("Generate proposal") when loading the list of AI models failed with no message at all.

issue.autoRun.noOpenRouterModels.text: No OpenRouter models are available under your key.
issue.autoRun.noOpenRouterModels.description: Toast shown before an automatic AI run that drafts a proposal for a request ("Generate proposal") when the viewer's OpenRouter key gives access to no AI model. "OpenRouter" is a service's name; "key" is an API key.

issue.autoRun.noModels.text: Couldn't load the model list. Try again.
issue.autoRun.noModels.description: Toast shown before an automatic AI run that drafts a proposal for a request ("Generate proposal") when the list of AI models came back empty.

issue.autoRun.openRouterStartFailed.text: The OpenRouter run could not start.
issue.autoRun.openRouterStartFailed.description: Toast shown when an automatic AI run that drafts a proposal for a request ("Generate proposal") could not start on the viewer's OpenRouter budget and the server gave no message. "run" is a noun.

issue.autoRun.startFailedHttp.description: Toast shown when an automatic AI run that drafts a proposal for a request ("Generate proposal") could not be started and the server gave no message. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

issue.autoRun.startFailedWith.description: Toast shown when an automatic AI run that drafts a proposal for a request ("Generate proposal") could not be started. {{error}} is the error's own message.

issue.autoRun.outOfCredits.text: You're out of free AI credits.
issue.autoRun.outOfCredits.description: Toast shown when an automatic AI run that drafts a proposal for a request ("Generate proposal") was refused because the viewer has used up the week's free AI allowance, and no fuller message came back.

issue.autoRun.model.free.description: Line under a model's name in the list of AI models to choose from in the "Generate proposal" dialog: using this model costs nothing.

issue.autoRun.model.low.description: Line under a model's name in the list of AI models to choose from in the "Generate proposal" dialog: this model is cheap to use.

issue.autoRun.model.medium.description: Line under a model's name in the list of AI models to choose from in the "Generate proposal" dialog: this model has a middling price.

issue.autoRun.model.high.description: Line under a model's name in the list of AI models to choose from in the "Generate proposal" dialog: this model is expensive to use.

issue.autoRun.model.recommendedFree.description: Line under a model's name in the list of AI models to choose from in the "Generate proposal" dialog: Homeroom recommends this model, and using it costs nothing.

issue.autoRun.model.recommendedLow.description: Line under a model's name in the list of AI models to choose from in the "Generate proposal" dialog: Homeroom recommends this model, and it is cheap to use.

issue.autoRun.model.recommendedMedium.description: Line under a model's name in the list of AI models to choose from in the "Generate proposal" dialog: Homeroom recommends this model, and it has a middling price.

issue.autoRun.model.recommendedHigh.description: Line under a model's name in the list of AI models to choose from in the "Generate proposal" dialog: Homeroom recommends this model, and it is expensive to use.

issue.autoRun.model.recommended.description: Line under a model's name in the list of AI models to choose from in the "Generate proposal" dialog: Homeroom recommends this model; its price is not known.

issue.autoRun.model.openRouter.description: Line under a model's name in the list of AI models to choose from in the "Generate proposal" dialog: nothing more is known about it than that it can be used through OpenRouter (a service's name).

issue.autoRun.model.available.description: Line under a model's name in the list of AI models to choose from in the "Generate proposal" dialog: nothing more is known about it than that it can be used.

issue.autoRun.billing.included.description: Note in the "Generate proposal" dialog saying what the run is paid from: the OpenRouter credits that come with the viewer's Homeroom account. "OpenRouter" is a service's name.

issue.autoRun.billing.openRouter.description: Note in the "Generate proposal" dialog saying what the run is paid from: the viewer's own OpenRouter account. "OpenRouter" is a service's name.

issue.autoRun.billing.homeroom.description: Note in the "Generate proposal" dialog saying what the run is paid from: the viewer's AI credits on Homeroom (the product's name).

issue.autoRun.intro.text: Homeroom will inspect the issue and repository, then create a proposal for review.
issue.autoRun.intro.description: First line of the "Generate proposal" dialog on a request: what the automatic AI run will do. "Homeroom" is the product's name; "the issue" is the request.

badge.reason.conflictFailed.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the platform tried to resolve the proposal's merge conflict by itself and failed, so a person has to.

badge.reason.conflictFailed.detail.text: The last automatic conflict resolution failed. {{remedy}}
badge.reason.conflictFailed.detail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the automatic attempt to resolve the merge conflict failed. {{remedy}} is one or more complete sentences saying who has to do what next.

badge.reason.mergeRefused.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: everything passed and the platform tried to merge the proposal, but GitHub (the service's name) would not.

badge.reason.mergeRefused.detail.text: This proposal passed every gate and the platform tried to merge it, but GitHub refused. {{remedy}}
badge.reason.mergeRefused.detail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: GitHub would not merge the proposal. "gate" is a condition a proposal must meet before merging. {{remedy}} is one or more complete sentences saying who has to do what next.

badge.reason.conflicts.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal no longer merges cleanly into the main line of code. A statement: this proposal conflicts. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.conflicts.labelFiles_one.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal no longer merges cleanly into the main line of code. {{count}} is how many files changed on both sides. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.conflicts.labelFiles_other.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal no longer merges cleanly into the main line of code. {{count}} is how many files changed on both sides. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.conflicts.files_one.description: Small text beside "Conflicts with main" in the ledger on a proposal's page: how many files changed on both sides. {{count}} is that number of files.

badge.reason.conflicts.files_other.description: Small text beside "Conflicts with main" in the ledger on a proposal's page: how many files changed on both sides. {{count}} is that number of files.

badge.reason.conflicts.detail.text: This proposal no longer merges into main on its own. {{remedy}}
badge.reason.conflicts.detail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the proposal no longer merges cleanly into the main line of code. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{remedy}} is one or more complete sentences saying who has to do what next.

badge.reason.conflicts.detailFiles.text: This proposal no longer merges into main on its own. {{remedy}} Changed on both sides: {{files}}.
badge.reason.conflicts.detailFiles.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the proposal no longer merges cleanly into the main line of code. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{remedy}} is one or more complete sentences saying who has to do what next. {{files}} lists the paths of the files that changed both in the proposal and in main.

badge.reason.conflicts.detailFilesMore_o.text: This proposal no longer merges into main on its own. {{remedy}} Changed on both sides: {{files}} and {{count}} more.
badge.reason.conflicts.detailFilesMore_o.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the proposal no longer merges cleanly into the main line of code. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{remedy}} is one or more complete sentences saying who has to do what next. {{files}} lists the paths of the first files that changed on both sides and {{count}} is how many more there are.

badge.reason.conflicts.detailFilesMore_o.text: This proposal no longer merges into main on its own. {{remedy}} Changed on both sides: {{files}} and {{count}} more.
badge.reason.conflicts.detailFilesMore_o.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the proposal no longer merges cleanly into the main line of code. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{remedy}} is one or more complete sentences saying who has to do what next. {{files}} lists the paths of the first files that changed on both sides and {{count}} is how many more there are.

badge.reason.conflicts.detailFilesSample.text: This proposal no longer merges into main on its own. {{remedy}} Changed on both sides: {{files}}. That list is a sample, not the whole set.
badge.reason.conflicts.detailFilesSample.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the proposal no longer merges cleanly into the main line of code. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{remedy}} is one or more complete sentences saying who has to do what next. {{files}} lists the paths of some of the files that changed on both sides; the full list is not known.

badge.reason.conflicts.detailFilesMoreSa.text: This proposal no longer merges into main on its own. {{remedy}} Changed on both sides: {{files}} and {{count}} more. That list is a sample, not the whole set.
badge.reason.conflicts.detailFilesMoreSa.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the proposal no longer merges cleanly into the main line of code. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{remedy}} is one or more complete sentences saying who has to do what next. {{files}} lists the paths of the first files that changed on both sides and {{count}} is how many more are known; the full list is not known.

badge.reason.conflicts.detailFilesMoreSa.text: This proposal no longer merges into main on its own. {{remedy}} Changed on both sides: {{files}} and {{count}} more. That list is a sample, not the whole set.
badge.reason.conflicts.detailFilesMoreSa.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the proposal no longer merges cleanly into the main line of code. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{remedy}} is one or more complete sentences saying who has to do what next. {{files}} lists the paths of the first files that changed on both sides and {{count}} is how many more are known; the full list is not known.

badge.reason.previewFailed.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal's staging preview fails to start.

badge.reason.previewFailed.detailWith.text: The staging preview failed to start, so automated checks can’t run: {{error}}
badge.reason.previewFailed.detailWith.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the preview fails to start. {{error}} is the build's own error text.

badge.reason.previewFailed.detail.text: The staging preview failed to start, so automated checks couldn’t run.
badge.reason.previewFailed.detail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the preview failed to start and no error text was recorded.

badge.reason.codeMissing.label.description: Red status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal's code (its branch) is not on Homeroom's own code host, because it did not come across when Homeroom moved off GitHub. It cannot be built, tested or merged until the code is back; votes on it are still recorded.

badge.reason.codeMissing.detail.text: This proposal’s code didn’t come across when Homeroom moved off GitHub. Its creator can submit it again, or Homeroom restores it when GitHub’s copy of the code arrives.
badge.reason.codeMissing.detail.description: Tooltip of the "Code missing" status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page. GitHub is a product name; Homeroom is the product's own name. "GitHub's copy of the code" is the export of the old repositories that GitHub is sending to Homeroom. "Submit it again" means put the same change up again.

badge.reason.waitsFor.label.description: Amber status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal is built on another open change's branch, so it goes live only after that change does. {{number}} is that other change's number. Nobody has to act on this proposal.

badge.reason.waitsFor.labelUnnumbered.description: Amber status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page, when the change it is built on has no number yet: the proposal is built on another open change's branch, so it goes live only after that change does.

badge.reason.waitsFor.detail.text: This change is built on #{{number}}, so it can go live only after #{{number}} does. Homeroom then moves it onto main and brings it up to date.
badge.reason.waitsFor.detail.description: Tooltip of the "Waits for #N" status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page. {{number}} is the number of the change it is built on. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.waitsFor.detailUnnumbered.text: This change is built on another change, so it can go live only after that change does. Homeroom then moves it onto main and brings it up to date.
badge.reason.waitsFor.detailUnnumbered.description: Tooltip of the "Waits for another change" status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page, when the change it is built on has no number yet. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.baseNotMain.label.description: Red status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal's pull request targets a branch other than main, and no open change in the project uses that branch, so it cannot go live until its base is changed to main. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.baseNotMain.detail.text: Its pull request targets {{branch}}, not main, and no open change here is built on that branch. Change its base to main on GitHub before it can go live.
badge.reason.baseNotMain.detail.description: Tooltip of the "Not based on main" status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page. {{branch}} is the name of the branch the pull request targets, as written on GitHub, and stays as it is. GitHub is a product name. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.checksRetry.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: beside a spinner; a run of the automated checks was interrupted and starts again by itself.

badge.reason.checksRetry.detailWith.text: {{reason}} Merge is blocked until they pass.
badge.reason.checksRetry.detailWith.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the checks were interrupted and will run again. {{reason}} is a complete sentence the platform recorded about the interruption; "they" are the checks. "Merge" is the noun.

badge.reason.checksRetry.detail.text: Merge is blocked until they pass.
badge.reason.checksRetry.detail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the checks were interrupted and will run again. "they" are the checks. "Merge" is the noun.

badge.reason.checksError.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the automated checks could not be run at all.

badge.reason.checksError.detailWith.text: The automated check run ended before it could produce a verdict: {{reason}}
badge.reason.checksError.detailWith.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the checks could not be run. "run" is a noun. {{reason}} is the reason the platform recorded, in its own words.

badge.reason.checksError.detail.text: The automated check run ended before it could produce a verdict. The preview may still be available.
badge.reason.checksError.detail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the checks could not be run and no reason was recorded. "run" is a noun.

badge.reason.checksFailing.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: automated checks that gate the merge are failing.

badge.reason.checksFailing.labelCount_on.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: automated checks are failing. {{count}} is how many failed.

badge.reason.checksFailing.labelCount_ot.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: automated checks are failing. {{count}} is how many failed.

badge.reason.checksFailing.detailNames_o.text: {{count}} automated test failed on the staging build: {{tests}}.
badge.reason.checksFailing.detailNames_o.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: checks are failing. {{count}} is how many failed and {{tests}} lists their names.

badge.reason.checksFailing.detailNames_o.text: {{count}} automated tests failed on the staging build: {{tests}}.
badge.reason.checksFailing.detailNames_o.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: checks are failing. {{count}} is how many failed and {{tests}} lists their names.

badge.reason.checksFailing.unnamed.description: Stands in for a failed check's name, in the list of failed checks in a proposal's status tooltip, when the check has neither a name nor a path. A noun, lower case.

badge.reason.checksFailing.detail.text: Automated tests are not passing on the staging build.
badge.reason.checksFailing.detail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: checks are failing and it is not known which.

badge.reason.checksFailing.mainDetail.text: These automated tests also fail on main, so they are not this change’s: {{tests}}.
badge.reason.checksFailing.mainDetail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: every test that failed also fails on main, the project's shared code, so the change is not at fault. {{tests}} lists their names. "main" is the name of the code branch and stays in English.

badge.reason.checksFailing.mainSomeDetai.text: These automated tests also fail on main: {{main}}. These fail only in this change: {{own}}.
badge.reason.checksFailing.mainSomeDetai.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: some failing tests also fail on main, the project's shared code, and some fail only in this change. {{main}} and {{own}} each list test names. "main" is the name of the code branch and stays in English.

badge.reason.behind.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the main line of code has moved on since the proposal was made. Not a block, only worth knowing. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.behind.labelCount_one.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the main line of code has moved on since the proposal was made. {{count}} is how many commits it has gained. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.behind.labelCount_other.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the main line of code has moved on since the proposal was made. {{count}} is how many commits it has gained. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.behind.detailCountConflict_.text: This proposal is {{count}} commit behind main. The conflict is what stands between it and merging; the distance itself does not.
badge.reason.behind.detailCountConflict_.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the main line of code has moved on since the proposal was made. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. The proposal also conflicts with main. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained.

badge.reason.behind.detailCountConflict_.text: This proposal is {{count}} commits behind main. The conflict is what stands between it and merging; the distance itself does not.
badge.reason.behind.detailCountConflict_.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the main line of code has moved on since the proposal was made. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. The proposal also conflicts with main. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained.

badge.reason.behind.detailCountClean_one.text: This proposal is {{count}} commit behind main but still merges cleanly. It merges as it stands; nothing needs syncing.
badge.reason.behind.detailCountClean_one.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the main line of code has moved on since the proposal was made. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. The proposal still merges cleanly. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained.

badge.reason.behind.detailCountClean_oth.text: This proposal is {{count}} commits behind main but still merges cleanly. It merges as it stands; nothing needs syncing.
badge.reason.behind.detailCountClean_oth.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the main line of code has moved on since the proposal was made. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. The proposal still merges cleanly. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained.

badge.reason.behind.detailConflict.text: This proposal is behind main. The conflict is what stands between it and merging; the distance itself does not.
badge.reason.behind.detailConflict.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the main line of code has moved on since the proposal was made. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. The proposal also conflicts with main, and it is not known by how many commits it is behind.

badge.reason.behind.detailClean.text: This proposal is behind main but still merges cleanly. It merges as it stands; nothing needs syncing.
badge.reason.behind.detailClean.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the main line of code has moved on since the proposal was made. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. The proposal still merges cleanly, and it is not known by how many commits it is behind.

badge.reason.olderMain.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal's checks passed, but against an older state of the main line of code. Not a block. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.olderMain.labelCount_one.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal's checks passed, but against an older state of the main line of code. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.olderMain.labelCount_other.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal's checks passed, but against an older state of the main line of code. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.integrating.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: beside a spinner; the platform is merging the main line of code into the proposal to resolve a conflict. Keep the ellipsis.

badge.reason.integrating.detail.text: The platform is merging main into this proposal to resolve a conflict. The result is previewed and checked, and it merges on its own once the vote passes. Nobody needs to do anything.
badge.reason.integrating.detail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the platform is resolving the proposal's conflict by itself. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.budget.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal needs an automatic merge with the main line of code, and the platform's shared daily AI budget is used up.

badge.reason.budget.detail.text: This proposal needs merging with main, but the platform’s shared token budget is spent for today. It resumes after the midnight UTC reset.
badge.reason.budget.detail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: the shared daily AI budget is used up. Keep the words "midnight UTC" exactly: the page replaces them with the viewer's local time. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.githubBusy.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal passed its vote and its checks, but GitHub held its merge back. The platform tries again by itself, so nobody has to act.

badge.reason.githubBusy.detail.text: GitHub said a merge of this change was already in progress. Homeroom tries again at {{time}}.
badge.reason.githubBusy.detail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page. {{time}} is a clock time such as 10:45, shown in the viewer's own time zone. "Homeroom" is the name of the platform and stays as it is.

badge.reason.githubBusy.detailSoon.text: GitHub said a merge of this change was already in progress. Homeroom tries again in a few minutes.
badge.reason.githubBusy.detailSoon.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page, when the next try's time has passed or was not recorded. "Homeroom" is the name of the platform and stays as it is.

badge.reason.githubRefused.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: the proposal passed its vote and its checks, but GitHub refused its merge for a reason nobody has to act on. The platform tries again by itself.

badge.reason.githubRefused.detail.text: GitHub refused the merge. Homeroom tries again at {{time}}.
badge.reason.githubRefused.detail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page, when GitHub refused the merge for a reason nobody has to act on. {{time}} is a clock time such as 10:45, shown in the viewer's own time zone. "Homeroom" is the name of the platform and stays as it is.

badge.reason.githubRefused.detailSoon.text: GitHub refused the merge. Homeroom tries again in a few minutes.
badge.reason.githubRefused.detailSoon.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page, when GitHub refused the merge for a reason nobody has to act on, and the next try's time has passed or was not recorded. "Homeroom" is the name of the platform and stays as it is.

badge.reason.mainPaused.label.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: no change of this app can go live for now, because the tests of the app's main line of code are failing.

badge.reason.mainPaused.labelRechecking.text: Going live is paused · re-checking main
badge.reason.mainPaused.labelRechecking.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: no change of this app can go live for now, and the failing tests of the main line of code are being run again to confirm. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.mainPaused.rechecking.description: Small text beside "Going live is paused" in the ledger on a proposal's page: the failing tests of the main line of code are being run again to confirm. Lower case. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is.

badge.reason.mainPaused.detailNote.text: {{note}}. Nothing about this change is wrong; it goes live once the app is healthy again or an admin resumes.
badge.reason.mainPaused.detailNote.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: going live is paused for the whole app. {{note}} is the platform's own sentence saying why, without its full stop.

badge.reason.mainPaused.detail.text: Main’s unit suite is failing, so going live is paused for this app. Nothing about this change is wrong; it goes live once the app is healthy again or an admin resumes.
badge.reason.mainPaused.detail.description: Tooltip of the status tag on a proposal's card, and text of the matching ledger row on its page: going live is paused for the whole app because the unit tests of its main line of code fail. "Main" is that line's name.

badge.reason.shots.retrying.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: beside a spinner; taking the before and after screenshots was interrupted and is starting again. "Screenshots" are the pictures Homeroom takes of what a proposal changes, before and after.

badge.reason.shots.running.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: beside a spinner; the before and after screenshots are being taken. "Screenshots" are the pictures Homeroom takes of what a proposal changes, before and after.

badge.reason.shots.notStarted.description: Status tag on a proposal's card and row label in the ledger on its page: taking the before and after screenshots has not begun. "Screenshots" are the pictures Homeroom takes of what a proposal changes, before and after.
