shots.screen.sized.description: First fact in the line under a before/after screenshot of a change: the screen size's name, for example "Desktop", then the screenshot's {{width}} and {{height}} in pixels. "Seen as …" follows it after a middle dot.

shots.claim.notInShots.description: Note under a declared change on a proposal's screenshots card. {{note}} is what the screenshot agent wrote about the part of the change its screenshots do not show. The tags make the lead-in bold.

shots.claim.requestHeld.text: <0>Controlled test:</0> the screenshot agent kept {{request}} waiting on both builds, to show it loading.
shots.claim.requestHeld.description: Note under a declared change on a proposal's screenshots card, when the screenshots were taken while the app's request for some data was deliberately left unanswered on both the version before and the version after the proposal, so that its loading state shows. {{request}} is that request as written in code, for example "GET /api/items?page=1"; leave it as it is. The tags make the lead-in bold.

shots.claim.requestFailed.text: <0>Controlled test:</0> the screenshot agent made {{request}} fail on both builds, to show what happens when it does.
shots.claim.requestFailed.description: Note under a declared change on a proposal's screenshots card, when the screenshots were taken while the app's request for some data was deliberately made to fail on both the version before and the version after the proposal, so that its error state shows. {{request}} is that request as written in code, for example "GET /api/items?page=1"; leave it as it is. The tags make the lead-in bold.

shots.claim.sampleFile.text: <0>Sample file:</0> the screenshot agent uploaded {{files}} on both builds, from Homeroom's own sample files.
shots.claim.sampleFile.description: Note under a declared change on a proposal's screenshots card, when the screenshots show the app after a file was uploaded into it, the same on the version before and the version after the proposal. {{files}} is the list of file names, for example "landscape.png and table.csv"; the files are made-up pictures, a table and a document that Homeroom provides for this. The tags make the lead-in bold.

shots.clip.beforeCaption.description: Caption over a short video of a declared change as it was before the proposal. {{size}} is the screen size it was recorded at, for example "desktop".

shots.clip.afterCaption.description: Caption over a short video of a declared change as it is after the proposal. {{size}} is the screen size it was recorded at, for example "desktop".

shots.clip.beforeLabel.description: Accessible name of the short video of a declared change as it was before the proposal. {{claim}} is the author's own sentence describing that change.

shots.clip.afterLabel.description: Accessible name of the short video of a declared change as it is after the proposal. {{claim}} is the author's own sentence describing that change.

shots.clip.none.description: Placeholder where a short video of one side (before or after) of a declared change is missing.

shots.clip.playAnimation.description: Disclosure label on a proposal's screenshots card: opens a video recording of an animation the proposal changes.

shots.clip.playInteraction.description: Disclosure label on a proposal's screenshots card: opens a video recording of someone using the changed feature.

shots.clip.animationLabel.description: Accessible name of a video recording of an animation the proposal changes. {{claim}} is the author's own sentence describing that change.

shots.clip.interactionLabel.description: Accessible name of a video recording of the changed feature being used. {{claim}} is the author's own sentence describing that change.

shots.screen.noShot.description: Placeholder in the before/after viewer where one side has no screenshot.

shots.screen.nothingBefore.description: Shown in the before/after viewer in place of the screenshot before the change, when the change builds a new app's first real screens: before it the app had only the starter template's placeholder screen, so there is no before.

shots.screen.altAfter.description: Description, for people who cannot see it, of the screenshot taken after the change. {{changes}} is the author's own sentences describing what changes on that screen.

shots.screen.altBefore.description: Description, for people who cannot see it, of the screenshot taken before the change. {{changes}} is the author's own sentences describing what changes on that screen.

shots.screen.altBeforeAbsent.description: Description, for people who cannot see it, of the screenshot taken before the change when the changed feature did not exist yet. {{changes}} is the author's own sentences describing what changes on that screen.

shots.screen.keyOutline.text: Dashed outline: also changed here, but no change on this list describes it
shots.screen.keyOutline.description: Legend under a before/after screenshot explaining a dashed box drawn on it: that area differs between before and after, but none of the listed changes accounts for it.

shots.screen.keyLine.text: Dashed line: where the change begins on a side that doesn’t have it
shots.screen.keyLine.description: Legend under a before/after screenshot explaining a dashed line drawn on it: it marks where the new content starts, on the side (before or after) where that content is absent.

shots.claim.failedBadge.description: Red badge beside a declared change on a proposal's screenshots card: the screenshot agent tried it on the new build and the app broke.

shots.claim.failedReason.text: The screenshot agent tried this on the after build, and the app broke.
shots.claim.failedReason.description: Explanation under a declared change marked "Didn’t work" on a proposal's screenshots card, when the server gave no reason. "This" is the declared change; the "after build" is the app with the proposal applied.

shots.claim.skippedBadge.description: Grey badge beside a declared change on a proposal's screenshots card: the screenshot agent could not reach it, so it has no screenshots.

shots.claim.skippedReason.text: The screenshot agent could not get to this change.
shots.claim.skippedReason.description: Explanation under a declared change marked "Skipped" on a proposal's screenshots card, when the server gave no reason.

shots.claim.where.description: Small print under a declared change on a proposal's screenshots card. {{sizes}} is the list of screen sizes it was screenshot at, for example "desktop, phone", and {{persona}} who the screen was viewed as, for example "member".

shots.compare.fallbackTitle.description: Title of the full-screen before/after comparison when the change it shows has no description of its own.

shots.compare.before.description: Heading over the left picture in the full-screen before/after comparison: the screen before the change.

shots.compare.beforeAbsent.description: Heading over the left picture in the full-screen before/after comparison when the changed feature did not exist before the change.

shots.compare.after.description: Heading over the right picture in the full-screen before/after comparison: the screen after the change.

shots.compare.notThereYet.description: Placeholder in the full-screen before/after comparison where the "before" picture would be: the changed feature did not exist yet.

shots.compare.noShot.description: Placeholder in the full-screen before/after comparison where one side has no screenshot.

shots.compare.openOriginal.description: Link under a picture in the full-screen before/after comparison: opens the full-size image in a new tab. Keep the arrow.

shots.compare.altBefore.description: Description, for people who cannot see it, of the "before" picture in the full-screen comparison. {{claim}} is the author's own sentence describing the change.

shots.compare.altBeforeUnnamed.description: Description, for people who cannot see it, of the "before" picture in the full-screen comparison when the change has no description of its own.

shots.compare.altBeforeAbsent.description: Description, for people who cannot see it, of the "before" picture in the full-screen comparison when the changed feature did not exist yet. {{claim}} is the author's own sentence describing the change.

shots.compare.altBeforeAbsentUnnamed.text: Before · Not there yet: before/after screenshot
shots.compare.altBeforeAbsentUnnamed.description: Description, for people who cannot see it, of the "before" picture in the full-screen comparison when the changed feature did not exist yet and the change has no description of its own.

shots.compare.altAfter.description: Description, for people who cannot see it, of the "after" picture in the full-screen comparison. {{claim}} is the author's own sentence describing the change.

shots.compare.altAfterUnnamed.description: Description, for people who cannot see it, of the "after" picture in the full-screen comparison when the change has no description of its own.

shots.toast.takingAgain.text: Taking the before & after screenshots again.
shots.toast.takingAgain.description: Brief notice after pressing "Take the screenshots again" on a proposal: the screenshots have started over.

shots.toast.takeAgainFailed.text: Could not take the screenshots again: {{error}}
shots.toast.takeAgainFailed.description: Brief notice when "Take the screenshots again" on a proposal failed. {{error}} is the server's own reason.

shots.toast.stopped.description: Brief notice after pressing "Stop" on a proposal's screenshots card: taking the screenshots was stopped.

shots.toast.alreadyFinished.text: The before & after screenshots had already finished.
shots.toast.alreadyFinished.description: Brief notice after pressing "Stop" on a proposal's screenshots card when the screenshots were already done, so there was nothing to stop.

shots.toast.stopFailed.text: Could not stop the before & after screenshots: {{error}}
shots.toast.stopFailed.description: Brief notice when "Stop" on a proposal's screenshots card failed. {{error}} is the server's own reason.

shots.tiles.before.description: Label over the small picture of a screen as it was before a change, in the pair of before/after pictures on a proposal or in a build chat.

shots.tiles.after.description: Label over the small picture of a screen as it is after a change, in the pair of before/after pictures on a proposal or in a build chat.

shots.tiles.openBefore.description: Tooltip of the small "Before" picture of a change: pressing it opens the full-size before/after comparison.

shots.tiles.openAfter.description: Tooltip of the small "After" picture of a change: pressing it opens the full-size before/after comparison.

shots.tiles.row.description: Label over one pair of before/after pictures of a change, naming the page they show. {{path}} is that page's address inside the app, for example "/settings"; keep it inside the tags, which set it in code type.

shots.tiles.rowMobile.description: Label over one pair of before/after pictures of a change taken at a phone's screen size. {{path}} is the page's address inside the app, for example "/settings"; keep it inside the tags, which set it in code type.

shots.tiles.newPage.text: New page (no production version to compare)
shots.tiles.newPage.description: Caption under a pair of before/after pictures when there is no "before" picture because the page did not exist in the live app.

shots.tiles.beforeFellBack.text: "Before" shows the home page. This page didn’t exist in production yet
shots.tiles.beforeFellBack.description: Caption under a pair of before/after pictures when the "Before" picture shows the app's home page, because the changed page did not exist in the live app. "Before" is the label of that picture.

shots.tiles.allScreens_one.description: Disclosure label under the first pair of before/after pictures of a change: opens the rest. {{count}} is how many pairs (screens) there are in all.

shots.tiles.allScreens_other.description: Disclosure label under the first pair of before/after pictures of a change: opens the rest. {{count}} is how many pairs (screens) there are in all.

shots.overlay.titleMobile.description: Title of the full-screen before/after comparison when the pictures were taken at a phone's screen size. {{path}} is the page's address inside the app, for example "/settings".

shots.overlay.before.description: Heading over the left picture in the full-screen before/after comparison opened from a small picture: the screen before the change. Also that picture's description for people who cannot see it.

shots.overlay.after.description: Heading over the right picture in the full-screen before/after comparison opened from a small picture: the screen after the change. Also that picture's description for people who cannot see it.

shots.overlay.noBefore.description: Placeholder in the full-screen before/after comparison where the "before" picture is missing.

shots.overlay.noAfter.description: Placeholder in the full-screen before/after comparison where the "after" picture is missing.

shots.overlay.openOriginal.description: Link under a picture or video in the full-screen before/after comparison opened from a small picture: opens the original file in a new tab. Keep the arrow.

shots.overlay.path.description: Line at the top of the full-screen before/after comparison naming the page the pictures show. {{path}} is that page's address inside the app; keep it inside the tags, which set it in code type.

shots.overlay.pathMobile.description: Line at the top of the full-screen before/after comparison when the pictures were taken at a phone's screen size. {{path}} is the page's address inside the app; keep it inside the tags, which set it in code type.

chips.work.inReview.description: Chip on a request's card: someone turned work on this request into a proposal, which is now waiting for votes.

chips.work.working.description: Chip on a request's card: someone has an agent session open that is working on this request.

chips.work.autoSolving.description: Chip on a request's card while an automatic run is trying to solve the request without a person. A spinner is drawn before it.

chips.work.started.description: Chip on a request's card: someone began work on this request but is not working on it right now. A past participle describing the request.

chips.work.answerNeeded.description: Chip on a request's card: an automatic run got part way and asked a question that someone must answer before it can go on.

chips.work.draftReady.description: Chip on a request's card: an automatic run finished and left a draft of the change for someone to look over.

chips.work.pickedUp.description: Chip on a request's card: someone said they will work on this request but has not started building yet. A past participle describing the request.

chips.work.botQueued.description: Chip on a request's card: the Homeroom bot (the platform's own building agent, a name) has been asked to build this request and has not started yet.

chips.work.botReading.description: Chip on a request's card while the Homeroom bot (the platform's own building agent, a name) is reading the request.

chips.work.botBuilding.description: Chip on a request's card while the Homeroom bot (the platform's own building agent, a name) is building the request.

chips.work.you.description: Stands for the viewer in the chip on a request's card that says who is working on it, after the state and a dot, for example "Being worked on · you". Lower case in English because it follows the dot.

chips.work.labelWho.description: Chip on a request's card naming the state of the work and who is doing it, for example "Picked up · maya". {{state}} is the state's own label and {{who}} a username or the word for "you". Only the separator is translated.

chips.work.labelWhoMore_one.description: Chip on a request's card naming the state of the work, who is doing it and how many other people are too, for example "Being worked on · maya +1". {{state}} is the state's own label, {{who}} a username or the word for "you", and {{count}} the number of other people.

chips.work.labelWhoMore_other.description: Chip on a request's card naming the state of the work, who is doing it and how many other people are too, for example "Being worked on · maya +2". {{state}} is the state's own label, {{who}} a username or the word for "you", and {{count}} the number of other people.

chips.work.openTitle.description: Tooltip of the work chip on a request's card when pressing it opens the change being made for the request. {{note}} is the full sentence describing who is working on it, which already ends with its own period.

chips.workNote.then.description: Joins two whole sentences of the note that explains who is working on a request. {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next sentence. Only the space between them is translated.

chips.workNote.inReview.you.text: You have put this up for review as a proposal, so it is waiting on reviewers rather than on more work.
chips.workNote.inReview.you.description: Note on a request (its page and the work chip's tooltip) when the viewer turned their work on it into a proposal. "This" is the request.

chips.workNote.also.claimsBotBuilding.text: Also: picked up by {{names}}; the Homeroom bot is building it.
chips.workNote.also.claimsBotBuilding.description: Closing sentence of the note on a request: others said they would work on it, and the Homeroom bot (a name) is building the request. {{names}} is a list of usernames.

chips.workNote.also.claimsAutoBotReading.text: Also: picked up by {{names}}; an auto-solve run is on it too; the Homeroom bot is reading it.
chips.workNote.also.claimsAutoBotReading.description: Closing sentence of the note on a request: others said they would work on it, an automatic run is working on it, and the Homeroom bot (a name) is reading it. {{names}} is a list of usernames.

chips.workNote.also.claimsAutoBotBuildin.text: Also: picked up by {{names}}; an auto-solve run is on it too; the Homeroom bot is building it.
chips.workNote.also.claimsAutoBotBuildin.description: Closing sentence of the note on a request: others said they would work on it, an automatic run is working on it, and the Homeroom bot (a name) is building it. {{names}} is a list of usernames.

chips.workNote.also.auto.text: Also: an auto-solve run is on it too.
chips.workNote.also.auto.description: Closing sentence of the note on a request: besides what was just said, an automatic run is working on it.

chips.workNote.also.autoBotReading.text: Also: an auto-solve run is on it too; the Homeroom bot is reading it.
chips.workNote.also.autoBotReading.description: Closing sentence of the note on a request: an automatic run is working on it and the Homeroom bot (a name) is reading it.

chips.workNote.also.autoBotBuilding.text: Also: an auto-solve run is on it too; the Homeroom bot is building it.
chips.workNote.also.autoBotBuilding.description: Closing sentence of the note on a request: an automatic run is working on it and the Homeroom bot (a name) is building it.

chips.workNote.also.botReading.text: Also: the Homeroom bot is reading it.
chips.workNote.also.botReading.description: Closing sentence of the note on a request: besides what was just said, the Homeroom bot (a name) is reading the request.

chips.workNote.also.botBuilding.text: Also: the Homeroom bot is building it.
chips.workNote.also.botBuilding.description: Closing sentence of the note on a request: besides what was just said, the Homeroom bot (a name) is building the request.

chips.issue.closes.description: Chip on a proposal's card linking to the request it will close when it goes live. A verb: this proposal closes that request. {{number}} is the request's number; keep the "#".

chips.issue.closed.description: Chip on a finished change's card linking to the request it closed. A verb in the past: this change closed that request. {{number}} is the request's number; keep the "#".

chips.issue.openTitle.description: Tooltip of a "#N" chip on a card: pressing it opens that request's discussion inside Homeroom. "Open" is a verb; an issue is a request. {{number}} is the request's number.

chips.issue.closesLink.description: Link on a proposal's page to the request it will close when it goes live; it opens that request's page. A verb: this proposal closes that request. {{number}} is the request's number; keep the "#".

chips.issue.closedLink.description: Link on a merged proposal's page to the request it closed; it opens that request's page. A verb in the past. {{number}} is the request's number; keep the "#".

chips.issue.closesRequestTitle.text: Open request #{{number}}, which this change closes
chips.issue.closesRequestTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Closes #N" link on a proposal's page: pressing it opens the request inside Homeroom, and the proposal will close that request when it goes live. "Open" is a verb. {{number}} is the request's number.

chips.issue.closedRequestTitle.text: Open request #{{number}}, which this change closed
chips.issue.closedRequestTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Closed #N" link on a merged proposal's page: pressing it opens the request inside Homeroom, which the proposal closed. "Open" is a verb. {{number}} is the request's number.

vote.row.votedYes.description: Read-only box that replaces the vote buttons on a proposal's row in a chat once the viewer has voted Yes. Yes is one of the two sides of a vote on a proposal.

vote.row.votedNo.description: Read-only box that replaces the vote buttons on a proposal's row in a chat once the viewer has voted No. No is one of the two sides of a vote on a proposal.

vote.row.retryPreview.description: Button beside the vote buttons on a proposal's row when its staging preview failed to build: tries building the preview again.

vote.row.retryPreviewTitle.text: Try building this proposal's staging preview again
vote.row.retryPreviewTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Retry preview" button on a proposal's row.

vote.row.adminMerge.description: Button beside the vote buttons on a proposal's row, shown to administrators: makes the proposal go live at once without waiting for the vote. "Merge" is a verb here.

vote.row.yes.description: The Yes vote button on a proposal's row in a chat or in the activity panel. Yes is one of the two sides of a vote on a proposal. {{tally}} is the number of Yes votes so far, for example "3", or "2✓ +1" where votes from approvers and advisory votes are counted separately.

vote.row.no.description: The No vote button on a proposal's row in a chat or in the activity panel. No is one of the two sides of a vote on a proposal. {{tally}} is the number of No votes so far, for example "1", or "1✓ +2" where votes from approvers and advisory votes are counted separately.

vote.row.yesNone.description: The Yes vote button on a proposal's row in a chat or in the activity panel while nobody has voted Yes yet: no count is shown, because a zero says nothing. Yes is one of the two sides of a vote on a proposal.

vote.row.noNone.description: The No vote button on a proposal's row in a chat or in the activity panel while nobody has voted No yet: no count is shown, because a zero says nothing. No is one of the two sides of a vote on a proposal.

vote.row.uncounted.text: Test account: this vote won’t count.
vote.row.uncounted.description: Note beside the vote buttons on a proposal when the viewer is signed in with a test account, whose vote is recorded but not counted.

vote.row.advisory.text: Your vote is advisory: it’s recorded, but it doesn’t decide this change.
vote.row.advisory.description: Note beside the vote buttons on a proposal in the chat and the activity panel, shown to someone outside the people who decide on this project — not an approver where only approvers decide, or outside every group the project’s rules name. Their vote is recorded and shown, but does not affect the outcome.

frame.open.proposal.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the Preview control on a proposal's card: opens the running preview of the app with the proposal applied. "Open" is a verb.

frame.open.proposalRebuild.text: Open this proposal’s staging preview (rebuilds it if it went to sleep)
frame.open.proposalRebuild.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the Preview control on a proposal's card when the preview may have been shut down for inactivity and pressing it builds it again. "Open" is a verb.

frame.open.ownSession.text: Open this session’s staging preview (rebuilds it if it went to sleep)
frame.open.ownSession.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the Preview control on the viewer's own build session: opens the running preview of their work in progress, building it again if it was shut down for inactivity. "Open" is a verb.

frame.open.ownSessionRebuild.text: Open this session’s staging preview (rebuilds it if it went to sleep) (rebuilds it if it went to sleep)
frame.open.ownSessionRebuild.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the Preview control on the viewer's own build session when no preview is running at the moment. The English repeats the parenthesis; a translation may say it once.

frame.open.sharedSession.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the Preview control on someone else's shared build session: opens the running preview of their work in progress. "Open" is a verb.

frame.open.sharedSessionRebuild.text: Open this session’s staging preview (rebuilds it if it went to sleep)
frame.open.sharedSessionRebuild.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the Preview control on someone else's shared build session when the preview may have been shut down for inactivity and pressing it builds it again.

frame.open.issueRun.text: Open the generated proposal’s staging preview
frame.open.issueRun.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the Preview control on a request that an automatic run turned into a draft proposal: opens the running preview of that draft. "Open" is a verb.

frame.open.issueRunRebuild.text: Open the generated proposal’s staging preview (rebuilds it if it went to sleep)
frame.open.issueRunRebuild.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the Preview control on a request that an automatic run turned into a draft proposal, when the preview may have been shut down for inactivity and pressing it builds it again.

frame.open.unavailableBecause.description: Tooltip of the crossed-out Preview control on a card when the staging preview failed. {{error}} is the server's own reason.

frame.open.unavailableDidNotStart.text: Preview unavailable: the submitted preview did not start
frame.open.unavailableDidNotStart.description: Tooltip of the crossed-out Preview control on a card when the staging preview failed and no reason was recorded.

frame.open.building.text: The staging preview is being built. This usually takes a few minutes. A Preview button appears here as soon as it’s ready.
frame.open.building.description: Tooltip of the Preview control on a card while the staging preview is still being built. "Preview" is the button's label.

vote.row.preview.description: Button beside the vote buttons on a proposal's row: opens the running preview of the app with the proposal applied. A verb.

vote.row.previewBuilding.description: Status chip beside the vote buttons on a proposal's row while its staging preview is being built. A spinner is drawn before it.

vote.row.previewBuildingTitle.text: The staging preview for this proposal is being built. This usually takes a few minutes. A Preview button appears here as soon as it's ready.
vote.row.previewBuildingTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Preview building…" chip on a proposal's row. "Preview" is the label of the button that will appear.

vote.row.previewUnavailable.description: Status chip beside the vote buttons on a proposal's row when its staging preview failed to build. The reason is in its tooltip.

vote.tally.tip.description: Tooltip of a Yes or No vote button in a community where only invited approvers' votes count. {{approvers}} is a phrase counting approver votes and {{advisory}} a phrase counting the other votes. Only the separator is translated.

vote.tally.approverYes_one.description: First part of the Yes vote button's tooltip on a proposal: how many Yes votes came from approvers, whose votes count. Yes is one of the two sides of the vote. {{count}} is the number.

vote.tally.approverYes_other.description: First part of the Yes vote button's tooltip on a proposal: how many Yes votes came from approvers, whose votes count. Yes is one of the two sides of the vote. {{count}} is the number.

vote.tally.advisoryYes_one.text: {{count}} advisory Yes vote (advisory votes don't count toward merging)
vote.tally.advisoryYes_one.description: Second part of the Yes vote button's tooltip on a proposal: how many Yes votes came from people who are not approvers. Yes is one of the two sides of the vote; "merging" is the proposal going live. {{count}} is the number.

vote.tally.advisoryYes_other.text: {{count}} advisory Yes votes (advisory votes don't count toward merging)
vote.tally.advisoryYes_other.description: Second part of the Yes vote button's tooltip on a proposal: how many Yes votes came from people who are not approvers. Yes is one of the two sides of the vote; "merging" is the proposal going live. {{count}} is the number.

vote.tally.approverNo_one.description: First part of the No vote button's tooltip on a proposal: how many No votes came from approvers, whose votes count. No is one of the two sides of the vote. {{count}} is the number.

vote.tally.approverNo_other.description: First part of the No vote button's tooltip on a proposal: how many No votes came from approvers, whose votes count. No is one of the two sides of the vote. {{count}} is the number.

vote.tally.advisoryNo_one.text: {{count}} advisory No vote (advisory votes don't count toward merging)
vote.tally.advisoryNo_one.description: Second part of the No vote button's tooltip on a proposal: how many No votes came from people who are not approvers. No is one of the two sides of the vote; "merging" is the proposal going live. {{count}} is the number.

vote.tally.advisoryNo_other.text: {{count}} advisory No votes (advisory votes don't count toward merging)
vote.tally.advisoryNo_other.description: Second part of the No vote button's tooltip on a proposal: how many No votes came from people who are not approvers. No is one of the two sides of the vote; "merging" is the proposal going live. {{count}} is the number.

vote.forceMerge.title.description: Title of the confirmation an administrator sees after pressing "Admin merge" on a proposal. To force-merge is to make it go live at once, skipping the vote; a PR (pull request) is the proposal's code change.

vote.forceMerge.message.text:
This bypasses the active-user vote majority and merges the PR right now.

Use only when you're confident the change should ship. The override is announced in group chat with your username.
vote.forceMerge.message.description: Body of the confirmation an administrator sees after pressing "Admin merge" on a proposal. Two paragraphs; keep the blank line between them.

vote.forceMerge.confirm.description: Confirm button of the administrator's force-merge confirmation: makes the proposal go live at once, skipping the vote. A verb.

vote.forceMerge.failedHttp.description: Brief notice when an administrator's force-merge of a proposal failed and the server gave no reason. {{status}} is the HTTP status code, a number.

vote.forceMerge.failed.description: Brief notice when an administrator's force-merge of a proposal could not be sent. {{error}} is the technical reason.

vote.reason.noTitle.description: Title of the prompt shown after pressing No on a proposal or a request's vote: offers a line saying why, if the voter wants to write one.

vote.reason.yesTitle.text: Add a line for the group?
vote.reason.yesTitle.description: Title of the prompt shown after pressing Yes on a proposal or a request's vote: offers to add an optional one-line comment.

vote.reason.noMessage.text: One line is plenty. It goes to the proposer with your vote.
vote.reason.noMessage.description: Text under the title of the prompt shown after pressing No on a vote. "It" is the line the voter writes; the proposer is the person who made the proposal.

vote.reason.noNeedsLine.text: A No comes with a line: what is not working for you?
vote.reason.noNeedsLine.description: Brief notice when a No vote is sent with no line from the prompt card that offers no list of reasons: a No may not be cast empty.

vote.reason.yesMessage.text: Optional. It shows beside your vote.
vote.reason.yesMessage.description: Text under the title of the prompt shown after pressing Yes on a vote. "It" is the line the voter may write.

vote.reason.noPlaceholder.text: What would you want to change?
vote.reason.noPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the text field of the prompt shown after pressing No on a vote.

vote.reason.yesPlaceholder.text: What do you like about it?
vote.reason.yesPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the text field of the prompt shown after pressing Yes on a vote. "It" is the proposal.

vote.reason.voteNo.description: Confirm button of the prompt shown after pressing No on a vote: casts the No vote with the line written, if any. No is one of the two sides of the vote.

vote.reason.voteYes.description: Confirm button of the prompt shown after pressing Yes on a vote: casts the Yes vote with the line written. Yes is one of the two sides of the vote.

vote.reason.skip.description: Second button of the prompt shown after pressing Yes on a vote: casts the Yes vote without adding a line.

vote.toast.failedHttp.description: Brief notice when a vote on a proposal or a request was refused and the server gave no reason. {{status}} is the HTTP status code, a number.

vote.toast.notSent.text: Your vote did not go through. Check your connection and try again.
vote.toast.notSent.description: Brief notice when a vote on a proposal could not reach the server.

vote.toast.queued.text: You're offline. Your vote will be sent when you're back online.
vote.toast.queued.description: Brief notice when a vote on a proposal could not reach the server and is kept on the device, to be sent once the connection is back.

vote.toast.queuedSent.text: Your vote from while you were offline was sent.
vote.toast.queuedSent.description: Brief notice when a vote kept on the device while offline reached the server.

vote.toast.queuedRefused.text: Your vote from while you were offline wasn't counted. Vote again.
vote.toast.queuedRefused.description: Brief notice when a vote kept on the device while offline was refused once sent, for example because the change was updated meanwhile.

vote.toast.codeMissing.text: Your vote is saved. This proposal can’t go live until its code is back.
vote.toast.codeMissing.description: Brief notice after a vote on a proposal whose code did not come across when Homeroom moved off GitHub: the vote was recorded, but nothing can be merged until the code (its branch) is restored or submitted again.

vote.toast.alreadyMerged.text: This change has already merged, so it no longer needs your vote.
vote.toast.alreadyMerged.description: Brief notice when a Yes or No was pressed on a change that merged after the list showing it was read: the vote was not counted because the change is already live.

vote.toast.noLongerUp.text: This change is no longer up for a vote.
vote.toast.noLongerUp.description: Brief notice when a Yes or No was pressed on a change that left the vote after the list showing it was read: the vote was not counted because the change is no longer being decided.

vote.toast.undoFailedHttp.description: Brief notice when the viewer pressed Undo after voting on a proposal and the server refused without giving a reason; their vote still stands. {{status}} is the HTTP status code, a number.

vote.toast.undoNotSent.text: Your vote wasn't taken back. Check your connection and try again.
vote.toast.undoNotSent.description: Brief notice when the viewer pressed Undo after voting on a proposal and the request could not reach the server; their vote still stands.

vote.toast.issueClosed.description: Brief notice after the viewer's vote decided a proposal to close a request: the request (issue) is now closed. {{number}} is its number, or "?" when unknown.

vote.toast.illustrationChanged.text: Featured illustration changed by group vote.
vote.toast.illustrationChanged.description: Brief notice after the viewer's vote decided a proposal to change the project's featured illustration.

vote.toast.illustrationRemoved.text: Featured illustration removed by group vote.
vote.toast.illustrationRemoved.description: Brief notice after the viewer's vote decided a proposal to remove the project's featured illustration.

vote.toast.issueAlreadyClosed.text: Issue #{{number}} was already closed. The proposal was resolved automatically.
vote.toast.issueAlreadyClosed.description: Brief notice after voting on a proposal to close a request that turned out to be closed already. {{number}} is the request's number, or "?" when unknown.

vote.toast.awaitingAdmin.text: Vote passed. An admin still needs to approve before it applies.
vote.toast.awaitingAdmin.description: Brief notice after the viewer's vote decided a proposal that also needs an administrator's approval. "It" is the proposed change.

vote.toast.applyFailed.description: Brief notice when a vote passed but applying the proposed change failed. {{error}} is the server's own reason.

vote.toast.failed.description: Brief notice when a vote on a request's proposal could not be sent. {{error}} is the technical reason.

vote.toast.failedConnection.description: Brief notice when a vote on a request's proposal could not be sent and no reason is known.

appUnavailable.message.text: This app could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
appUnavailable.message.description: Message shown in place of a project's build screens when the app's record could not be fetched, above a "Try again" button.

session.unavailable.text: That session is private or no longer exists.
session.unavailable.description: Brief notice after following a link to a build session that the viewer cannot open; they land on the project's Workshop instead. A session is a chat with the coding agent.

menu.secrets.noManifest.description: Small status beside "App secrets" in a project's "+" menu before the app has been deployed for the first time, so its list of required settings (its manifest) is not known yet.

menu.secrets.requiredMissing_one.description: Small red status beside "App secrets" in a project's "+" menu: how many required secret values (such as API keys) have not been set. {{count}} is the number.

menu.secrets.requiredMissing_other.description: Small red status beside "App secrets" in a project's "+" menu: how many required secret values (such as API keys) have not been set. {{count}} is the number.

frame.loader.opening.description: Title of the loading screen shown the moment a staging preview is opened, before the server has answered.

frame.loader.rebuilding.description: Title of the preview's loading screen while a preview that was shut down for inactivity is being built again.

frame.loader.rebuildingSub.text: The preview was paused after a while of inactivity. Rebuilding it from the session’s latest changes. This usually takes 20–60 seconds.
frame.loader.rebuildingSub.description: Text under "Spinning the preview back up…" on the preview's loading screen. A session is a chat with the coding agent.

frame.loader.wakingSub.text: Nobody had opened this preview for a while, so it was asleep. Waking it up now, with nothing rebuilt. This usually takes 10 to 30 seconds.
frame.loader.wakingSub.description: Text under "Spinning the preview back up…" on the preview's loading screen when the preview was asleep (stopped to save resources, everything else kept) and is being started again rather than rebuilt.

frame.loader.slow.text: This is taking longer than expected
frame.loader.slow.description: Title of the preview's loading screen when building or loading the preview has run well past the usual time.

frame.loader.slowRebuild.text: The rebuild is still running on the server. Close this and click Preview again in a moment.
frame.loader.slowRebuild.description: Text under "This is taking longer than expected" on the preview's loading screen when a rebuild has not finished after several minutes. "Preview" is the label of the button that opens the preview.

frame.loader.slowLoadFailed.text: The preview didn’t finish loading. Close this and click Preview again in a moment.
frame.loader.slowLoadFailed.description: Text under "This is taking longer than expected" on the preview's loading screen when the preview's page failed to load. "Preview" is the label of the button that opens the preview.

frame.loader.slowStillLoading.text: The preview is still loading. Close this and click Preview again in a moment.
frame.loader.slowStillLoading.description: Text under "This is taking longer than expected" on the preview's loading screen when the preview's page has not finished loading in time. "Preview" is the label of the button that opens the preview.

frame.loader.slowRebuildRetry.text: The rebuild is still running on the server. The preview opens here when it’s done. If it doesn’t, retry in a moment.
frame.loader.slowRebuildRetry.description: Text under "This is taking longer than expected" on the preview's loading screen when a rebuild has not finished after several minutes, above the "Retry preview" button.

frame.loader.slowLoadFailedRetry.text: The preview didn’t finish loading. Retry in a moment.
frame.loader.slowLoadFailedRetry.description: Text under "This is taking longer than expected" on the preview's loading screen when the preview's page failed to load, above the "Retry preview" button.

frame.loader.slowStillLoadingRetry.text: The preview is still loading. If it doesn’t appear soon, retry.
frame.loader.slowStillLoadingRetry.description: Text under "This is taking longer than expected" on the preview's loading screen when the preview's page has not finished loading in time, above the "Retry preview" button.

frame.loader.retryPreview.description: Button on the preview's loading screen after the preview could not be opened: tries opening (and if needed rebuilding) it again.

frame.loader.retrySignIn.description: Button on the preview's loading screen after signing in to the preview failed: tries signing in again.

frame.loader.signingIn.description: Title of the preview's loading screen while the viewer is being signed in to the previewed app.

frame.loader.signInFailed.text: Could not sign in to the preview
frame.loader.signInFailed.description: Title of the preview's loading screen when signing the viewer in to the previewed app failed.

frame.loader.signInFailedSub.text: Check your connection, then try again.
frame.loader.signInFailedSub.description: Text under "Could not sign in to the preview" on the preview's loading screen.

frame.loader.loading.description: Title of the preview's loading screen while the previewed app's page is loading.

frame.loader.checksRunning.text: Automated checks are running against this preview, so the first load may be a little slower.
frame.loader.checksRunning.description: Text under the title of the preview's loading screen while Homeroom's automated checks are still using the same preview.

frame.loader.waiting.text: Waiting for the preview to respond…
frame.loader.waiting.description: Title of the preview's loading screen while Homeroom waits for the preview's server to answer.

frame.loader.waitingLonger_one.text: Taking a little longer than usual ({{count}}s).
frame.loader.waitingLonger_one.description: Text under "Waiting for the preview to respond…" after about twenty seconds. {{count}} is the seconds waited so far; "s" abbreviates seconds.

frame.loader.waitingLonger_other.text: Taking a little longer than usual ({{count}}s).
frame.loader.waitingLonger_other.description: Text under "Waiting for the preview to respond…" after about twenty seconds. {{count}} is the seconds waited so far; "s" abbreviates seconds.

frame.loader.stillWaiting.description: Title of the preview's loading screen after a minute without an answer from the preview's server.

frame.loader.stillWaitingSub_one.text: The preview hasn’t responded yet ({{count}}s). Hang tight, this keeps retrying automatically.
frame.loader.stillWaitingSub_one.description: Text under "Still waiting on the preview". {{count}} is the seconds waited so far; "s" abbreviates seconds.

frame.loader.stillWaitingSub_other.text: The preview hasn’t responded yet ({{count}}s). Hang tight, this keeps retrying automatically.
frame.loader.stillWaitingSub_other.description: Text under "Still waiting on the preview". {{count}} is the seconds waited so far; "s" abbreviates seconds.

frame.unavailable.title.description: Title of the preview's loading screen when the preview cannot be opened; the reason is shown under it.

frame.unavailable.notRebuilt.text: This preview could not be rebuilt.
frame.unavailable.notRebuilt.description: Reason under "Preview unavailable" when the server refused to rebuild the preview and gave no reason of its own.

frame.unavailable.network.text: Network error while rebuilding the preview. Try again in a moment.
frame.unavailable.network.description: Reason under "Preview unavailable" when the request to open or rebuild the preview could not reach the server.

frame.unavailable.demo.text: Live previews can’t be rebuilt in this demo environment.
frame.unavailable.demo.description: Reason under "Preview unavailable" on a demonstration copy of Homeroom, where previews are not built.

frame.unavailable.unhealthy.text: The submitted preview is running but is not answering its health check. Try again in a moment.
frame.unavailable.unhealthy.description: Reason under "Preview unavailable" when the preview's server is up but does not answer the platform's test request.

frame.unavailable.edge.text: The submitted preview is not reachable through its public address. Try again in a moment.
frame.unavailable.edge.description: Reason under "Preview unavailable" when the preview is running but cannot be reached at its web address.

frame.unavailable.missingReader.text: This preview is no longer running. A collaborator can rebuild it.
frame.unavailable.missingReader.description: Reason under "Preview unavailable" for a viewer who may only read: the preview was shut down and only someone allowed to build can start it again.

frame.unavailable.notNow.text: This preview isn’t available right now.
frame.unavailable.notNow.description: Reason under "Preview unavailable" when the preview is not running and nothing more specific is known.

frame.unavailable.unexpected.text: This preview returned an unexpected response.
frame.unavailable.unexpected.description: Reason under "Preview unavailable" when the server's answer about the preview could not be understood.

frame.unavailable.rebuildFailedTitle.description: Title of the preview's loading screen when rebuilding the preview failed.

frame.unavailable.rebuildFailed.text: The preview failed to build. See the agent session for details.
frame.unavailable.rebuildFailed.description: Text under "Preview couldn’t be rebuilt" when the server gave no reason. The agent session is the chat with the coding agent that made the change.

frame.unavailable.noAddress.text: This preview did not provide a usable address.
frame.unavailable.noAddress.description: Reason under "Preview unavailable" when a rebuild finished without a web address for the preview.

frame.title.named.description: Title in the bar above a staging preview. {{app}} is the app's name; "Preview" says this is its preview, not the live app. A noun.

frame.title.plain.description: Title in the bar above a staging preview when the app's name is not known. A noun.

frame.fullscreen.enter.description: Button in the bar above a preview docked beside the build chat: expands the preview to fill the screen.

frame.fullscreen.exit.description: Button in the bar above a full-screen preview that was opened from the build chat: puts it back beside the chat.

frame.fullscreen.enterTitle.text: Expand the preview to fill the screen
frame.fullscreen.enterTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Full screen" button in the bar above a docked preview.

frame.fullscreen.exitTitle.text: Dock the preview back beside the chat
frame.fullscreen.exitTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Exit full screen" button in the bar above a preview: puts the preview back in its panel beside the build chat.

frame.testing.useButton.text: Use the button above to jump to the changed feature.
frame.testing.useButton.description: Text in the "How to test" panel of a preview when the change has a link to the changed screen but no written testing instructions. The button is the preview bar's test button.

frame.testing.openAtFeature.text: Open the preview at the changed feature
frame.testing.openAtFeature.description: Tooltip of the test button in the bar above a preview when the change has a link to the screen it changes: pressing it goes to that screen. "Open" is a verb.

frame.testing.showInstructions.description: Tooltip of the test button in the bar above a preview when the change has written instructions for trying it out.

bridge.appNotIdentified.text: This app could not be identified. Reopen it and try again.
bridge.appNotIdentified.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when the app asked for AI access or a device permission and Homeroom could not tell which app was asking.

bridge.llmSignedOut.text: Sign in to Homeroom to give an app access to AI.
bridge.llmSignedOut.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when the app asked for AI access and the person is not signed in. Homeroom is the product's name.

bridge.llmLoadFailed.text: Failed to load AI permission state.
bridge.llmLoadFailed.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when Homeroom could not read whether the person has allowed this app to use AI.

bridge.saveFailed.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when the person allowed a permission and the server refused to save it without giving a reason.

bridge.saveNetwork.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when the person allowed a permission and the request to save it could not reach the server.

bridge.permissionSignedOut.text: Sign in to Homeroom to give an app access to this.
bridge.permissionSignedOut.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when the app asked for a device permission (camera, location and so on) and the person is not signed in. "This" is whatever the app asked for; Homeroom is the product's name.

bridge.permissionLoadFailed.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when Homeroom could not read which permissions the person has given this app.

bridge.uploadFailed.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when saving a file to the app's storage failed and the server gave no reason. {{status}} is the HTTP status code, a number.

bridge.fileNotFound.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when the app asked for a stored file that does not exist.

bridge.deleteFailed.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when deleting a file from the app's storage failed and the server gave no reason. {{status}} is the HTTP status code, a number.

bridge.usageFailed.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when reading how much storage the app uses failed and the server gave no reason. {{status}} is the HTTP status code, a number.

bridge.network.text: Network error talking to the platform.
bridge.network.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when a request for the app's stored files or for the member directory could not reach Homeroom's server. "The platform" is Homeroom.

bridge.directoryLookupFailed.description: Error handed back to an embedded app, which may show it to its user, when looking up a member in Homeroom's directory failed and the server gave no reason. {{status}} is the HTTP status code, a number.

dialog.permission.title.description: Title of the dialog Homeroom shows when an app asks for a device permission. {{app}} is the app's name and {{action}} what it wants to do, in the platform's own words, for example "use your camera".

dialog.permission.titleUnnamed.description: Title of the dialog Homeroom shows when an app asks for a device permission. {{action}} is what the app wants to do, in the platform's own words, for example "use your camera". Used when the app's name is not known; "This app" is written as the dialog has always shown it.

dialog.permission.titleCapability.description: Title of the dialog Homeroom shows when an app asks for a device permission that has no description. {{app}} is the app's name and {{capability}} the permission's technical name, for example "geolocation".

dialog.permission.titleCapabilityUnnamed.description: Title of the dialog Homeroom shows when an app asks for a device permission that has no description. {{capability}} is the permission's technical name, for example "geolocation". Used when the app's name is not known; "This app" is written as the dialog has always shown it.

dialog.permission.notePreview.text: This preview cannot turn the permission on, but your answer is saved for the app itself.
dialog.permission.notePreview.description: Note in the permission dialog when it was opened from a preview of an app rather than the app itself: the answer is remembered but has no effect in the preview.

dialog.permission.note.text: Only {{app}} gets this, and you can take it back anytime in Settings.
dialog.permission.note.description: Note in the permission dialog. {{app}} is the app's name; "this" is the permission being asked for.

dialog.permission.noteUnnamed.text: Only This app gets this, and you can take it back anytime in Settings.
dialog.permission.noteUnnamed.description: Note in the permission dialog. "this" is the permission being asked for. Used when the app's name is not known; "This app" is written as the dialog has always shown it.

dialog.permission.noteReopen.text: Only {{app}} gets this, and you can take it back anytime in Settings. The app will reopen so the change takes effect.
dialog.permission.noteReopen.description: Note in the permission dialog when the app has to be loaded again for the permission to work. {{app}} is the app's name; "this" is the permission being asked for.

dialog.permission.noteReopenUnnamed.text: Only This app gets this, and you can take it back anytime in Settings. The app will reopen so the change takes effect.
dialog.permission.noteReopenUnnamed.description: Note in the permission dialog when the app has to be loaded again for the permission to work. "this" is the permission being asked for. Used when the app's name is not known; "This app" is written as the dialog has always shown it.

dialog.permission.allow.description: Confirm button of the permission dialog: gives the app the permission it asked for.

dialog.permission.allowReopen.description: Confirm button of the permission dialog when the app must be loaded again for the permission to work: gives the permission and reloads the app.

dialog.llm.fallbackApp.description: Stands where the app's name is shown on its own in the dialog that asks whether an app may use AI on the person's account, when the name is not known. Shown alone, as a label; the dialog's sentences have unnamed wordings of their own.

dialog.llm.introOwnKey.text: This lets {{app}} use your own Anthropic API key, without exposing the key to the app.
dialog.llm.introOwnKey.description: Opening line of the dialog that asks whether an app may use AI, when it would be paid for with the person's own Anthropic API key. {{app}} is the app's name; Anthropic is a company's name.

dialog.llm.introOwnKeyUnnamed.text: This lets This app use your own Anthropic API key, without exposing the key to the app.
dialog.llm.introOwnKeyUnnamed.description: Opening line of the dialog that asks whether an app may use AI, when it would be paid for with the person's own Anthropic API key. Anthropic is a company's name. Used when the app's name is not known; "This app" is written as the dialog has always shown it.

dialog.llm.introBudget.text: This lets {{app}} spend from your weekly AI budget (the same one your agent sessions use) up to the daily cap below.
dialog.llm.introBudget.description: Opening line of the dialog that asks whether an app may use AI on the person's daily Homeroom AI budget. {{app}} is the app's name; the cap is the spending limit set in the field below.

dialog.llm.introBudgetUnnamed.text: This lets This app spend from your weekly AI budget (the same one your agent sessions use) up to the daily cap below.
dialog.llm.introBudgetUnnamed.description: Opening line of the dialog that asks whether an app may use AI on the person's daily Homeroom AI budget. The cap is the spending limit set in the field below. Used when the app's name is not known; "This app" is written as the dialog has always shown it.

dialog.llm.capSuggested.text: Suggested by this app. You can change it.
dialog.llm.capSuggested.description: Note under the daily cap field in the AI access dialog when the amount shown was proposed by the app.

dialog.llm.capChangeLater.text: You can change this anytime in Settings.
dialog.llm.capChangeLater.description: Note under the daily cap field in the AI access dialog. "This" is the daily spending cap.

dialog.llm.ownKeyRequired.text: Use my own API key for this app (required until platform credits are unlocked; still limited by the cap above).
dialog.llm.ownKeyRequired.description: Checkbox label in the AI access dialog when the person has no platform AI credits, so the app can only run on their own API key.

dialog.llm.ownKeyFallback.text: If my weekly platform budget runs out, let this app keep going on my own API key (still limited by the cap above).
dialog.llm.ownKeyFallback.description: Checkbox label in the AI access dialog: lets the app continue on the person's own API key once their daily Homeroom budget is spent.

dialog.llm.capInvalid.text: Enter a valid daily cap (at least $0.01).
dialog.llm.capInvalid.description: Error in the AI access dialog when the daily cap field is empty, not a number, or below one cent. The amount is in US dollars.

dialog.llm.capTooHigh.text: The cap can't exceed your own daily limit ({{limit}}).
dialog.llm.capTooHigh.description: Error in the AI access dialog when the daily cap entered is higher than the person's own daily AI limit. {{limit}} is that limit as a dollar amount, for example "$25.00".

dialog.llm.ownKeyMustBeOn.text: Your own API key must be enabled while platform credits are locked.
dialog.llm.ownKeyMustBeOn.description: Error in the AI access dialog when the person unticked the own-API-key checkbox although they have no platform credits to use instead.

age.justNow.description: Compact age of a card or row on a project's page: less than a minute ago.

age.minutes_one.description: Compact age of a card or row on a project's page. {{count}} is the number of minutes; "m" abbreviates minutes.

age.minutes_other.description: Compact age of a card or row on a project's page. {{count}} is the number of minutes; "m" abbreviates minutes.

age.hours_one.description: Compact age of a card or row on a project's page. {{count}} is the number of hours; "h" abbreviates hours.

age.hours_other.description: Compact age of a card or row on a project's page. {{count}} is the number of hours; "h" abbreviates hours.

age.days_one.description: Compact age of a card or row on a project's page. {{count}} is the number of days; "d" abbreviates days.

age.days_other.description: Compact age of a card or row on a project's page. {{count}} is the number of days; "d" abbreviates days.

page.menu.editRequests.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a change's page, for its owner, when the change is already linked to requests (filed issues): opens the editor that changes which requests it is linked to. "Edit" is a verb.

page.menu.addRequest.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a change's page, for its owner, when no request is linked yet: opens the editor that links the change to an existing request (filed issue). It does not file a new request.

page.menu.requestsTitle.text: Change which requests this change addresses
page.menu.requestsTitle.description: Tooltip on the Edit requests and Add a request rows in the ⋯ menu of a change's page. The first "Change" is a verb, "this change" is the proposal, and a request is a filed issue it would resolve.

page.menu.shotDetails.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a change's page when its before and after screenshots were taken: opens the technical details of those screenshots.

page.menu.shotDetailsTitle.text: How each change was reached, at which screen sizes, and on which builds
page.menu.shotDetailsTitle.description: Tooltip on the Screenshot details row in the ⋯ menu of a change's page, listing what the details hold: the steps taken to reach each visible change, the screen sizes photographed, and the two builds of the app compared.

page.menu.takeShotsAgain.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a change's page, for its author or an admin: starts taking the before and after screenshots over again.

page.menu.takeShotsAgainTitle.text: Take the before & after screenshots again on this exact build
page.menu.takeShotsAgainTitle.description: Tooltip on the Take the screenshots again row in the ⋯ menu of a change's page. "Build" is a noun: the built copy of the app the screenshots are taken of.

page.menu.viewPr.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a change's page, for a change whose pull request is on GitHub: opens it on GitHub in a new tab. "PR" is short for pull request.

page.menu.viewCode.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a change's page, for a change whose code is on Homeroom's own git host rather than GitHub: opens that code in a new tab. "View" is a verb.

shots.details.builds.text: Taken on the exact before and after builds of this change:
shots.details.builds.description: Lead-in at the bottom of the Screenshot details sheet of a change's page. It ends with a colon and is followed by the short ids of the two code revisions the screenshots were taken of and of the screenshots themselves. "Builds" is a noun: built copies of the app; "change" is the proposal.

shots.thread.title.description: Title of the card on a change's page that holds its before and after screenshots, and the accessible name of that card's contents.

shots.pane.close.description: The × at the right of the head above a change's before and after screenshots, shown beside a thread on the Homeroom bot tab, in the Workshop's request panel or on a request's page: closes those screenshots and returns the column to the thread. Its accessible name and tooltip.

shots.pane.back.description: On a phone, the arrow at the top left of a change's before and after screenshots, which cover the screen: goes back to the thread the change is in. Its accessible name and tooltip.

request.page.askerUnknown.description: Stands in for the name of the person who filed a request, at the top of the request's page, when that person is not known. Lower case, as a username would sit there.

request.status.lead.live.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. The change that fulfils the request was approved by the group's vote and is now part of the running app ("live").

request.status.lead.nobody.text: Nobody is working on this yet.
request.status.lead.nobody.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. "This" is the request.

request.status.lead.botQuestion.text: Waiting for an answer to Homeroom bot's question.
request.status.lead.botQuestion.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant, which builds changes; it asked a question on the request and waits for someone to answer it.

request.status.lead.botPlanWaiting.text: @{{username}}'s plan is ready. Any member can build it below.
request.status.lead.botPlanWaiting.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands, for anyone but the person who asked for it. Homeroom bot wrote a plan for the change, drawn right below this card, and any member of the community may press its Build it button. {{username}} is the person who asked for it, after an @.

request.status.lead.botPlanYours.text: Your plan is ready. Build it is on the plan below.
request.status.lead.botPlanYours.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands, read by the person who asked for it while Homeroom bot's plan for it waits for Build it. The plan, with its Build it button, is drawn right below this card. "Build it" is the name of that button: keep it as the button reads.

request.status.lead.botPlanWaitingUnname.text: The plan is ready. Any member can build it below.
request.status.lead.botPlanWaitingUnname.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands, when the person who asked for it cannot be named. Homeroom bot wrote a plan for the change, drawn right below this card, and any member of the community may press its Build it button.

request.status.lead.botHeld.text: Homeroom bot will start when one of its changes here is voted in or closed.
request.status.lead.botHeld.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant, which builds changes; it already has as many changes waiting for a vote on this project as it may, so it starts on this request when one of them is approved or closed. "Here" is the project.

request.status.lead.botHeldTurn.text: Homeroom bot will start when one of the changes it is building here is done.
request.status.lead.botHeldTurn.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant, which builds changes; it is already building as many changes on this project at once as it may, so it starts on this request when one of those builds is done. "Here" is the project.

request.status.lead.upForVote.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. The change that fulfils the request is built and waits for the group's vote; used when how many more yes votes it needs is not known.

request.status.lead.upForVoteNeeds_one.text: Up for a vote: needs 1 more yes.
request.status.lead.upForVoteNeeds_one.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. The change that fulfils the request is built and waits for the group's vote; it needs one more yes vote. English spells the one out; a translation may use {{count}}.

request.status.lead.upForVoteNeeds_other.text: Up for a vote: needs {{count}} more yes.
request.status.lead.upForVoteNeeds_other.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. The change that fulfils the request is built and waits for the group's vote; it needs {{count}} more yes votes. "Yes" is the vote, as a noun.

request.status.lead.upForVoteChecksFaili.text: Up for a vote, but a test is failing. It needs a fix before it can go live.
request.status.lead.upForVoteChecksFaili.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. The change that fulfils the request is up for the group's vote, but one of its tests failed, so it cannot go live until its author fixes it; the card counts no yes votes while that is so.

request.status.lead.reviewYours.text: Your change for this is waiting for approval.
request.status.lead.reviewYours.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. The viewer's own change (a proposal that fulfils the request) is up for the group's vote. "Change" is a noun.

request.status.lead.reviewNamed.text: {{username}}’s change for this is waiting for approval.
request.status.lead.reviewNamed.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. {{username}} is the person whose change (a proposal that fulfils the request) is up for the group's vote. "Change" is a noun.

request.status.lead.review.text: A change for this is waiting for approval.
request.status.lead.review.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. Somebody's change (a proposal that fulfils the request) is up for the group's vote, and its author is not named. "Change" is a noun.

request.status.lead.botQueued.text: Homeroom bot will build this next.
request.status.lead.botQueued.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant, which builds changes; the request is next in its queue. "Build" is a verb.

request.status.lead.botOnHoldUntil.text: Homeroom bot has this on hold until {{date}}.
request.status.lead.botOnHoldUntil.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant, which builds changes; it has the request in its queue but holds it until {{date}}, a short month and day, and nothing needs to be done meanwhile.

request.status.lead.botWaitsPlan.text: Homeroom bot is waiting for your plan.
request.status.lead.botWaitsPlan.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page while the viewer, who asked for it, works on it with Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) in a private thread: the bot builds nothing until they post a plan on it or let it go ahead.

request.status.lead.waitingDecide.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands: Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) read the request and handed it back for a person to decide. {{reason}} is the bot's own sentence on why, which ends with a full stop.

request.status.lead.waitingDecidePlain.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands: Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) read the request and handed it back for a person to decide, without having given a reason.

request.status.lead.waitingDetail.text: Waiting for more detail from you. {{reason}}
request.status.lead.waitingDetail.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands: Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) read the request and needs more detail before it can build anything. {{reason}} is the bot's own sentence on what is missing, which ends with a full stop.

request.status.lead.waitingDetailPlain.text: Waiting for more detail from you.
request.status.lead.waitingDetailPlain.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands: Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) read the request and needs more detail before it can build anything, without having given a reason.

request.status.lead.waitingDone.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands: Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) read the request and thinks what it asks for may already work, so somebody should check before building. {{reason}} is the bot's own sentence on why, which ends with a full stop.

request.status.lead.waitingDonePlain.text: It may already work. Close it, or say what is missing.
request.status.lead.waitingDonePlain.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands: Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) read the request and thinks what it asks for may already work. Somebody can close the request, or say what is still missing from it.

request.status.lead.botReading.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant; it has started on the request and is reading it before building.

request.status.lead.botBuilding.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant; it is writing the change that fulfils the request.

request.status.lead.autoSolving.text: An auto-solve run is working on this.
request.status.lead.autoSolving.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. An auto-solve run is an automatic AI session started on the request.

request.status.lead.answerNeeded.text: An auto-solve run asked a question that needs an answer.
request.status.lead.answerNeeded.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. An auto-solve run is an automatic AI session started on the request; it stopped to ask something.

request.status.lead.draftReady.text: An auto-solve run left a draft to look over.
request.status.lead.draftReady.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. An auto-solve run is an automatic AI session started on the request; it finished and left a draft change for a person to review.

request.status.lead.startedYou.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. A working session on the request was started and nobody is in it right now. The viewer started it.

request.status.lead.startedYouOthers_one.text: You and {{count}} other started working on this.
request.status.lead.startedYouOthers_one.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. A working session on the request was started and nobody is in it right now. The viewer and {{count}} more people started work.

request.status.lead.startedYouOthers_oth.text: You and {{count}} others started working on this.
request.status.lead.startedYouOthers_oth.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. A working session on the request was started and nobody is in it right now. The viewer and {{count}} more people started work.

request.status.lead.startedNamed.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. A working session on the request was started and nobody is in it right now. {{username}} is the person who started it.

request.status.lead.startedNamedOthers_o.text: {{username}} and {{count}} other started working on this.
request.status.lead.startedNamedOthers_o.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. A working session on the request was started and nobody is in it right now. {{username}} is one of the people who started work and {{count}} is how many more there are.

request.status.lead.startedNamedOthers_o.text: {{username}} and {{count}} others started working on this.
request.status.lead.startedNamedOthers_o.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. A working session on the request was started and nobody is in it right now. {{username}} is one of the people who started work and {{count}} is how many more there are.

request.status.lead.startedSomeone.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. A working session on the request was started and nobody is in it right now. The person is not named.

request.status.lead.startedSomeoneOthers.text: Someone and {{count}} other started working on this.
request.status.lead.startedSomeoneOthers.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. A working session on the request was started and nobody is in it right now. Nobody is named; {{count}} is how many people there are besides the first.

request.status.lead.startedSomeoneOthers.text: Someone and {{count}} others started working on this.
request.status.lead.startedSomeoneOthers.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. A working session on the request was started and nobody is in it right now. Nobody is named; {{count}} is how many people there are besides the first.

request.status.lead.workingYou.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. Somebody is working on the request now, or said they would. It is the viewer.

request.status.lead.workingYouOthers_one.text: You and {{count}} other are working on this.
request.status.lead.workingYouOthers_one.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. Somebody is working on the request now, or said they would. It is the viewer and {{count}} more people.

request.status.lead.workingYouOthers_oth.text: You and {{count}} others are working on this.
request.status.lead.workingYouOthers_oth.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. Somebody is working on the request now, or said they would. It is the viewer and {{count}} more people.

request.status.lead.workingNamed.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. Somebody is working on the request now, or said they would. {{username}} is that person.

request.status.lead.workingNamedOthers_o.text: {{username}} and {{count}} other are working on this.
request.status.lead.workingNamedOthers_o.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. Somebody is working on the request now, or said they would. {{username}} is one of them and {{count}} is how many more there are.

request.status.lead.workingNamedOthers_o.text: {{username}} and {{count}} others are working on this.
request.status.lead.workingNamedOthers_o.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. Somebody is working on the request now, or said they would. {{username}} is one of them and {{count}} is how many more there are.

request.status.lead.workingSomeone.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. Somebody is working on the request now, or said they would. The person is not named.

request.status.lead.workingSomeoneOthers.text: Someone and {{count}} other are working on this.
request.status.lead.workingSomeoneOthers.description: The one sentence on the status card of a request's page that says where the request stands. Somebody is working on the request now, or said they would. Nobody is named; {{count}} is how many people there are besides the first.
